## 1. Summary and decisions needed

### 1.1 What changes

Today NIMBUS holds an order's start and works out its finish: finish equals start plus run time, in plain elapsed hours, in every place that places or reads an order. The owner wants NIMBUS to schedule backward, the way SAP's backward scheduling does (which SAP engine applies is unconfirmed, Appendix D). Under the new rule each order stores a placed finish (the finish the planner or the optimizer chose), and the start is derived backward from that finish through working hours, blackouts and setup. A routing or run-time change then makes a bar grow to the left, and the finish that NIMBUS sent to SAP does not move while the order stays firmed in SAP (4.13.1). The finish SAP sent in the first place is kept as the due date and is never rewritten. If the backward walk would start before now, the order is placed forward from now instead and shows as late; this switch to a forward placement is called a "reversal" in the rest of this document. All plants switch at once, and the old forward paths are replaced, not kept behind a switch (decisions O1 to O4, section 3), apart from the exceptions listed at the end of this section.

Five facts shape everything else:

1. **The existing code already overwrites the due date.** The first time SAP echoes back a finish that NIMBUS sent, ingest stores the planner's finish as the due date in four places. No column keeps the original afterwards (4.5.3). (The echo behaviour is assumed from the staging design and a simulator test; the real-SAP check is blocker 18.)
2. **There is no server-side calendar.** The database can subtract elapsed hours but cannot walk working hours, so the derived start has to be computed by the browser and stored. Every server reader of "the start" then depends on that stored value (4.1.5).
3. **A held finish cannot always be honoured.** Under the split policies `never` and `overlong_only`, an order may have no contiguous slot that ends at the held finish, and any code that re-derives the finish forward from a stored start moves it (4.2.3). `never` is the schema default, and under it an order longer than every working window is one continuous elapsed bar for which no backward rule exists yet (OQ50).
4. **Running and frozen status can flip by data.** A derived start moves whenever the run time changes, and it would move with the calendar or with "now" if anything re-derived it; who re-derives a stored start after a calendar edit is undecided (OQ51), because ordinary calendar edits are alert-only today. So an order can leave or enter the running state or the frozen window with no planner action. The running-order protection fails in the unsafe direction under an elapsed start or end (4.5.7, 4.11).
5. **A bar that grows to the left can overlap the bar before it, and nothing repairs the overlap.** When a run-time increase pushes a derived start back into its predecessor's slot, the system only raises an alert; it does not move either bar. This is not yet an owner question (Follow-ups 17 and 18; 4.3, 4.9); the ordering rule for reversals on one line is OQ53.

The work touches the database read and save path, the calendar engine, 25 places reviewed that write, restore or clear dates on an order (22 set dates, one clears them, one writes none and one acts only through another; 4.3), ingest and the SAP round trip, distribution, the optimizer, alerts and KPIs, and the UI and its five locales. Only about 4 percent of existing tests assert the forward relation (classified from test titles, so approximate), so the suites will mostly stay green while behaviour changes; the 33 groups of new tests in 10.5 are the real gate (10.1). Every worked-example number in this document was traced by hand; none was executed (stated again in the introduction to section 12).

**Exceptions to the headline rules.** The sentences above state the rules in their plain form: the finish holds, the finish sent to SAP does not move while the order stays firmed in SAP (4.13.1), the due date is never rewritten, the old forward paths are replaced. The document's own recommendations depart from the plain form in the ten places below. Each is a proposal in section 12, not a decision; the owner accepts or rejects each one there.

1. **Running orders stay start-anchored (OQ3(iii)).** A run-time change on an order that is running moves its finish and holds its start. Example: started Wed 06:00, finish Wed 14:00, run time 8 to 12 h: the finish becomes Wed 18:00.
2. **Never-placed rows keep a start-plus-run-time read (OQ33(B)).** An order nobody has placed shows today's bar (SAP start plus run time) and is not sent until it has a placed finish; the due date is not its fallback. 6.2 states this rule once.
3. **Retained forward paths.** The optimizer and its Apply (Reading A, OQ14(a)), the alert "Fix" with its cascade and Remove Backlog (both listed in 4.3) place forward, from a cursor or from now. `Engine.schedulePatchFor` (through `Engine.heldStartPatchFor`) is also retained, for the OQ3 running-order start hold. "Replaced" means their output is stored as the placed finish, not that they become backward walks.
4. **The held finish can still move.** When no contiguous slot ends at it (OQ13), when reversal flips the walk forward (O2), when the minimum-piece rule pulls a landing (OQ55), and for the degenerate inputs of 4.2.5 (a finish in closed time, run time zero, a shutdown of many days). Who re-derives a stored start after a calendar edit is OQ51.
5. **The optimizer's ranking is not wholly unchanged.** OQ20 moves its instability and "moved" keys from the start to the finish (2.3 says the ranking objectives do not change).
6. **The outbound firm flag follows derived starts.** A run-time change can move an unfirmed order's derived start into the frozen window and add the SAP firm flag, which SAP never clears (4.11; OQ54). "The planner's firm flag keeps its role" holds for the planner flag only.
7. **OQ33 changes which orders Send.** Under the recommended B a row with no placed finish is not an outbound candidate. Today every row with a computed end is sent.
8. **A manual setup override can be left pointing at the wrong pair.** A run-time growth that moves a derived start before its predecessor swaps predecessor and successor. That leaves a manual setup override pointing at a pair that no longer sits together (4.9). "Override rows: unchanged" holds only where adjacency does not change.
9. **A reversal under the due date is silent today; OQ53 proposes a notice.** Reversal moves the finish later than held. The "late" warning (OQ6(a)) fires only past the due date. So a finish SAP was given can change at the next Send without any signal. OQ53 recommends a notice on every system move of a finish, which would end the silence.
10. **A reversal-placed order and a later run-time change.** Under the recommended OQ18(a), a reversal-placed order counts as running from the moment it is placed, because its start is at or before now. So OQ3(iii) governs it: its start holds and its finish moves. OQ7 ("a manual run-time edit holds the finish") governs only orders that are not running. When several orders reverse on one line, the recommended ordering (OQ53(b)) places the first at now and the later ones after it. Only the first one meets the running test at the moment of placement. If the owner takes OQ18(c) instead (a stored reversal flag), OQ7 governs until the order has truly started. Consequence under the recommendations: after a later run-time change, the sentence "the finish that NIMBUS sent to SAP does not move" is false for a reversal-placed order that counts as running.

### 1.4 Decisions the owner must make

**Update 2026-10-14: every question below has been answered; see 1.6 for the decisions, which override the recommendations in this table.** The full list is section 12 (62 questions: OQ1 to OQ12 from the brief, OQ13 to OQ49 raised by the investigation and OQ50 to OQ62 raised by the second review of 2026-10-13, Appendix E). The last column names the questions a decision depends on. Each line below is the recommendation only; the reason, the options with one concrete example each, and the evidence are in section 12. Items marked **gate** are the decisions without which a phase's central work cannot start; section 7.1 lists every decision each phase also depends on, including the unmarked ones.

| OQ | Question | One-line recommendation | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|

### 1.5 What the owner does before any code (Phase 0 checklist)

Phase 0 writes no code. This is the one list of owner actions; 7.2 points here and keeps only its gate statement. Phase 1 is the only change that can ship to production before the cutover, because it moves no bar for orders that have a run time or a stored end (7.3), once a release mechanism exists (7.1.1). It delivers: protection of the due date at every place that writes it (including the fix for a finish at exactly midnight in SAP's time zone), retiring the browser's rewrite of the due date together with the date-only lateness read rule, stopping the import's fabrication of finishes, and a one-time repair of legacy due dates limited to orders never sent to SAP (7.3). It must be live before the first Send to SAP reaches production, and the as-sent baselines must be snapshotted first (item 5; 7.3; 8.13 step 2).

1. **Decide the Phase 1 gate questions.** Only these block Phase 1: OQ23 (time of day of a date-only finish), OQ24 (rows with no usable finish), OQ28 (run time at or over 168 hours; decide it in Phase 0), OQ29 (distribution baseline writes), OQ30 (repairing legacy due dates, never-sent orders only), OQ31 (guard or immutable column for the due date) and OQ45 (hygiene counts and the purge preview). OQ10 (ship the cutover with or after SAP staging) and OQ61 (should Send transmit unfirmed orders) must be decided before the first live Send. The Phase 2 gate questions (OQ1 to OQ5, OQ7, OQ13, OQ15, OQ32 to OQ34, OQ50 to OQ54, OQ59, and the others marked gate for Phase 2 in 7.1) are decided during Phase 1 and block Phase 2 only; Phase 4 gates (OQ35, OQ36, OQ62) are decided before the cutover.
2. **Choose the release mechanism (7.1.1).** A release branch for each releasable step, or keeping Phase 2 and 3 work on a feature branch until the cutover. This is an owner decision with no OQ number, and it is a precondition of Phase 1: today every deploy ships everything merged to `main`.
3. **Identify the live image.** Read the image tag with `az containerapp show` and the `NIMBUS_BUILD_ID` in the served page, map both to a commit, and list what is inside (7.1.1). It settles whether the SAP staging apply, Send to SAP and the Machine Hours rule are already live.
4. **Confirm whether any Send to SAP has already happened on the pilot** (the 2026-10-13 roll is unverified, 8.9). If one has, the as-sent due dates of those orders are already overwritten.
5. **Take a baseline snapshot before any Send** and before any repair: the due-date column, the as-sent start and finish, and the record of what was sent, in a snapshot file that contains none of the deploy runner's blocked words (8.13 step 2).
6. **Take the pilot-database dump and rehearse on a restored copy** (8.13 step 0a, part 1), together with the pilot-database rehearsal the SAP staging work still owes. Named owner: `<name: takes the pg_dump of pgdb-nimbus-dev/nimbus and records how>`. The owner reviews the rehearsal numbers (gate G-10, part 1). No repository document gives a dump procedure.
7. **Run the real-SAP echo test (blocker 18).** In a SAP test client, send one unfirmed order, one firmed order and one order whose finish puts SAP's own start in the past; export them from SAP and compare every field with what NIMBUS sent (4.13.8, Appendix D). Put the other Appendix D questions to SAP Development at the same time (blank and zero times, calendar-boundary shifting, the real SAP zone, the date that selects a production version, whether SAP reschedules the start when Machine Hours change, whether weekly renumbering of unfirmed orders is as described). Answers are given in writing, or accepted by the owner in writing as assumptions, before the first production Send and in any case before Phase 4. SAP contact: `<name: SAP Development contact who answers Appendix D>`.
8. **Run the profile queries Q0 to Q17 (8.12) and probes P1 to P5 (P1 in 4.13.8, P2 in 4.13.4, P3 in 4.13.5, P4 in 4.13.7, P5 in 4.6.3).** Where they run: all of them on the restored copy from item 6, so the live database carries no load; then Q4 and Q12 again on the live database in a read-only transaction, because they depend on the current time and describe only the moment of the dump. Each block runs in its own read-only transaction. Review in particular: Q13 (lines with no calendar row) and Q15 (plants with no time zone), both stops for gate G-2 until a rule is chosen (OQ62, OQ52); Q16 (overlong orders per line, OQ50); Q17 (orders carrying the mismatch flag, OQ53); Q1 (orders with no run time and no stored end, 7.3); Q8 (repairable legacy due dates); Q10 (distribution families); Q11 (what a first Send would do).
9. **Do the five-minute browser check** of the timeline library's behaviour (which edge a drag moves, whether resize handles show, what the move event's time is; OQ1, 4.3, 4.12).
10. **Get the platform operator's facts:** point-in-time restore enabled and its retention (8.8); and for the Send check of 7.1.2, whether the Mulesoft database role exists, the firewall addresses, the poll interval, and the server clock and zone. Platform operator: `<name: backup, restore, firewall>`.
11. **Get the caller list for the bulk-update route (OQ59):** who else writes order dates (scripts, integrations, admin tools). It is requested now and needed before the cutover.
12. **Confirm the Functional Specification finish gate (Follow-up 13).** The re-saved FSD says the planned-order export is limited relative to the planned-order finish, in a sentence that is cut off. The owner confirms whether that is the intended rule; it decides whether NIMBUS's start-keyed vanish test must change.
13. **Name the roles** before Phase 4 (8.13): decider (go, no-go, abort), deploy operator, platform operator (item 10), dump owner (item 6), SAP contact (item 7), watcher, capturer.
14. **Set the abort thresholds for the first shift after the cutover** (the `N = <owner>` values in the 8.13 step 6 table). Needed before Phase 4, not before Phase 1.
15. **Run the owner check of 7.1.2** against the current state even though no Send is planned: it is the list of what must be true before one is.

### 1.6 Owner decisions of 2026-10-14 (these override the recommendations elsewhere in this document)

On 2026-10-14 the owner answered the open questions, in prompts, in plain language. Where an answer differs from a recommendation in section 12, the answer governs, and the recommendation text is left in place only as the record of what was proposed. Each question in section 12 now ends with an **Owner decision** line that says which. One new question, OQ63, came out of the answers (below). Nothing in the code has changed.

The owner's stance, in their words: this is still a pilot, so "what happens happens"; the tool is detailed schedule planning, not an MES (shop-floor execution system).

**Decisions that differ from the recommendation**

| OQ | Decision | What the recommendation was |
|---|---|---|
| OQ5 | At cutover, re-derive every order from its due date, including running and firmed orders ("absolutely everything"). Confirmed reading: a running order's start stays and its finish follows the run time (OQ3); a firmed order is re-derived, and its new finish goes to SAP at the next Send. | Keep every placed finish as the board shows it today, so no bar moves. |
| OQ28 | The maximum order length rises from 168 hours to 336 hours or the planning horizon, whichever comes first (owner's words: "extend the bar to be the full length"). The cap measures the order's run time (its working hours), not the drawn span: confirmed 2026-10-14, so a 300-hour order on a splitting plant is placed as pieces over several weeks even though its drawn span is longer. An order with more than the cap goes to Needs Planning, and a planner can approve and release it. | Reject the row, naming it. |
| OQ31 | Option (b): new immutable "original start" and "original finish" columns. They hold what SAP sent, until SAP's finish matches the finish NIMBUS sent. From then on they are frozen. A later genuine SAP change updates them. The match is judged on the finish only, because SAP may recompute its own start. | A guard on the existing due-date column at the three write sites. |
| OQ32 | Re-purpose the existing `scheduled_end` column as the placed finish. | A new column. |
| OQ33 | A row nobody has placed is derived backward from its due date at cutover (the bar will jump on release day). | Keep today's bar (start plus run time) and send nothing until it is placed. |
| OQ35 | Re-align distribution families at cutover, like everything else. | Leave them as they are until a planner re-weights. |
| OQ36 | Operational notice only: tell planners to save and close their tabs. No code protection. | Notice, plus refusing the old save route and discarding cached edits. |
| OQ50 | An order longer than the longest working window on a "never split" plant is refused to Needs Planning. When a planner releases it, it is drawn as one continuous bar ending at its held finish and marked as an approved exception. | One continuous bar, with no refusal. |
| OQ54 | Keep today's firm rule as built: an order is sent firm if a planner firmed it, SAP already had it firm, or it starts inside the frozen horizon. No confirm step. | The same rule, plus a confirmation listing orders firmed only by the frozen window. |
| OQ61 | Send transmits only firmed orders: planner-firmed, frozen-horizon-firmed or SAP-firmed. Unfirmed orders are never sent. | Send every order, with the summary split into "will hold" and "will be replaced". |

**Decisions with additions or specifics**

| OQ | Decision |
|---|---|
| OQ1 | Accepted, plus OQ63 (below). |
| OQ3 | Accepted. An order that has not started works backward from its held finish, and reverses forward from now if the backward start would fall before now. An order that has already started keeps its real start and its finish moves later. |
| OQ23 | Accepted. SAP development is adding a time of day to the feed. A finish with no time is read as the end of the working day. |
| OQ53 | Accepted. Orders that reverse together on one line are queued by held finish, and every system move of a finish gets a notice. |
| OQ63 (new) | Firmed orders can be placed outside working hours on purpose (one-off overtime), after a confirm. Such an order needs a per-order marker so that later recalculations and the optimizer leave it alone. |

**Accepted as recommended (no change from section 12):** OQ2, OQ4, OQ7, OQ10, OQ13, OQ15, OQ24, OQ29, OQ30, OQ34, OQ45, OQ51, OQ52, OQ59, OQ62. The owner also accepted every recommendation for the remaining smaller questions in one block: OQ6, OQ8, OQ9, OQ11, OQ12, OQ14, OQ16 to OQ22, OQ25 to OQ27, OQ37 to OQ44, OQ46 to OQ49, OQ55 to OQ58, OQ60. That includes deferring Reading B (section 5). The release mechanism (7.1.1) is option B: Phase 2 and 3 work stays on a feature branch until the cutover.

**What these decisions change in the plan (consequences to carry into section 7 and 8)**

1. **The cutover is a bulk re-derive, not an identity write.** OQ5, OQ33 and OQ35 together mean every bar is recomputed from its due date, in the browser, because the server has no calendar (blocker 2). Every placed bar, every optimizer sequence and every firmed finish can move on release day, and lateness changes everywhere at once. Blocker 6 (the browser reconcile ignores firm, running and frozen status and has no clamp to now) now sits on the critical path: the reconcile must keep a running order's start, and the reversal queue (OQ53) applies whenever many orders reverse together. The identity-sheet idea of 8.1 and 8.2 and the exclusion classes E1 to E9 no longer apply, so the as-sent snapshot and the database dump are the only way back (blockers 14 and 22).
2. **The `scheduled_end` backfill is smaller than in 6.2 and 8.2, but not zero.** OQ32 re-purposes the column, and OQ5 replaces its contents at cutover rather than preserving them. The stored ends are an unmarked mixture (4.1.7), so that is acceptable only because every row is rewritten. A stale-tab save can still write an old pair into a row the cutover did not touch (OQ36 is operational only; blocker 13 stays open).
3. **The 168-hour limit moves.** The owner's cap (336 hours or the planning horizon, whichever comes first) measures run time, confirmed 2026-10-14. The database check that exists today is also on run time (`schema.sql:117-121`, `run_time < 168`), so that check rises to the new cap, and the statement in 4.1.6 that a derived start is at most 168 hours before the finish no longer holds: a continuous bar can now be up to 336 hours, and on a plant that splits orders a bar's drawn span can be longer still, which also affects the conflict-scan lookback (OQ27). It needs a schema change (the deploy runner treats it as destructive; blocker 15). The planning horizon has to be named: which plant setting, and what happens when it is shorter than 336 hours. The Machine Hours unit is still unconfirmed (Appendix D), and the share of sample rows above 336 hours is not yet measured.
4. **One new per-order marker serves two decisions.** OQ63 (overtime on a firmed order) and OQ50 (an overlong order released from Needs Planning) both need a stored flag that says "this bar is placed outside normal derivation on purpose". Decide at implementation whether one column or two. The derivation, the reconcile and the optimizer must all leave a marked order alone.
5. **The Send candidate rule changes.** OQ61 limits Send to firmed orders, so the candidate query (`sap_staging.py:2206-2215`) and the aggregate roll-up change, and blocker 19 (unfirmed orders replaced by SAP's weekly run) shrinks to the orders that are firmed. The OQ33 B1 "sends nothing until placed" rule is no longer needed. OQ54 keeps the add-only firm flag, so an order can still be firmed in SAP just by growing into the frozen window. That is accepted, and it is unconfirmed what SAP does with such a flag (Appendix D).
6. **New original-date columns are an ALTER.** Nothing existing is renamed or repurposed for this: the columns that hold the SAP start and finish today (`basic_start_date`, `basic_finish_date`, wire `original_start_date` and `original_end_date`) stay as they are, and the echo can still overwrite them. The new columns are locked copies that the due-date readers use instead. There are two because two accepted decisions each need one: the original finish (OQ31, the due date as received) and the original start (OQ26, "the SAP start as first received", which the document says needs its own storage). The Original Start column on the grid (OQ16, retired) is a screen field and is unrelated to these. If the owner wants only the finish locked, OQ26 would have to be revisited. This adds an ALTER, so the deploy runner's override switch (blocker 15) applies, and the due-date work (Phase 1) now includes a schema change, not only a guard. The match test needs a defined tolerance, which depends on the real-SAP echo test (blocker 18, assumption A9). Orders that already echoed keep a lost original; OQ30 (repair for never-sent orders only) still applies.
7. **Phase 1 content is now:** the new original columns and their match rule (OQ31), stopping the distribution baseline writes (OQ29), the repair for never-sent orders (OQ30), the midnight echo fix, the end-of-working-day reading of a finish with no time (OQ23), rejection of unusable rows (OQ24), the raised limit and the Needs Planning route for longer rows (OQ28), and the purge preview fix (OQ45). The feature-branch release mechanism makes "Phase 1 alone" real.

## 2. What changes in business terms

### 2.1 Today versus target

| Topic | Today | Target | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Which edge is held | The start. The finish is start plus run time in plain elapsed hours, ignoring working hours, blackouts and setup. | The finish. The start is derived backward through working hours, blackouts and setup. | 3.1, 4.3 |
| What the SAP finish means | A column that is sometimes SAP's value, sometimes a value ingest invented, sometimes the browser's "end of the working day of the start", and after an echo the planner's own finish. | The due date, as received, never rewritten. Lateness is the placed finish against it. | 3.2, 4.5, 4.6 |
| What goes back to SAP | A computed elapsed end (start plus run time). Whether an untouched order's first Send moves SAP's finish earlier or later depends on whether SAP's window is longer or shorter than the order's run time: earlier in the document's worked examples, later for 585 of 593 rows of the COOIS sample (which may be a different order type from the pilot feed; 4.13.7). | The stored placed finish. | 4.5.4, 4.13.7 |
| A run-time change | The start holds and the finish moves, calendar-blind, at read time. Only a flagged order is re-fitted by the browser, forward from its start. | The finish holds and the start moves left. | 4.4 |
| A drag | The start the planner chose is kept; the finish is start plus run time; the dropped right edge is thrown away. | The dropped finish is kept; the start is derived. | 4.3 |
| Optimizer | Packs forward and writes both edges; the finish survives a reload only by coincidence. | Still sequences forward but its result is defined and stored as the placed finish. | 4.8 |
| A start before now | Nothing special; a late bar simply sits in the past. | The walk flips forward from now and the order shows as late. | 4.2.4, 4.11 |
| Distribution children | Start-aligned: every child starts together at SAP's start and ends apart. | Finish-aligned by default: every child ends together at the due date and starts apart. | 4.7 |

### 2.2 Five worked examples

**A drag.** *Today:* a 10 h order on a line open 06:00 to 18:00 shows Friday 04:00 to 14:00 (possible, because manual edits never snap). The planner drags it by 3 days and 5 hours; the bar lands on Monday 09:00 to 19:00. NIMBUS keeps the start (Mon 09:00) and sets the finish to start plus 10 h (Mon 19:00), one hour after closing; only an alert says so. *Under the new rule:* the dropped right edge (19:00) is the held finish, clamped to the last working instant (Mon 18:00), and the 10 h walk back lands on Mon 08:00: the bar jumps one hour left on release. A drop at Mon 05:00 to 15:00 cannot hold 10 h inside Monday's window (06:00 to 15:00 is 9 h). Under policy `never` the calendar walk's own answer is Fri 08:00 to 18:00, the previous working day (three calendar days earlier); that is option (a) of OQ13 applied to a drop. OQ13 recommends instead that a manual drop which cannot hold its finish is not accepted: the bar snaps back to where it was before the drag, with an alert, so the planner sees the bar return rather than leap. A start-held calendar-aware alternative would jump 21 hours right, to Tue 06:00 to 16:00. *Why it matters:* the edge the planner "holds" decides which way the bar jumps (OQ1, OQ15), and what happens when the drop cannot fit is OQ13. Source: 4.3.

**A run-time change.** *Today:* an order placed Mon 08:00 to 18:00 (10 h) on a plant open 08:00 to 20:00 has its run time raised to 14 h by a routing update. The bar becomes Mon 08:00 to 22:00, two hours past closing; nobody repairs it. At routing switch-on the browser re-places it from the start, Mon 08:00 to Tue 10:00 in two pieces under `partial_allowed`, and finds nothing under `never` (14 h exceeds the 12 h window). *Under the new rule:* the finish stays Mon 18:00 and the start moves left: pieces Sun 16:00 to 20:00 and Mon 08:00 to 18:00 under `partial_allowed`; start Mon 04:00 on a 24-hour calendar; under `never` no contiguous slot ends at 18:00, so the held finish is infeasible and an owner rule is needed (OQ13). If now is Sun 22:00 the walk reverses: Mon 08:00 to 20:00 plus Tue 08:00 to 10:00, finish Tue 10:00, 16 hours later than held. *Why it matters:* the finish SAP was given no longer moves with the run time. Source: 4.4 (SIM-A).

**The SAP round trip.** *Today:* SAP sends start Mon 19 Oct 06:00 and finish Wed 21 Oct 18:00 for a 20 h order on a plant open 06:00 to 22:00 Monday to Friday. The bar runs Mon 06:00 to Tue 02:00. If the planner presses Send before touching it, NIMBUS transmits Tue 02:00, 40 hours earlier than SAP's own finish (in this example SAP's 60 hour window is longer than the 20 hour run time; where SAP's window is shorter, as for 585 of 593 rows of the production-order sample in 8.11, the first Send moves SAP's finish later, 4.13.7; which case the pilot's planned orders fall in is unprofiled). If the planner instead places the order to finish Thu 22 Oct 12:00 and sends, and SAP stores the finish as sent and sets its own start (the document uses Wed 16:00, 20 elapsed hours earlier: NIMBUS's arithmetic, not an SAP result, **[unverified: needs SAP Development; assumption A9]**), SAP echoes Thu 12:00; ingest then stores Thu 12:00 as the due date, so lateness reads 0 where against the real due date it is 18 hours. *Under the new rule:* what an untouched order shows and sends depends on OQ33, whose rule 6.2 states once. Under the recommended option B an untouched Order Z keeps its bar Mon 06:00 to Tue 02:00 and sends nothing until a planner places it, so there is no first-Send error to correct. The numbers that follow assume option A (the placed finish starts as the due date) or an order the planner has already placed: placed finish Wed 18:00, derived start Tue 14:00, first Send transmits Wed 18:00. The derived start assumes a splitting policy (`partial_allowed`, or `overlong_only`, which also splits a 20 h order against a 16 h window); under the schema default `never` the 20 h order is one continuous bar and its backward rule is OQ50 (see the policy note after the shared example in section 4). After the planner's move the due date must survive the echo. *Why it matters:* O4: the SAP finish is never rewritten and the finish sent to SAP never drifts on NIMBUS's side; whether SAP leaves a finish alone once it has it is a separate question (4.13.2). Source: 4.5.1, 4.13.

**A distribution family.** *Today:* SAP plans 1,000 units on a work center from Mon 19 Oct 06:00 to Fri 23 Oct 16:00 (a timed finish for illustration; both sample workbooks hold date-only finishes, which OQ58 covers); NIMBUS splits it 60/40 into two machines, 6 h and 8 h, on a Mon to Fri 06:00 to 22:00 calendar. Child 1 shows Mon 06:00 to 12:00, child 2 Mon 06:00 to 14:00, and Send reports Mon 14:00, four days earlier than SAP's finish. A re-weight to 50/50 (5 h and 10 h) moves it to Mon 16:00. *Under the new rule*, if someone writes the shared finish (OQ58) and the children are placed: child 1 shows Fri 10:00 to 16:00 and child 2 Fri 08:00 to 16:00, Send reports Fri 16:00 (an unplaced child sends nothing, OQ33 B1), and a re-weight to 50/50 (Fri 11:00 to 16:00 and Fri 06:00 to 16:00) cannot move it. *Why it matters:* this is exactly "the finish sent to SAP never moves" for share changes; families created before the cutover stay start-spread unless the owner decides otherwise (OQ35). Source: 4.7.3, 4.7.9.

**An optimizer run.** *Today and under Reading A:* one machine open Mon to Fri 06:00 to 18:00, now Mon 19 Oct 08:00; order A (6 h, due Wed 21 Oct 18:00), B (4 h, due Thu 22 Oct 12:00), C (8 h, due Thu 22 Oct 18:00). The forward walk places A Mon 08:00 to 14:00, B Mon 14:00 to 18:00, C Tue 06:00 to 14:00. Those finishes become the placed finishes and what Send reports; the due dates are untouched. Later B's run time grows from 4 h to 6 h. Today the server read shows Mon 14:00 to 20:00 (two hours past closing, finish +2 h) while the browser reconcile re-searches forward and shows Tue 06:00 to 12:00 (overlapping C, finish +18 h). With the finish held B shows Mon 12:00 to 18:00 (overlapping A for two hours, an alert), and the finish does not move. *Why it matters:* two re-derivations that disagree with each other and with the placed finish are the reason every re-derivation path must change together. Source: 4.8.6.

### 2.3 What does NOT change

| Item | Why it stays | Anchor |
|---|---|---|
| Order ids, plant and machine keys | No finding proposes a key change; duplicate-id sequencing stays on the as-sent start, provided any derived start is assigned after id assignment | `db.py:3468-3482`, 4.5.15 |
| The `base_version` / xmin concurrency contract | The comparison under row lock is unchanged; a backfill or any new server writer bumps versions and stales in-flight edits. xmin guards the order row only: it does not detect a start that was derived on a different calendar, a different "now" or different neighbours (OQ51). | `db.py:1372`, `1302`, 4.1.7 |
| The planner's manual firm flag and the frozen-horizon setting | They keep their roles (the SAP firm flag stays display-only); what changes is that a derived start can cross the frozen window by data (OQ4), and the outbound firm flag SAP receives follows the derived start, which is an exception (4.11, OQ54). | `sap_staging.py:2148-2158`, 4.11 |
| Setup matrix, machine states, override rows | Setup is never stored; it is recomputed from adjacency on every read, so there is nothing to migrate on the server. An override row is keyed to an exact predecessor and successor pair, so a run-time change that reorders neighbours orphans it (4.9). | `engine.mts:434-437`, 4.9 |
| Priority lists (color, tooling, production version) | No workstream finding makes them depend on a bar's start or finish **[unverified: absence of findings, not a proof; see 13.1]** | 13.1 |
| SAP staging tables and the Mulesoft contract | Tables and the contract (one finish, the production version and the firm flag per aggregate) stay; only the value sent changes, from the computed elapsed end to the stored placed finish, and under OQ33(B) which orders are sent: a row with no placed finish sends nothing. | `sap_staging.py:2210-2211`, `2249-2272`, 4.5.4 |
| Queued (Needs Planning) orders | They still carry no dates; a database rule forbids stored dates on them | `schema.sql:1969-1976`, 4.11 |
| Split orders | Segments remain the authority; the last segment end is already the placed finish and no new column is needed | `db.py:222-245`, 3.2 |
| Wire field names | `start_date`, `end_date`, `original_end_date` can stay; their meaning changes (derived start, placed finish, due date) | 3.2 |
| Optimizer sequencing and its ranking objectives | Under Reading A it keeps sequencing forward; only its output contract is restated, and under OQ20 its instability and "moved" keys move from the start to the finish. | `engine.mts:2046-2048`, 4.8.1 |
| Calendars, blackouts, shift data, and ordinary calendar edits | Stored data is unchanged; calendar edits still do not silently rewrite schedules. A consequence the document had not stated: a stored start can go stale after a calendar edit and nothing re-derives it; who does, and when, is OQ51. | 4.2, 4.3 |
| Plant horizon settings (frozen, visibility, pull, push) | They stay plant settings; no server write path enforces them | `schema.sql:294-295`, 4.1.6 |
| The run-time bound of 0 up to but excluding 168 h | A representation limit independent of the anchor; it also caps the longest backward walk | `schema.sql:117-121`, 4.1.6 |
| Manual run-time precedence rules | They survive unchanged; only the release anchor of a held order needs a decision | 4.4 |

**Exceptions to the "does not change" rows.** Rows above say "unchanged" for structure. Six of them have an exception in the body, listed in 1.1 (items 1 to 10): the optimizer's instability key (OQ20, item 5); the outbound firm flag (OQ54, item 6); the override orphan (4.9, item 8); which orders Send (OQ33, item 7); the stale stored start after a calendar edit (OQ51, item 4); and the xmin limit (this section). The ones that bear on whether a bar moves are items 1 to 4 and 9 of 1.1.

## 3. Definitions

### 3.1 The five terms, in the code's own terms

| Term | Meaning in this document | Where it lives today | What is different under the owner's decisions |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Due date** | The finish SAP sent, as received, never rewritten (O4). | The wire field `original_end_date` is the raw column `orders.basic_finish_date` (`db.py:558`, `backend/scheduling/routes.py:196`). The raw as-sent copy is `orders.sap_basic_finish_date`, which is not on the wire. | Today the column is a mixture of three things: the finish as sent; a value the ingest invented (start plus run time) when SAP sent no finish, a finish not after the start, or an exact-midnight finish (`db.py:3962`, `3982-3988`, `4005-4012`); and the client's "end of the working day of the start" (`persistence.mts:1099`, written back by `db.py:1750`). After the first Send and echo it is also overwritten by NIMBUS's own placed finish (`db.py:2829`). Under O4 all three alterations must stop. |
| **Placed finish** | The finish the planner or optimizer placed; the schedule anchor, and what goes back to SAP (O4). | Not a stored concept today. `scheduled_end` exists and the browser writes it on every save (`persistence.mts:1416-1417`, stored as sent `db.py:1107-1112`), but the read path ignores it whenever a run time is set (`db.py:212-217`). | Becomes authoritative. For split orders it already is: the last segment end (`db.py:222-245`). |
| **Derived start** | Placed finish minus run time, walked backward through working hours, blackouts and setup. | Not a concept today. Today's start is a stored planner start or SAP's own start (`db.py:553`). | Must be a stored, client-written value (see 4.1: the server has no calendar). The server can only offer an elapsed approximation (finish minus run time). |
| **Reversal** | If the backward walk lands before now, place forward from now instead and accept a late finish (O2). | Nothing equivalent. The forward walk starts at the requested start and never meets "the past" as a limit. | New logic; needs a distinct result from the calendar engine (4.2). |
| **Effective end** | The server's current computed finish. | Two shared SQL fragments plus copies (4.1 table). | Retired as a concept for placed orders: the stored placed finish is read directly. "Effective" survives only as the read rule for an order never placed (6.2, pending OQ33: start plus run time under the recommended option B). |

Worked example (Order Z, the planner drags the bar so it ends Thu 22 Oct 12:00, which today means placing the start at Wed 16:00, 20 elapsed hours earlier, and saves). The browser sends a start and an end and the server stores both, but on the next read it shows start plus 20 elapsed hours, ignoring the stored end. If the resolver later changes the run time to 26 h the displayed end moves from Thu 12:00 to Thu 18:00 and the next Send to SAP carries the new, later finish (WS01-17 simulation; `sap_staging.py:2211`). Under the new rule the stored Thu 12:00 holds, the start moves left, and the finish SAP was given does not change.

### 3.2 Field roles, before and after (from WS07, ADJ-WS01 and VERIFY-WS02c)

| Field / wire name | Meaning today | Role after O4 | What must change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orders.basic_start_date` | SAP start after ingest; the bar start of an order the planner never placed; overwritten on every written re-ingest (`db.py:2828`). Also feeds production-version validity (`resolver.py:277`). | Information only (SAP's own back-scheduled start). Fallback bar start only until a derived start is stored. | Every reader that treats it as "the start of an unplaced order" needs a derived-start source (4.1, 4.5). |
| `orders.basic_finish_date` | Mixture of as-sent finish, ingest-fabricated value, client end-of-shift value, and (after an echo) the placed finish. | **Due date.** | Close the three alteration paths and guard the three write sites (4.5.3). |
| `orders.sap_basic_start_date` | Start as last sent by SAP; always equals `basic_start_date` at write time (`db.py:3533`). | Change-detection baseline and vanish key; never an input to placement. | Never let a NIMBUS-derived start land here (4.5). |
| `orders.sap_basic_finish_date` | Finish as last sent by SAP, NULL when SAP sent none (`db.py:3961`); after a Send it holds NIMBUS's own placed finish (echo). Not on the wire. | Change-detection baseline ("what SAP last sent"). It may correctly follow the echo. | It cannot double as the due-date store (it follows echoes and is NULL when SAP sent none). |
| `orders.scheduled_start` | Planner start override. | Derived-start cache: stored, client-written, authoritative. | Writers change from "client start" to "client-derived start"; running test, horizon gates and Send's firm rule read it. |
| `orders.scheduled_end` | Planner end as sent; ignored by the read when run time is set; returned only while the mismatch flag is set (`db.py:258-263`). | Placed-finish candidate (see 6: re-purpose vs new column). | The read stops overriding it. |
| `order_schedule_segments` | Authoritative productive pieces of a split order. | Unchanged: last end is the placed finish, first start the derived start. | No new column for split orders. |
| `orders.run_time` | Duration in hours, 0 up to but excluding 168 (`schema.sql:117-121`). | Width of the backward walk. | Reader code unchanged; effect on the start flips. |
| `orders.runtime_schedule_mismatch` | "Run time changed while a placement exists" (3 writers, 1 computed arm, 1 clearer; 4.1). | Meaning to be decided (OQ34). | See 4.1 lifecycle. |
| `order_sap_sent.sent_finish` | What NIMBUS last sent, plant-local; the echo input (`sap_staging.py:2256`). | Must hold the stored placed finish that was sent. | Send must read the stored finish (4.5). |
| `order_distribution.basic_finish_date` | A second stored copy of the finish, one per aggregate, refreshed on every ingest (`distribution/data.py:1173-1174`, `schema.sql:181`). | Must keep the finish as received. | Same echo guard as the order row (4.5). |
| Wire `start_date` / `end_date` | Effective start / effective end (`db.py:553-554`, queued orders NULL). | Derived start / placed finish. | Source expressions change; wire names can stay. |
| Wire `original_start_date` / `original_end_date` | Raw `basic_start_date` / raw `basic_finish_date`. | SAP start (information) / due date. | Remove the client rewrite of `original_end_date`; add it to `/tasks/refresh` (4.6). |

### 3.3 The alias-inversion trap

Three names mean different things on different sides of the same call. This is the single easiest way for an implementer to flip the wrong field.

| Name | Where | What it actually holds |
|---|---|---|
| SQL alias `BASIC_FINISH_DATE` | `db.py:554` | The **effective end** (segment end, else the mismatch-held stored end, else start plus run time). `routes.py:194` renames it to wire `end_date`. |
| SQL alias `ORIGINAL_END_DATE` | `db.py:558` | The raw `basic_finish_date`: the **due date** column. `routes.py:196` renames it to wire `original_end_date`. |
| SQL alias `BASIC_START_DATE` | `db.py:553` | The **effective start**. Renamed to wire `start_date`. |
| Client field `BASIC_START_DATE` | `persistence.mts:820-821` | The **raw SAP start**, synthesized from `original_start_date`; it is not on the wire. Same spelling as the SQL alias above, different value. Production-version validity reads it (`frontend/routing/runtime-client.mts:192`). |
| Client field `BASIC_FINISH_DATE` | `store.mts:910`; set only by the demo seeder and the distribution pane (`distribution-pane.mts:113`) | Effectively unused; no reader (VERIFY-WS02c W-F5). Deletion candidate. |
| Uppercase `ORIGINAL_END_DATE` fallbacks | `engine.mts:1092,1118`, `setup-scheduler.mts:1197,6223` | Dead on live data: the wire carries only the lowercase name; introduced in commit `eea65a8` (VERIFY-WS02c-1). |

Consequence: re-purposing any DTO field silently re-means the client's `BASIC_START_DATE` and the routing client's validity check (GAP13). Root `CLAUDE.md`'s phrase "raw SAP start" holds only because of the synthesis step in `persistence.mts`.

| Wire `original_end_date` | Raw column, client-rewritten in memory and persisted | Due date, never rewritten | high | `db.py:558`, `routes.py:196`, `persistence.mts:1099` | none pin the client phase (WS07-9); `tests/test_ingest_data_layer.py:840-856` pins the server function |

## 4. Impact by area

Each subsection states, for one area, what happens today, what happens under the new rule, a worked example, an impact table (surface, today, under the new rule, severity, anchors, tests that pin it), the open owner questions it feeds (numbered in section 12) and the items that could not be verified. Severity is blocker, high, medium or low. A test is named only where it was found to pin the behaviour; "none" means no test would fail if the behaviour changed. SAP field codes appear only inside the anchor columns.

Shared example, "Order Z" (used in 3, 4.1, 4.2 and 4.5): SAP start Mon 19 Oct 2026 06:00, SAP finish Wed 21 Oct 18:00, run time 20 h, machine open 06:00 to 22:00 Monday to Friday. Today the bar is Mon 06:00 to Tue 02:00 (start plus 20 elapsed hours). With the finish held at Wed 18:00 and the start derived backward through working hours, Wednesday contributes 12 h (06:00 to 18:00) and the remaining 8 h come from Tue 14:00 to 22:00, so the derived start is Tue 14:00.

**Policy label for Order Z.** The derived start Tue 14:00 above is a split bar: Tuesday's window holds 8 h (14:00 to 22:00) and Wednesday's 12 h (06:00 to 18:00). Order Z (20 h) is longer than the longest working window (16 h), so it splits under `partial_allowed` and under `overlong_only`. Under the schema default `never` (`schema.sql:293`) an order longer than every window is not split: `findContiguousSlot` flags it overlong and `allocateRuntime` builds one continuous elapsed bar (`calendar-engine.mts:428-435`, `540-547`). A backward elapsed walk then gives Tue 22:00 to Wed 18:00, which is the very value this document calls the server's wrong substitute. Whether a backward walk for an overlong order under `never` is a continuous elapsed bar, a refusal or something else is not decided here: OQ50. Most of the production-order sample is overlong in this sense (median Machine Hours 281.7 h against windows of at most 24 h; 8.11, sample-dependent). Every Order Z figure that depends on the split (the derived start Tue 14:00 and the 8-hour gap to the server's substitute in 1.2, 2.2, 3.1, 4.1.1, 4.1.5, 4.5.1 rows (a) and (d), and 4.5.7) is therefore stated for `partial_allowed` or `overlong_only` and is not a statement about `never`.

### 4.1 Server read/save path and SQL

#### 4.1.1 The merged variant table (V1 to V4) and every consumer

Today the server has no single finish formula. Two shared SQL fragments, a stored-end-first shape, a Python mirror, and a hand copy exist, and one order can show different finishes in different code paths.

| Variant | Expression | Anchor | Every consumer |
|---|---|---|---|
| **V1** plain effective end | stored start (else SAP start) plus run time hours; else stored end; else due date | `db.py:212-217` | save prefetch (`db.py:1282`); conflict scan (`db.py:1049`, `1056`); distribution aggregate roll-up (`distribution/data.py:2454-2462`, a regex rewrite of the SQL text) |
| **V2** plain effective end with a hold | V1 plus a hold: while the mismatch flag is set, return the stored end | `db.py:258-263` | `GET /tasks` (`db.py:554`); `/tasks/refresh` (`db.py:842`); Send to SAP (`sap_staging.py:2211`, group end is the latest member end `2184-2189`); distribution child read (`distribution/data.py:3027`) |
| **V3** stored end first, no run time | `COALESCE(scheduled_end, basic_finish_date)` | `db.py:1829` (purge), `db.py:2188-2189` (diagnostics) | purge preview and delete; deep stats |
| **V4** Python mirror | V1 without the hold, written in Python (`_order_is_running`) | `db.py:3216-3226` | SAP-change reset protection (`db.py:3652`); resolver running set (`resolver.py:608-628`); zero-open sweep (`sap_staging.py:~1793`); vanish detail (`sap_staging.py:786-802`) |
| V1 hand copy | V1 re-typed in the setup domain, with its own segment lateral, no hold and **no queued-order filter** | `backend/setup/data.py:497-511` | last completed order for derived machine state |
| Segment envelope | first start and last end of the order's segments (the lateral join) | `db.py:222-245` | first term of every projection |
| Computed mismatch arm (not stored) | a mismatch computed from the segments: two or more segments whose productive minutes differ from the run time | `db.py:247-252` | `/tasks/refresh` (`db.py:845`), distribution child read (`distribution/data.py:3023`) |

The start expression is not shared either. The three-way form (queued rows NULL, else first segment start, else stored start, else SAP start) is typed inline at `db.py:553`, `654`, `658`, `701`, `841`, `1281`, `sap_staging.py:2210`, `distribution/data.py:2451`, `3025`; the two-way form at `db.py:1039`, `1048`, `1055`, `backend/setup/data.py:993`, `997`, `schema.sql:78`, `89`.

Worked example (a flagged order; a splitting policy is assumed, see the policy note after the shared example). Order Z was placed calendar-aware, Tue 14:00 to Wed 18:00, and saved; the resolver then changes its run time to 26 h and sets the flag. `/tasks` and Send show the stored Wed 18:00 (V2); the save prefetch and the conflict scan judge it at start plus run time (V1) = Wed 16:00, two hours earlier than the board shows. The distribution docstrings claiming the aggregate "can never drift" from the Gantt (`distribution/routes.py:200`, `distribution/data.py:2427`) are false for flagged children. Under the new rule all of these must read one stored finish or the board, the save validator, the conflict scan, Send, purge and the setup observer will disagree.

#### 4.1.2 Impact table

| Surface | Today | Under the new rule | Severity | Anchors | Tests pinning it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| End formula (V1) | Run time wins over a stored end | Stored placed finish wins. For a row never placed the read rule of 6.2 applies (pending OQ33: start plus run time under the recommended option B; the due date under option A) | blocker | `db.py:212-217` | `tests/test_task_response_models.py:296` (column order of the refresh row); the expression text itself is not grepped by any test (zero hits for `_EFF_END` in `tests/test_distribution.py`, ADJ-WS01 R1); behavioural pins unverified |
| V2 mismatch hold | Only "finish held" branch; flag set by 3 writers | Collapses into V1 for the end side (INFERENCE, ADJ-WS01 Q01.7) | high | `db.py:258-263` | `tests/test_distribution.py:741-745`, `4035` |
| Save prefetch and edge completion | A missing edge is borrowed from the old derived edge | The server cannot complete a single edge correctly (no calendar) | medium | `db.py:1281-1282`, `1493-1495`, `1551-1558`, `1572-1573` | `tests/test_task_concurrency.py` (stale/xmin cases; line-level pin unverified) |
| Duration validation | None for continuous orders; segments only | Needed once the stored finish is read as truth | high | `db.py:1521-1522`, `1551` | none (nothing to pin today) |
| Flag clearing on save | Any browser save clears it | Must not clear without a matching width | high | `db.py:1585`, `1128-1129`, `persistence.mts:1423` | `tests/test_distribution.py:4371-4384` |
| Conflict scan | Start-keyed window, V1 end. The lookback is sized by the longest elapsed run time, capped at 30 days. Advisory: the batch commits and reports. The strict optimizer save (atomic Apply with strict conflicts) is the one path that rolls the whole batch back, and it judges overlap on the same elapsed end | Window sized from the start; end check reads the stored finish. The elapsed lookback can miss a bar whose calendar span is longer than its run time (OQ27). #### 4.1.3 Edge completion on save: the exact rule

A browser save carries both edges and always a `schedule_segments` key (empty for continuous orders), so the following applies to other callers but the hazards matter once the stored finish is trusted.

1. A missing edge is taken from the prefetch, the order's current effective edge, not recomputed from the newly sent edge. The borrowed end is V1: the OLD start plus run time (stored end only if run time is NULL). The server never computes new start plus run time and never derives a start (`db.py:1493-1495`).
2. The borrowed edge is only used to validate, except when the request carries a segments key (`db.py:1347`): then the completed pair is written (`db.py:1572-1573`). **Segments-key hazard:** a start-only request that also says `schedule_segments: []` writes the borrowed (derived) end into the stored end. Reachable only by non-browser callers; neither original report saw it (ADJ-WS01 R2).
3. Start-only, no segments key: rejected if the new start is at or after the old derived end (`db.py:1551`); otherwise only the start is written and any stored end is left (possible `chk_orders_sched_range` violation against a stale stored end is an INFERENCE, `schema.sql:94-97`).
4. End-only: validated against the old effective start; only the stored end is written; the read then ignores it when a run time is set.
5. Segments present and non-empty: sent edges must equal the segment envelope (`db.py:1533-1537`).

Worked example. Order Z has a stored start Mon 06:00, run time 20 h, so the old derived end is Tue 02:00. A caller sends only a new start of Wed 16:00: rejected (Wed 16:00 is after Tue 02:00) even though a 20 h bar from Wed 16:00 is perfectly valid. A caller sends only a new start of Mon 12:00 plus an empty segments list: stored end becomes Tue 02:00, a value belonging to the old placement. Under the new rule a single-edge write has no correct completion on the server; "reject single-edge writes" is listed under options raised and is tied to OQ1.

#### 4.1.4 The mismatch flag: lifecycle

| Event | Effect on the stored flag | Anchor |
|---|---|---|
| Resolver cutover on a placed, scheduled order | set TRUE | `backend/routing/resolver.py:674-679`, `718` |
| Ingest upsert of a distribution child whose run time changes and that has a planner start or segments (not gated by routing) | set TRUE | `db.py:2842-2852` |
| Child upsert from distribution writes (same shape) | set TRUE | `distribution/data.py:1380-1386` |
| Ordinary order, Excel re-upload changes run time (routing-off plant) | **not set**; start held, end moves silently | `db.py:2852`; GAP01-3 |
| Resolver run-time change outside a cutover (including a production-version flip after an echo) | **not set** | `resolver.py:673-679`; GAP02 |
| Order with 2 or more pieces whose productive minutes differ from run time | computed TRUE at read, never stored | `db.py:247-252` |
| Any browser save carrying an edge or the segments key | cleared; no width check | `db.py:1585` to `1128-1129` |
| SAP-change reset (`db.py:3663-3666`) and routing hold (`resolver.py:~765-769`) | untouched; a stale TRUE survives | grep finds no other writer |

Readers: V2 (`/tasks`, refresh, Send, distribution child read) and the alert rule that reads only the flag (`frontend/nimbus-compute-core.js:781`, `784`). Under the new rule the alert and V2 lose their old meaning: the board shows the stored finish for every placed order regardless of the flag. Options raised (not conclusions): (a) the flag means "stored start is stale", set by every run-time trigger and cleared only by a save that passes a duration check; (b) retire the flag and let the client re-derive on load. Either way the ingest signal that exists only for distribution children (`db.py:2847-2852`) is the in-repo template for extending the signal to every placed order (GAP01-10).

#### 4.1.5 The "no server calendar" verdict and its consequence (design-determining)

Postgres can subtract `run_time * INTERVAL '1 hour'` (the operator at `db.py:214`), so it can derive an **elapsed** start. It cannot derive a working-hours start: there is no SQL function or trigger in `schema.sql`; work hours and blackouts are stored as data (`schema.sql:1056`, `1071`, `1094`, `1127`); the engine is JavaScript (`frontend/calendar/calendar-engine.mts` delegating to `frontend/nimbus-compute-core.js`). Working windows are one per day and never span midnight (`master_data.py:2576`).

Consequences, each stated for Order Z:
- The derived start Tue 14:00 can only be produced by the browser. The server's substitute is Tue 22:00 (Wed 18:00 minus 20 elapsed hours), later by 8 hours. This assumes a splitting policy (policy note after the shared example). Under `never`, if the backward rule for an overlong order is a continuous elapsed bar (one possible answer to OQ50), the browser's own result is the same Tue 22:00, and the 8-hour gap exists only where the order is split.
- Split orders already prove the model: their pieces are stored client-computed and only validated server-side (`db.py:336-398`, `1533-1537`); a finish alone cannot encode where the pieces fall.
- Every server reader of "the start" (running test, reset fallback, Send's firm rule, horizon gates, vanish key) therefore either reads a stored client-written start or an elapsed approximation. Which one is the whole difference between a safe and an unsafe running-order test (4.5.7).
- A one-hour wall-clock vs elapsed difference exists across a daylight-saving change (server timestamps are naive wall clock, `db.py:214`; the browser uses epoch milliseconds, `persistence.mts:977`): low, relevant only to a provisional start (WS01-12).

#### 4.1.6 Indexes, horizons and constraints

Start-keyed: `idx_orders_basic_start`, `idx_orders_machine_start`, `idx_orders_machine_eff_start`, `idx_orders_plant_eff_start`, `idx_order_schedule_segments_order_start`, `idx_order_distribution_plant_start`; filters and sorts at `db.py:653-654`, `658`, `701`, `1038-1056`, `routes.py:179`, `setup/data.py:997`, `distribution/data.py:2084-2087`, `2133`, `2442-2445`, vanish `sap_staging.py:710`, firm flag `sap_staging.py:2156`, frozen warning `distribution/data.py:3102`, `3141`. There is no index on any end expression. The comment at `schema.sql:75` ("matches the ORDER BY exactly") is inaccurate: the index is two-way, the ORDER BY is three-way with a lateral alias (`db.py:658`); non-use of the index is an INFERENCE (no EXPLAIN). No write path enforces the frozen horizon or the pull/push windows server-side; they are master-data settings only. A derived start is at most 168 h before the finish for a continuous order (`schema.sql:117-121`).

Constraints: `chk_orders_sched_range` (`schema.sql:94-97`) is `NOT VALID`, exists only in `schema.sql` (no dated migration) and is checked on every UPDATE of a row; `orders_planning_state_check` forbids stored dates on a queued order (`schema.sql:1969-1976`).

#### 4.1.7 xmin, history and the open data question

The `base_version` contract is unchanged (comparison `db.py:1372` under row lock `1302`). Any new server writer bumps xmin and stales in-flight planner edits; Send to SAP writes only `order_sap_sent` and deliberately does not bump it (`sap_staging.py:~2256-2272`, read by agreement of both reports, not re-read by the adjudicator).

What the historical stored end contains is **unknown from the repo**: two code comments disagree in tone (`db.py:205-206` "most stored scheduled ends hold a flat SAP-window duration"; `db.py:1824-1828` the three predicates "agreed exactly" on 1,842 orders in one plant on 2026-09-08) and the measurement is not in the repo (ADJ-WS01 R6). Profiling SQL is in section 8 of the final document.

**Options raised, not decided** (all from the workstream reports): a single shared start fragment and end fragment before any rule change; collapse V2 into V1; add a duration validator and gate flag clearing on it; reject single-edge date writes; delete the baseline-correct route (4.6); let the resolver write a provisional elapsed start in the same statement as the run-time change; add a queued-order filter to the setup copy.

**Open owner questions this section feeds:** OQ1 (single-edge writes and which edge a gesture anchors), OQ3, OQ4, OQ5, OQ7, OQ32 (re-purpose `scheduled_end` or add a column), OQ34 (fate of the mismatch flag).
**[unverified]:** index usage (no EXPLAIN); the content of historical stored ends; `routes.py:443-444` (singular `/task/update` maps any invalid result to a 400) and `db.py:1472-1481` (routing-resolved run time stale rejection) were taken by agreement of two reports, not re-read.

### 4.2 Calendar engine and mirrors

#### 4.2.1 Primitive matrix

Every placement primitive lives only in `frontend/calendar/calendar-engine.mts`. The shared compute core (`frontend/nimbus-compute-core.js`) exports window and capacity math only; the compute worker (`frontend/nimbus-worker.ts`) dispatches alerts and utilization and places nothing. The optimizer re-implements availability independently in `setup-scheduler.mts`.

| Primitive (calendar-engine.mts line) | Direction today | In core / worker? | Backward twin needed? | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nextAvailable` 261 | forward; null on no window, overlong, nothing in 90 days | no | yes (`latestAvailable`: day-walk back, clamp finish to window close, floor-snap, jump to block start) | `tests/modules/calendar/calendar-engine.test.mjs` (null contract, snap-up, 90 d bound) |
| `_nextContiguousMinuteSlot` 394, `findContiguousSlot` 429, `nextOperatingInstant` 346 | forward | no | yes | `capacity-allocation-integration.test.mjs:111-116`, `remove-backlog.test.mjs` |
| `_freeIntervals` 495 | forward, 90 days after `from`, clipped on the left only, rebuilt per call | no (optimizer has its own index) | yes (right clip at the finish; lookback bounded by now) | `capacity-allocation-integration.test.mjs:58-63`, `73-81` |
| `allocateRuntime` 531 | forward fill, earliest fragments first, minimum-piece rule | no | yes (fill from the latest fragment; mirror the rule) | integration test, `split-order.test.mjs`, `engine.test.mjs` |
| Calendar `placeWithSetup` 603 | forward adapter | no | yes (setup rule is OQ2) | `split-order.test.mjs` |
| `workWindow` 168, `_dayWindow` 161, `_blockingIntervals` 449, `_ceilMinute`/`_floorMinute` 437/443, `hasNominalWindow` 378, capacity functions | direction-neutral | window and capacity delegated to core; `workWindow` partly duplicated | no (reusable as-is) | `tests/js/compute-core.test.js` |
| `fitsContinuous` 337 | direction-neutral | no | usable as the backward validity check | only `capacity-allocation-integration.test.mjs:65-71`; **no production caller** |
| Persistence `CalendarService` seam | forward `nextAvailable` only | n/a | widen the interface and the wiring | `persistence.mts:134-139`, `frontend/app.js:285-290` |

The detached optimizer's pure `placeWithSetup` (`setup-scheduler.mts:307`), its free-interval index (`2450`, `2524`, `2554`) and its availability walkers need backward versions only for the just-in-time reading; under the finish-anchored reading, store-verbatim ("A-lite") needs no new primitive inside the optimizer, whereas re-deriving the start of an optimizer output ("A-strict") needs a backward placer of roughly 200 to 260 lines shared with the just-in-time post-pass (XC-R3). That is an open owner question (OQ14, section 12). `Calendar.workWindow` duplicates core's `workWindow` despite the root CLAUDE.md claim; a third copy sits in the optimizer (`localWindow`, `intersectWindows`, `jointWindowForDay`).

#### 4.2.2 The mirrors and the worker payload

No placement code is mirrored in core or any worker, so a backward placer is a new function in `calendar-engine.mts` (and, only for the just-in-time reading, a second one in `setup-scheduler.mts`). The payload carries everything a backward walk needs: the optimizer snapshot has calendars, blocks, plant policy, `frozenHorizonEnd`, and the request carries `now`, `planningStart`, `horizonEnd` (`engine.mts:168-184`, `optimizer-worker-contract.mts:22-26`); due dates ride inside whole task objects. The compute worker needs no change for placement; a late alert would need the due date, which is already on the task (only the production version is stripped, `services.mts:187-190`).

Default shift hours (7 to 19, weekends off) are stored independently in four places (core `DEFAULT_SHIFT`, `Config.DEFAULT_SHIFT`, `engine.mts:286`, store), and the optimizer's `hasNominalWindow` returns false for a missing calendar where the walkers default; a backward twin inherits that existing divergence.

#### 4.2.3 Simulation 1: a held finish cannot always be honoured (the `never` / `overlong_only` blocker)

Setup: machine and plant open Mon to Fri 06:00 to 18:00; a 2 h blackout Thu 22 Oct 10:00 to 12:00; minimum productive piece 30 minutes. Free fragments: Wed 06:00-18:00, Thu 06:00-10:00 and 12:00-18:00, Fri 06:00-18:00. Order: 8 h.

| Case | Backward result | Forward re-derivation from that start |
|---|---|---|
| Finish Fri 14:00, any policy | start Fri 06:00, one piece. | Same: a fixed point. |
| Finish Fri 10:00, policy `never` or `overlong_only` | Fri has only 4 h before 10:00 and no Thursday fragment holds 8 h (4 h and 6 h). The latest contiguous 8 h block is Wed 10:00 to 18:00. **The held finish Fri 10:00 cannot be honoured; it moves to Wed 18:00**, two days earlier. | n/a |
| Finish Fri 10:00, policy `partial_allowed` | pieces Thu 14:00-18:00 and Fri 06:00-10:00, start Thu 14:00, finish held. | Forward `partial_allowed` reproduces it. **Forward `never` from Thu 14:00 jumps to Fri 06:00 and ends Fri 14:00**: the finish moved 4 h. |

Why it matters: "the finish never moves" holds only under a splitting policy, or when a window holds the whole order at the held finish. Any code that re-derives the end forward from a stored start (the server's V1 formula, the client's reconcile, the load-time snap, the schedule patch function) will move the finish on its next run unless every path becomes finish-anchored. The owner must choose what a held finish does when no contiguous slot ends there (OQ13): move earlier with an alert, refuse the edit, reverse forward, or treat the order as splittable for this purpose. Severity: blocker (semantics). Source: WS03-6, WS03-7.

#### 4.2.4 The null contract becomes "reached now"

Forward `nextAvailable` returns null for three reasons: no working window at all; the order is longer than the longest window (the helper never splits); nothing fits in 90 days. Callers treat null as "leave it unmoved" (`frontend/insights/services.mts:424-428`, `persistence.mts:976`, `engine.mts:1175`). For a backward walk the first two stay null (they do not depend on the anchor). The third becomes "the walk reached now before placing the order", which is the reversal of O2 and **not an error**: it must come back as a distinct non-null result so the caller flips forward from now; only if the forward attempt also fails is it a failure. A finish more than 90 days out also needs the lookback to start at the finish, not at now plus 90. Existing null handlers must be updated or a reversal will be silently swallowed as "do not move".

Reversal example (GAP01 simulation): order with a 6 h run time and a held finish Mon 19 Oct 12:00 on a 08:00-20:00 calendar. Backward start is Fri 16 Oct 18:00. If now is Fri 16 Oct 19:00 the walk lands before now, so the order is placed forward from now: Fri 19:00-20:00 plus Mon 08:00-13:00, finish Mon 13:00, one hour later than held, shown as lateness.

**Which "now" the walk uses (open, OQ52).** Reversal, the running test and the frozen test all compare a stored date with "now", and the code reads several clocks. The client running and frozen tests compare naive plant-wall-clock task dates with the viewer's own instant (`Engine.isFrozenHorizon` and `Engine.isInProgress`, `engine.mts:1015-1027`, default `new Date()`). The optimizer projects the viewer's instant into the plant zone and floors it to the minute (`engine.mts:2028-2031`). Remove Backlog projects into the plant zone and throws when the plant has no valid zone (`engine.mts:1293-1311`). The server uses plant-local now and falls back to UTC when the zone is missing (`db.py:3197-3206`). The header clock helper falls back to the viewer's clock and returns only hour and minute (`foundation.mts:749-767`). A planner whose browser zone differs from the plant's, or whose clock is skewed, sees an order flip into or out of running at a different moment than the server does. Which single clock reversal, running and frozen use, and what a plant with no timezone does, is OQ52.

**Bulk reversal has no ordering rule and an on-time reversal is silent (open, OQ53).** The cutover reconcile places each flagged order from its own start and sees no neighbours (`engine.mts:1258-1262`). Remove Backlog has a sequence-preserving cursor (`cursor = end`, `engine.mts:1387-1432`); per-order reversal has none. Example: three orders of 6 h, 4 h and 8 h on one line whose backward walks all land before now (Wed 10:00) are each placed forward from Wed 10:00 and all start at the same instant, overlapping, with alerts only. Separately, a reversal moves a finish later than the one held, not necessarily past the due date: an order held to finish Tue 20 Oct 12:00 with due date Fri 23 Oct reverses to Tue 20 Oct 20:00, which is still before its due date, so the "late" warning of OQ6(a) stays silent and the next Send reports the later finish with no signal. The ordering rule and the reporting of an on-time reversal are OQ53.

#### 4.2.5 Snapping, boundaries and DST

| Question | Rule found | Anchor |
|---|---|---|
| Boundary: finish exactly at window close | valid; no clamp | forward analogue `calendar-engine.mts:310` |
| Boundary: finish exactly at window open | zero capacity that day; hop to the previous open day's close | WS03-8 |
| Finish after close (for example 18:01 or 18:08) | clamp to the close; nearest 15-minute snap of 18:08 gives 18:15, which is after close | `foundation.mts:225-228` (`Util.snap` is nearest) |
| Blackout rounding | forward rounds the block END up so the start clears; backward must round the block START down so the finish clears | `calendar-engine.mts:263`, `317-320`; free-interval rounding is already symmetric (`496-509`) |
| Derived start grid | only minute-aligned unless re-snapped; a second snap would break start plus run time equals finish | WS03-9 |
| DST | calendar window math reads the browser's local date getters on naive wall-clock task values, so it follows the viewer's clock, not the plant zone (`engine.mts:1288-1290`); the one exception is `Engine._plantWallNow` (`engine.mts:1293-1311`), which projects "now" into the plant zone and is used by Remove Backlog only; durations in epoch ms; day hops must use `setDate(getDate() - 1)` never minus 24 h | `nimbus-compute-core.js:72-78`, `248-260` |
| Fall-back hour | a finish inside the repeated hour serializes as a naive string and reloads one hour earlier | `foundation.mts:366`; low |
| Daylight-saving tests | no test pins `nextAvailable` or `allocateRuntime` across DST; the F2 index-versus-day-walk test is the nearest | `setup-scheduler.test.mjs:5615-5617` |

Worked example (DST). Seven-day plant open 00:00 to 24:00; Sunday 8 March 2026 has 23 elapsed hours in Chicago. Finish Sun 04:00 CDT, 5 h order: Sunday contributes 3 elapsed hours (the wall clock reads 4), Saturday 22:00 to 24:00 supplies the other 2; the two pieces touch and merge into one bar Sat 22:00 CST to Sun 04:00 CDT, 5 elapsed hours but 6 wall-clock hours. Wall-clock subtraction would return Sat 23:00, giving only 4 hours. Two planners in different browser time zones would derive different starts for the same finish (WS03-13).

**Degenerate inputs the backward walk must answer (undecided).** None of the rows below has an owner decision; they are decided with OQ13 (a held finish that cannot be honoured), which is extended to cover them, except the last row.

| Input | What the code does today | What the walk would do under the boundary rules above | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A finish inside a blackout or on a closed day, from a system source (a date-only SAP finish at 00:00, or a blackout added after the finish was set) | The finish is never walked: end is start plus elapsed run time | Clamp to the latest operating instant before it (blackout start rounds down, closed day goes to the previous open day's close). Example: date-only finish Mon 26 Oct 2026 00:00 read literally (OQ23(a)) on a Mon to Fri 06:00 to 22:00 line clamps to Fri 23 Oct 22:00, three calendar days earlier, with no alert unless OQ13's alert is raised; under OQ23(b) the same row reads Mon 26 Oct 22:00 | Undecided; with OQ13 and OQ23 |
| Run time zero or NULL | Run time 0 is legal (`chk_orders_run_time_bounds` allows `run_time >= 0`, `schema.sql:117-121`) but both patch functions return null for zero or non-finite minutes (`engine.mts:1172`, `1210`), so no derived start is produced; the reconcile then logs a "90-day calendar search" warning that does not describe the cause (`engine.mts:1260-1264`). A NULL run time is a routing hold and has no dates. A stored range must increase strictly (`chk_orders_sched_range`, `schema.sql:94-97`, `scheduled_end > scheduled_start`), so a placed zero-run-time order has no storable start equal to its finish | A derived start equal to the finish cannot be stored | Undecided. The 26 sample rows with finish equal to start (8.11) are SAP dates, a different thing from run time 0; how many live orders have run time 0 is unprofiled |
| A shutdown of many days (a blackout across all lines) | No walk | A finish inside or just after the shutdown clamps to the latest operating instant before it, possibly weeks earlier, and the lookback has no stated backward bound (the forward walk stops at 90 days, `calendar-engine.mts:264-267`). Example: a blackout Mon 21 Dec 2026 to Fri 15 Jan 2027 on every line, and a finish Wed 6 Jan 2027 12:00: clamps to Fri 18 Dec 22:00, 19 days earlier | Undecided: a maximum earlier move, and whether it is reported |
| A finish in the first minutes of a window (minimum-piece landing) | The tail rule protects the last piece going forward | A held finish inside a window's first minimum-piece minutes is a second infeasibility trigger, separate from OQ13 (4.11, backward allocation table) | Owner decision: OQ55 |

**The DST primitive is viewer-local, not plant-local (OQ46, effort not yet sized).** The DST row above says day hops must use calendar-date arithmetic. The calendar engine's own hops are `next.setDate(next.getDate() + 1); next.setHours(0,0,0,0)` (`calendar-engine.mts:298`, `304`, `312`), and window reads use the viewer's local getters (`_dayWindow` delegates to the core, `calendar-engine.mts:161-163`). The shared core already records that `setHours(0)` fails in zones where a DST jump skips local midnight and builds the next day from local year, month and day instead (`nimbus-compute-core.js:74-78`); the calendar engine's hops have not adopted that form. So the Chicago example above is right for a zone whose change does not skip midnight and for a walk crossing a change in the viewer's own zone. A walk that crosses a change in the plant's zone but not the viewer's (or the reverse) can give two planners different starts. OQ46's recommendation (plant zone for any stored backward walk) must be sized before it is accepted: every local getter and `setHours` in the engine (`calendar-engine.mts:161-168`, `298`, `304`, `312`) and the core's window readers would move to plant-zone arithmetic, and today's only plant-zone helper converts one instant, not a day boundary (`Engine._plantWallNow`, `engine.mts:1293-1311`).

#### 4.2.6 Free-interval index and the 24/7 divergence

`Calendar._freeIntervals` indexes nothing persistent: each call walks 90 days forward from the start's midnight. For a finish at F with a floor of now, one build serves only finishes up to now plus 90 days; beyond that the cap must move to the finish. The optimizer's index covers `[planningStart midnight, horizonEnd]` and can serve a backward query for any finish inside the horizon with a reverse scan; beyond the horizon it falls back to a plain day walk (a performance cliff for far-out due dates, a hazard only for the just-in-time reading because the forward optimizer never leaves the span; XC-R1).

Existing divergence a backward twin inherits: for a 24/7 plant the optimizer merges intervals across midnight (`setup-scheduler.mts:147`) so it can place a contiguous order across midnight, while the calendar engine's `never` policy cannot (per-day window, `calendar-engine.mts:310`). Two backward implementations would diverge on day one unless the owner defines "contiguous" once (OQ47).

Worked example (minimum piece, mirror). A 4 h 20 m order, finish Fri 10:00, `partial_allowed`: Friday holds 240 min, the leftover 20 min is under the 30 min floor, so Friday takes 230: pieces Thu 17:30-18:00 and Fri 06:10-10:00. The 10 unused minutes sit at the window-open side of Friday (WS03-19).

**[unverified]:** no execution; all traces are by hand. `Alerts.applyFix` `never` branch calls the calendar without a run bracket (WS03 learned), cost not measured.

---

### 4.3 Manual placement, every edit path, undo and history

**What happens today.** Every way a planner can place an order by hand (drag, grid cell, Inspector, Override dialog, Ctrl+K "Push +1 hour") ends in the same two functions. They take the START the planner chose, round it to 15 minutes, and set the finish to start plus run time as plain elapsed hours. They never look at working hours, blackouts or setup. The right edge of a dragged bar is read once, to decide "did anything move", and then thrown away.

**What the new rule needs.** The same functions must receive the FINISH and return a start. For a same-length drag in plain elapsed arithmetic the answer is identical to today. The difference shows up in four places: when the derivation consults the calendar, when run time differs from bar width (every routing machine move), on every resize gesture, and on split orders.

**Example.** Order of 10 h on a line open 06:00-18:00. The planner drops the bar so it covers Monday 09:00-19:00 (the right edge overhangs closing by one hour). Today the bar stays exactly there. Under the new rule with a calendar-aware backward walk it snaps one hour left to Monday 08:00-18:00. With a calendar-aware FORWARD walk from the start (the alternative anchor) it would jump a full day right to Tuesday 06:00-16:00. Which edge the planner "holds" decides which way the bar jumps (evidence for OQ1).
