#### The Store commit sites that the Haiku inventory missed

The first inventory said the Gantt "never writes a date" and listed no Store sinks. Verification corrected both. Dates land on an order through two Store sinks, and every one of the 25 sites above commits through them.

| Sink | Behaviour | Anchors |
|---|---|---|
| `Store.updateTask` | Replaces the task object, auto-sets status to "scheduled" when both dates arrive without a status, normalises, emits `task:update`. No equality check, so a no-op patch still emits | `store.mts:366-385` |
| `Store.updateMany` | Mutates tasks in place with the same auto-status rule; emits `tasks:bulkUpdate`. Undo goes through it with source "undo" | `store.mts:423-436`, `1005-1016` |

The Gantt itself calls them at four lines: dragged item (`gantt.mts:4456`), companions (`4457`), single drag (`4495`), unschedule (`4720`). `_normalizeDates` snaps only rows that carry no status (almost none after load) and overwrites a split order's start and finish from its first and last segment (`store.mts:909-932`). So a placed finish needs no Store exemption on single-piece orders, and on a split order the held finish is simply the last segment's end.

#### Drag simulation (worked example)

Line L1, 10 h run time, open 06:00-18:00 daily, weekends closed, policy "never", no setup. The bar currently shows Friday 04:00-14:00 (possible today because manual edits never snap). The planner drags it by +3 days 5 hours; vis moves both edges rigidly to Monday 09:00-19:00.

*Today (traced):* the handler computes `newStart` = Mon 09:00 and sees the end only in the `moved` test. `manualSchedulePatchFor` returns start Mon 09:00, end Mon 09:00 + 600 min = Mon 19:00, no calendar. The order is stamped scheduled, dirtied, an undo entry is pushed, and the save sends both edges. The server stores them, and on reload recomputes finish = start + 10 h = Mon 19:00, identical. Load-time snap skips it because the order is user-placed (`persistence.mts:953`). Result: Mon 09:00-19:00, one hour past closing, surfaced only by an alert. Note that "snap on save" does not exist (a correction to the survey): the snap runs on load and calendar hydrate (`persistence.mts:578`, `calendar-sync.mts:250`).

*Under the new rule, by option:*

| Option | Result for the drop at Mon 09:00-19:00 | What the planner sees |
|---|---|---|
| Hold finish, calendar-blind | start = finish - 600 min = Mon 09:00 | identical to today |
| Hold finish, calendar-aware backward | finish clamps to last working instant, Mon 18:00; contiguous 10 h gives start Mon 08:00 | bar jumps 1 h left of where released |
| Hold finish, drop at Mon 05:00-15:00 | 10 h cannot fit before 15:00 inside one window (06:00-15:00 is 9 h). The walk's own answer (OQ13(a), the latest finish that fits) is Fri 08:00-18:00. Under OQ13's recommended rule for manual drops the drop is refused and the bar returns to where it was before the drag, with an alert | bar leaps to the previous working day (Friday, three calendar days left), or snaps back to its old position |
| Hold start, calendar-aware forward (the same Mon 09:00-19:00 drop) | 09:00 + 10 h passes closing; next window Tue 06:00-16:00 | bar jumps 21 h right |
| Routing machine move to M2, run time 6 h, finish held | end Mon 19:00, start Mon 13:00 (raw) | bar shrinks from the left; today it ends Mon 15:00 and the vis bar keeps the dropped 09:00-19:00 width until a rebuild |

Conclusion for OQ1: same-length drags are invisible to the choice in raw arithmetic. The anchors diverge on routing machine moves, on resizes, on segment drags, and on any bar straddling a shift boundary once derivation is calendar-aware. A leftward jump can also cross "now", at which point reversal flips it forward from now.

**A cross-line drop checks nothing against the new line's calendar.** `manualSchedulePatchFor` sets `MACHINE: line` and then either rebuilds the finish as the snapped start plus run time in raw milliseconds (continuous orders, `engine.mts:1225-1232`) or translates every piece of a split order verbatim by one delta (`engine.mts:1233-1244`). Neither reads the target line's working hours. Under the new rule a held finish dropped on another line can land in that line's closed time, and the pieces of a split order can land on days the new line is closed. The machine-move rule (site S7) must name the new line's calendar for continuous orders and decide whether split pieces are re-walked or stay translated (OQ17 states what a split drop holds).

**Manual drops that cannot hold the finish.** The drop that falls to Fri 08:00-18:00 in the table above is the calendar walk's own answer. OQ13 recommends that a manual drop which cannot hold its finish snaps back to the previous legal finish with an alert; the leap appears in 2.2 and in OQ15(b) only as the walk's answer before that rule, and 1.4's OQ13 line now says so.

#### Right-edge resize is a no-op that still dirties

The Gantt options leave time editing on, with no move or resize callbacks (`gantt.mts:274-280`; grep finds no `onMove`/`onMoving`/`onUpdate`). On release vis updates the item's end **[unverified: vis-timeline 7.7.3 behaviour is inferred from the options and the handler, not observed; see the list at the end of this section]**. The handler snaps both edges, finds `moved` true because the end differs, sees a zero start delta, and runs the single-drag branch. That branch passes only the start to the patch function, which rebuilds the finish from run time, so the planner's new width is never stored. But `Store.updateTask` still swaps the task and emits, the app marks the order unsaved, and an undo entry titled "Move ..." is pushed (`gantt.mts:4495-4498`; `store.mts:366-385`). The vis bar keeps the dragged width because the store listener returns early for source "timeline" (`gantt.mts:521-526`). It snaps back only at the next rebuild. A left-edge resize is processed as a move of the start with the finish recomputed.

Correction to the migration log: the document note (F12 in the migration doc) says an edge-resize "persists a stored finish but reverts on reload". The visible effect is right (the bar looks resized and then reverts) but the mechanism is wrong. The resized width is never sent. The only stored finish is start + run time. Reading "honour an explicit resize" would need new code, not a read-path preference. The warning in the same note not to change the server's finish formula silently is still correct (`db.py:212-217`).

#### Auto-reflow has one caller, and the docs are wrong

The cascade that pushes later peers out of the way is called from exactly one place: the alert "Fix" button (`services.mts:449`). Drag, grid, Inspector and Override do not call it; tests pin that ("must NOT be called", `gantt.test.mjs:1296`, and the orders tests). Stale statements: `frontend/scheduling/CLAUDE.md` ("called from this domain's Interaction/drag handlers"), the input-flow diagram comment at `gantt.mts:3349`, and a comment near the segment-drag test. A drag that overlaps a peer raises an overlap alert and moves nothing. The cascade walks later peers in start order, skips peers that already end before the changed order's start, pushes a peer only if it starts before the cursor plus the required setup, leaves firmed, running, frozen and aged peers where they are, and re-places each moved peer forward. Direction is later only; upstream peers are never pulled earlier. Under the new rule the cascade still pushes later, but a pushed split order's finish is the forward placement's end, and a backward walk from that finish does not always reproduce the forward start (see 4.11, 620-minute example). This is the A-lite versus A-strict question (OQ14).

**Overlaps, the cascade and idle time under a held finish (open items).** Three facts and two undecided points that the document had not put together.

1. **Overlaps are alert-only today.** The only response to two overlapping orders is the `ovl-` alert (`nimbus-compute-core.js:435-441`, id at line 437). The save's conflict scan is advisory by default: the batch commits and the conflicts are reported (`db.py:1225-1231`). Only an atomic optimizer save with strict conflicts rolls the whole batch back (`db.py:1631-1638`), and it judges overlap on the elapsed end (`db.py:1049`, `1056`).
2. **No backward reflow exists.** `autoReflow` anchors its cursor on the changed order's end (`engine.mts:2658`) and pushes later peers only; its one caller is the alert "Fix" (`services.mts:449`); it reads `Store.selectedPlant` only (`engine.mts:2650`). A bar that grows left under a held finish therefore overlaps its predecessor and triggers nothing. A resolver or ingest run-time change is not a planner save, so not even the advisory scan runs.
3. **Nothing reclaims idle time after a shrink under Reading A.** A run-time shrink with a held finish leaves a gap in front of the bar (the one-hour gap in 4.9). Compaction happens only when the optimizer next runs; Reading B is deferred (OQ48). No idle or earliness figure measures the gap.
4. **Open item OI-1: who resolves overlaps created by finish-held growth.** The planner by hand, a predecessor-side cascade, or the optimizer on its next run. This is not yet an owner question; it is listed in the follow-ups (item 17) and should be raised if the owner wants overlaps resolved rather than alerted.
5. **Open item OI-2: the held-finish cascade is undefined.** Trigger (the alert Fix only, today; also after a run-time change?), direction (later only today; upstream peers are never pulled earlier), stop rule (the cascade passes over peers that are firmed, in progress, in the frozen window or aged, `engine.mts:2670`; those tests flip by data, 4.11) and reporting (a cascade-moved peer's finish moves later, which is its own held and possibly already sent finish; the only report is the toast for the changed order, `services.mts:449-452`). Follow-up item 18.

#### Undo, What-If, Time Machine, Diff

- **Undo** clones the whole task (both edges, segments, run time, status, everything except the firm flag) and restores it verbatim, re-applying the live row version (`store.mts:1005-1016`). Reason: restoring the firm flag would flip a lock with no save marker, so it is stripped.
- **What-If** clones every task plus calendars, blackouts and firms, and restores them together; applied-scenario undo asks first if calendars changed since (`sandbox.mts:42-128`). It stays internally consistent because calendars travel with the tasks.
- **Time Machine** snapshots start, finish, machine and segments but restores only the two dates (`nimbus-intelligence.js:1449-1467`). Segments, machine, run time and status stay current, and Store normalisation then overwrites the restored edges for a currently split order or nulls them for a queued one (`store.mts:929-938`). It is unpinned by any test.
- **After a calendar or run-time change** the restored pair was derived under the old calendar. Ordinary calendar edits are deliberately not allowed to rewrite schedules silently, so a derived start has to be stored, not recomputed on read. The same fact means a stored start goes stale after a calendar edit and nothing re-derives it (who does, and when, is OQ51). Time Machine restore additionally needs run time and segments in its patch or the restored pair contradicts the order.
- **Diff** calls a pure move "start", a finish-only change "finish" (`nimbus-intelligence.js:2226-2234`). Under the new rule a run-time change moves only the start, so it reads as "start", the opposite of today, and the headline delta (the start delta) is the less meaningful number. Three tests flip.

#### "Was this order moved?" detection

Load-time re-snap skips an order if it is firmed, split, flagged as run-time-mismatched, user-placed, or if its start or finish no longer equals the SAP start plus run time (`persistence.mts:948-965`). An end-moved twin already exists there. The cache overlay has none (it compares only start to the SAP start, `persistence.mts:865-895`), so an end-only edit is not overlaid from cache. The user-placed flag is defined two ways: the server says "has segments, or a stored start, or a stored finish" (`db.py:559`), the distribution pane says "has a stored start" (`distribution-pane.mts:116`). Under the new rule the SAP start stops being a schedule baseline once a placed finish exists, so "moved" must mean "placed finish differs from the due date" or the server flag, and the pane's definition must adopt the server's, or a placed child with no stored start would be re-snapped forward on every load.

#### Push +1 hour

Today: for policy "never" and fewer than two segments both edges move +1 h wall-clock and the stored width is preserved even if it differs from run time. Otherwise start + 1 h goes through the patch function and the finish is normalised to start + run time. The selection filter is only "has both dates", so firmed, frozen and running orders are pushed (Delete and Fix respect those locks; the palette does not).

Worked example (OQ8 evidence): order start Mon 09:00, finish Mon 17:00 (8 h wide), run time 6 h, policy "never". Today: Mon 10:00-18:00. On a partial-allowed plant: Mon 10:00-16:00. With the finish held and pushed +1 h: finish Mon 18:00, start derived 12:00 (raw), so the 6 h bar's left edge moves +3 h, not +1 h, because the old 8 h bar was not run-time wide. With a 6 h-wide bar in raw arithmetic the two readings coincide. Calendar-aware, a finish pushed past closing gains nothing, so "+1 h" degenerates at a shift boundary.

#### Segment-drag rule

Each segment of a split order is its own vis item, but the handler measures the delta against the PARENT start, so the whole order moves and the dropped segment's start becomes the order's first-segment start. Test data: segments Aug 20, 21, 22 at 08:00-16:00; segment 3 dropped on Aug 24 08:00 moves everything by 4 days, so segment 3 ends two days after where it was dropped. The test pins this as an owner-resolved rule ("OD-B1a", `gantt.test.mjs:1041`). Under the new rule a dragged segment's right edge is the order finish only for the last one. The anchor-neutral rule is rigid translation (delta = dragged edge minus the same segment's old edge), and it contradicts the pinned rule. This is a decision, not a derivable answer.

#### Distribution children under manual placement

A child drag writes only that child (start, finish, no siblings; each child row has its own version, so one save never bumps a sibling). Family moves exist only through multi-select ("Show on Gantt" in the pane selects all live children); firmed siblings are skipped silently (the "skipped firmed" list is declared and never filled, `gantt.mts:4404`). A closed-time drop is raw like any order; the child-specific effect arrives later, when the pane's reconcile forward-snaps a flagged child from its own start. Under the new rule a shared finish stays shared only if the family delta is applied to finishes. The shares editor's "Current start" column reads the stored start (else the SAP start), not the effective start the code comment claims; it would show a wrong value for a placed child whose start is derived (`data.py:2388-2397`; `distribution-pane.mts:817, 2479`). Full child semantics are in 4.7.

### 4.4 Run-time change propagation

**What happens today.** Nothing on the server recomputes a date when a run time changes. The routing resolver (and every other run-time writer) writes only the run time. The visible finish then moves at READ time, because the server defines finish = scheduled start (else SAP start) + run time, in plain elapsed hours (`db.py:212-217`). So every trigger holds the START and moves the FINISH, calendar-blind. The one calendar-aware repair is the browser's reconcile, reached only for orders carrying the "run time no longer matches schedule" flag.

**What the new rule needs.** The placed finish must survive; the start must be re-derived. Because the server has no working calendar, the derived start has to be stored (or derived by the browser); the server read can no longer be "start + run time".

**Example.** An order placed Monday 08:00-18:00 (10 h) has its run time raised to 14 h by a routing update. Plant open 08:00-20:00. Steady state today: Monday 08:00-22:00, two hours past closing, nobody repairs it. Routing switch-on today: Monday 08:00 to Tuesday 10:00 in two pieces (browser re-places it from the start). Under the new rule the finish stays Monday 18:00 and the start moves left (numbers below).

#### Trigger matrix

| # | Trigger | Path | Edge that moves today | Firm / frozen / running today | What flips | Sev |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Resolver after SAP or Excel upload (routing plant) | `db.py:3808-3817` -> `resolver.py:898, 796, 525, 348, 645, 690-728` | Start held, finish moves at read; no flag, so single-piece finish is calendar-blind; split orders flagged on read | Written for firmed, frozen and running alike; running protected only against being HELD (`resolver.py:872-889`) | Placed finish stays; start derived; reversal logic needed | blocker |
| T2 | Routing switch-on (first resolve of a plant) | same, `is_cutover` at `resolver.py:826-829`, flag set `:673-679` | Server shows OLD finish until the browser repairs; reconcile holds the start | NO order kept in place; firmed, SAP-firmed, frozen, running all flagged (test `test_audit_routing_db.py:327-343`) | Anchor := today's effective finish; reconcile goes backward | blocker |

Two behaviours must collapse into one. Steady state is calendar-blind (a bar can end after closing), cutover is calendar-aware (`resolver.py:673-679`, SIM-A). The migration must not carry both. Routing master-data edits also refresh only the narrow set in T4; orders from other run-time sources keep their old run time until a full recompute (`resolver.py:569-576`), so the cutover test matrix has to say which orders can move.

#### The mismatch flag, from the browser side

- **Set** by the cutover resolve, by the upload SQL for a placed distribution child whose run time moves, by the child upsert, and computed on every read for 2+ pieces when productive minutes differ from run time (`resolver.py:718`; `db.py:2842-2852, 247-252`; `distribution/data.py:1380-1386`).
- **Read** by `/tasks` and refresh (the finish returned while flagged is the STORED finish), by Send to SAP (`sap_staging.py:2211`), by the browser reconcile (`engine.mts:1259`), by the load re-snap skip (`persistence.mts:948`), by the refresh copy (`persistence.mts:1742`), and by the "runtime no longer matches" alert (`nimbus-compute-core.js:784`, hard-coded English, kept visible after the old window passes, pinned by `split-order.test.mjs:312-322`).
- **Cleared** only by a save whose payload carries a start, finish or segments (`db.py:1585` -> `1128-1129`), and locally by the reconcile (`engine.mts:1268`). Not cleared by a hold or by the SAP-change reset, so stale flags are possible today (`resolver.py:764-779`; `db.py:3663-3668`).
- **Triggers for the browser repair:** calendar hydration (`engine.mts:2777-2780`), a conflict refresh (`2782-2790`), and a distribution save (`distribution-pane.mts:1428`). The repaired schedule is marked unsaved and persisted only at the next explicit Save (`application-shell.mts:2252-2257`). Until then another session, and Send to SAP, see the old finish with the new run time.
- **Under the new rule** the flag's meaning flips from "stored finish is authoritative and the duration is stale" to "run time changed and the start has not been re-derived". Today's flagged state is already a held-finish state, so under the new rule it becomes the NORMAL state and the stale quantity is the start. The server-side variant that returns the stored finish while flagged becomes redundant. The computed 2+-piece arm stays valid. Hold and SAP-change reset must clear the flag (the order has no placed anchor left).

#### The cutover reconcile is unguarded

The reconcile runs forward from the order's current start for every flagged order. It ignores firm (stated in its own comment, `engine.mts:1247-1251`), has no running or frozen check, no clamp to now, and a guard on the start that must become a guard on the finish. Evidence that it can move a running order's start: window 08:00-20:00, running order started Monday 14:00, run time 6 -> 8 h, policy "never": the forward search finds 14:00 + 8 h passes closing and jumps to Tuesday 08:00-16:00. The order stops being running. Under "never", an order longer than the longest window is not repaired at all (the search returns nothing); the flag and alert stand. Severity blocker, because this is the only site that implements "bar grows right", and it runs in bulk at cutover.

**Two further hazards of the same reconcile.** (1) It runs when calendar hydration lands (`engine.mts:2777-2780`), including after the 8-second calendar fetch has timed out and the page has painted the offline cache or the default hours (`calendar-sync.mts:96-99`; the comment at `231-233` records that earlier passes "ran against default/stale hours"). A derived start saved after such a pass was computed on default hours and nothing records which calendar produced it; whether a derive-and-save waits until the calendar is authoritative is OQ51. (2) Each flagged order is placed from its own start with no knowledge of its neighbours (`engine.mts:1258-1262`); once the reconcile holds the finish, bulk reversal at cutover would land several orders on one instant (4.2.4, OQ53).

#### Running-order rule: evidence

The code says it directly: a re-derived run time "may move its end, never its start" (`resolver.py:610-613`, repeated in `backend/routing/CLAUDE.md`). That is true for the steady-state resolver (start untouched) but false for cutover (the example above). Resolved outcomes are never suppressed for running orders; only HOLD outcomes are (`resolver.py:872-889`). Facts for OQ3: there is no actual-start field anywhere, so a start in the past is a derived value with nothing to check against; a derived start can flip a running order out of "running" both ways (see 4.11 simulations); a shrinking run time can already end running status today through the finish edge.

#### Manual run-time precedence (survives the new rule unchanged)

(1) A planner can key a run time only on a routing plant while the order is held for an unresolved run time (UI) or pending (server); (2) the resolver never loads manual rows, in any mode (`resolver.py:559, 570`); (3) a machine move keeps it (`engine.mts:1189`); (4) an explicit production-version edit overrides it with the routing value (`db.py:1438`); (5) a SAP re-upload keeps it unless SAP changed the row, in which case the source resets and the resolver re-derives (`db.py:2864-2869`); (6) on routing-off plants the file's value wins on re-upload even over a manual row (`db.py:2861-2863`); (7) distribution keeps a routing or manual child run time, and N-to-1 collapse carries a manual one (`data.py:1348-1350, 2851-2856`); (8) Machine Hours override on the manual Excel path. Only the release anchor (T7) and "manual survives recompute with a held finish" need new decisions.

#### WS05 simulations (corrected arithmetic)

*SIM-A.* Placed Monday 08:00-18:00, 10 h, window 08:00-20:00 daily, run time to 14 h.

| Path | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Today, steady state (T1) | Mon 08:00-22:00 | two hours past closing; nobody repairs it |
| Today, cutover, partial-allowed | Mon 08:00-Tue 10:00, two pieces (12 h + 2 h) | repaired by browser, saved on next Save |
| Today, cutover, policy "never" | no result: 14 h exceeds the 12 h window | flag and alert stand |
| New rule, 24-hour calendar | start Mon 04:00 (18:00 minus 14 h), one piece | corrected: the lane wrote Sun 20:00 |
| New rule, partial-allowed | pieces Sun 16:00-20:00 and Mon 08:00-18:00; start Sun 16:00 | finish held |
| New rule, policy "never" | no contiguous slot exists before the finish | the held finish is infeasible; define the outcome (flag and alert, or fall back to forward) |
| New rule, reversal (now = Sun 22:00) | start Sun 16:00 is before now, so Mon 08:00-20:00 + Tue 08:00-10:00; finish Tue 10:00 | 16 h later than held |

*SIM-B.* Running order started Monday 08:00, now Monday 10:00, scheduled to 18:00, run time 10 -> 14 h. Today steady state: finish Mon 22:00, start unchanged, still running. Today cutover, partial-allowed: start held, finish Tue 10:00. Naive new rule: derived start (Sun 16:00, or Mon 04:00 on 24 h) is before the actual start and before now, which rewrites history. Literal reversal gives start Mon 10:00, finish Tue 12:00, so it moves both the actual start and the finish. A running order therefore needs an explicit third rule (start is physical, finish moves, today's behaviour). Shrink case: run time 1 h gives derived start Mon 17:00, in the future, so the order un-starts under the new rule.

*Analogous forward cases today (Q05.5).* Nothing enforces precedence: run-time growth pushes the finish into the successor and raises an overlap alert (`nimbus-compute-core.js:435-441`); no cascade follows. Nothing clamps manual or reconcile placement to now (only optimizer paths clamp). So the reversal rule is net-new logic for every non-optimizer path. Under the new rule growth pushes the START into the PREDECESSOR. That overlap is alert-only as well, and unlike today's it is created without any planner save: no backward reflow exists (`autoReflow` anchors on the changed order's end and moves later peers only, `engine.mts:2658`; open items OI-1 and OI-2 in 4.3), and the advisory conflict scan runs only on a planner save (`db.py:1225-1231`), not on a resolver or ingest run-time change.

### 4.5 Ingest, SAP inbound/outbound and the echo rule

#### 4.5.1 The six-scenario sequence table (plant on routing; zones equal; run time 20 h; Order Z)

| Scenario | Today (stored and shown) | Under the new rule | Anchors |
|---|---|---|---|
| **(a) First snapshot** SAP start Mon 06:00, finish Wed 18:00 | finish kept (later than start, not midnight); run time defaulted then resolved by routing; bar Mon 06:00 to Tue 02:00. **If the planner presses Send before touching it, the first Send transmits Tue 02:00, 40 h earlier than SAP's own finish (here SAP's 60 h window is longer than the 20 h run time; where the window is shorter the first Send moves SAP's finish later, 4.13.7).** | Which read applies to an untouched row is the rule of 6.2 (pending OQ33). Recommended option B: the row keeps the bar Mon 06:00 to Tue 02:00 and sends nothing until a placed finish exists. Option A: the placed finish starts as the due date Wed 18:00, derived start Tue 14:00 (splitting policy assumed; policy note in section 4) and the first Send transmits Wed 18:00, which equals SAP's own finish but not today's bar or today's Send. Under option A, if now is after Tue 14:00, reversal (O2) places it forward from now. | `db.py:3975-3980`, `3507-3510`, `sap_staging.py:2210-2211` |
| **(b) Unchanged re-snapshot** | no write, no xmin bump, no change detection | identical, but only if the as-sent start baseline is never replaced by a NIMBUS-derived start | `db.py:2762-2765`, `2914`; `tests/test_ingest_data_layer.py` `TestSapTruthReupload` |
| **(c) Planner finishes Thu 12:00, Send. SAP then sets its own start and, if it stores the finish as sent, echoes Thu 12:00** (illustrative: this document puts SAP's start 20 elapsed hours earlier, Wed 16:00. That is NIMBUS arithmetic, not an SAP result; SAP's start depends on its lead time, factory calendar and setup and queue time. **[unverified: needs SAP Development; assumption A9]**) | row is written (SAP start moved); due date Wed 18:00 is overwritten by Thu 12:00; no reset (finish echo); slot and firm kept | same, but the due date must survive; the echo test is the only shield (the slot echo needs SAP's start to equal the planner's, true only by coincidence) | `db.py:2639-2666`, `2829`, `2836` |
| **(d) SAP moves the finish itself** to Fri 06:00 (start Thu 10:00) | reset: slot, firm and segments cleared; falls back to SAP start plus elapsed run time | reset reads as a never-placed row (SAP start plus run time, nothing sent until a planner places it; 6.2, OQ33 B1); under option A it would fall back to the SAP finish with a derived start Wed 18:00 (splitting policy assumed; policy note in section 4) and a derived-start source would be needed until the next client save (4.5.7); the remembered sent finish (Thu 12:00) is not cleared and could later mask a genuine move back to Thu 12:00 | `db.py:3660-3669` |
| **(e) SAP changes quantity only** | reset (slot wiped) whether or not dates moved | owner decision: keep wiping, or keep the placed finish and re-derive the start (OQ25) | `db.py:2674-2688` |
| **(f) SAP returns a date-only finish (Thu 22 Oct, time blank or 000000)** | treated as midnight; hygiene replaces the stored finish with start plus run time; the baseline keeps midnight; a limited date-only echo acceptance applies | the start-plus-run-time substitute cannot stay; a time-of-day rule is needed (OQ23) | `sap_staging.py:184-227`, `db.py:2655-2659`, `4005-4012` |

Worked example for (c), quantified. The SAP behaviour in it is assumed, not measured (4.13.2). Planner places Order Z to finish Thu 22 Oct 12:00 and sends it. Suppose SAP sets its own start to Wed 16:00 (20 elapsed hours before the finish, which is NIMBUS's arithmetic and not SAP's lead-time result) and returns the finish as sent. Stored after the snapshot: SAP start Wed 16:00, finish Thu 12:00 in **both** the due-date column and the baseline; placed finish unchanged. Lateness of an end at Thu 12:00 now reads 0, where against the real due date (Wed 18:00) it is 18 hours late. "Every sent order turns green after the first Send" (WS07 simulation 5). If SAP instead moves the finish itself (float, its own reversal, rounding), the case is scenario (d), not (c); 4.13.2 sets out how that can happen.

#### 4.5.2 The ruled echo rule and its truth table (ADJ-WS06 2.a)

The two original reports stated one rule from opposite defaults. The rule, once: the SAP-changed signal "dates" is raised if and only if (the SAP start differs from its baseline OR the SAP finish differs from its baseline) AND NOT (both incoming edges equal the planner's stored slot to the second) AND NOT (the incoming finish matches the remembered sent finish to the minute, or is an exact-midnight value on the sent finish's date). Code: `db.py:2639-2666` (`dates_differ` 2639, slot echo 2641, finish echo 2653, midnight branch 2655-2659, decision 2665).

| Start differs | Remembered sent finish | Incoming finish versus sent | Raised? | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | exists | equal to the minute, or midnight on the same date | no (echo veto) | `tests/test_orders_routing_ingest.py:599` |
| yes | exists | differs by a minute or more | yes | test at `:605` (40 s tolerated, 1 min not) |
| yes | none (never sent, member skipped at Send, archive restore, purge cascade) | n/a | **yes, from the start alone** | `:628` (`test_no_sent_finish_behaves_as_before`) |
| yes, finish not sent | any | n/a | yes | n/a |
| no, finish differs | exists, equal | equal | no | n/a |
| yes | exists | midnight on a different date than sent | yes | `:640` |

Under the new rule the slot echo is effectively dead (it needs SAP's start to equal the planner's to the second), so the finish echo is the sole shield, and it depends on the remembered sent finish existing. Example: Order Z is never sent; SAP back-schedules its own start for an unrelated reason (a lead-time change). With no remembered finish the start difference alone raises "dates" and the planner's placement is wiped, even though the finish SAP holds did not change.

#### 4.5.3 The due-date overwrite blocker, across all four places

Under O4 the SAP finish as received is never rewritten. As the code stands it is overwritten on the first echo, by the ingest itself, with no client involvement. The row is written on an echo even when SAP's start is unchanged, because the finish differs from the stored baseline (`_SAP_DIFFERS_SQL` finish clause, `db.py:2764-2765`; write gate `db.py:2914`).

| Place the finish is stored | Overwritten by | After the first echo | Must hold under O4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. `orders.basic_finish_date` (wire `original_end_date`) | `_UPSERT_SQL`, `db.py:2829` | placed finish (or start plus run time if the echo is midnight, not after the start, or absent) | the due date: **guard needed** |
| 2. `orders.sap_basic_finish_date` (as-sent baseline) | same statement, `db.py:2836` (`COALESCE(incoming, stored)` keeps stored only when incoming is NULL) | placed finish | may follow the echo (it is the change-detection baseline) but then no column holds the original |
| 3. `order_distribution.basic_finish_date` (header, one per aggregate) | `_write_header_facts`, `distribution/data.py:1173-1174`, refreshed whenever facts differ (`1184`) | placed finish | the due date: guard needed (a fourth place no first report listed) |
| 4. Children: `basic_finish_date` and their baseline | `_CHILD_UPSERT_SQL`, `distribution/data.py:1355`, `1376`; values copied from the parent row (`784-785`, `898-900`) | placed finish | the due date: guard needed |
| (`order_sap_sent.sent_finish`) | Send | the placed finish | holds what NIMBUS sent; no due-date column exists there |

No column anywhere holds the original SAP due date after the first echo. The staging row holds the as-sent finish only until the next applied batch (retention rule from `backend/integration/CLAUDE.md`, not re-verified in code). Before the first Send, the true as-sent finish lives only in `sap_basic_finish_date`, which is not on the wire and is NULL when SAP sent none.

Where a guard must live (WS07): the three write sites are the order upsert (`db.py:2829`; the SAP variant is derived from it by string transform at `2926-2941` so it inherits an edit), the child upsert (`distribution/data.py:1355`) and the header refresh (`1174`, differs-test `1184`), or, in place of the order-upsert SQL edit, an in-memory patch of the incoming rows (the tuples built before the chunk transaction, `db.py:3538-3545`; the before-image already carries the sent finish, `db.py:3177`). The four stored places of the table above are covered by these three sites: the order upsert covers places 1 and 2, the header refresh place 3 and the child upsert place 4. The predicate to reuse is the corrected predicate of 7.3 item 1 (date-only detection before zone conversion), not the existing echo test as it stands (it fails at SAP-zone midnight, 4.5.5); in outline: incoming finish as sent equals the remembered sent finish to the minute, or the midnight-same-date branch); when true keep the stored due date, otherwise take the incoming value as a genuine SAP change. The echo test runs in Python **after** the upsert today, while the overwrite is in the SQL `SET`, though the before-image read precedes the upsert (`db.py:3168-3195`), so the deciding facts are available before the write. A guard at `db.py:2829/2836` alone is not enough: the child upsert and header refresh are independent overwriters and a later re-weight would copy the echoed finish from the header back onto the children (GAP03-7). `order_sap_sent` has no join in either upsert statement, so the guard needs a lookup inside the statement or the in-memory patch.

Residual risks the guard inherits (WS07, ADJ-WS06 open items): once sent, NIMBUS is the only keeper of the due date (purge and archive delete cascade the sent row; `restore_vanished_order` restores only the order and segments, `db.py:2073-2094`); if SAP moves a finish to a calendar boundary on import (design assumption A9, unverified) the echo never matches and the due date drifts every Send cycle; a stale snapshot racing a second Send can misread an old echo.

Whether the due date should be a new immutable column instead is an option raised in section 6 (OQ31).

#### 4.5.4 Outbound: Send transmits a computed end, not a stored finish

`queue_send_to_sap` reads `COALESCE(seg.last_end, mismatch-aware effective end)` (`sap_staging.py:2210-2211`), the group end being the latest member end (`2188-2189`), converted at `2249` and remembered plant-local at `2256`. In precedence: segment end; else the stored end while the mismatch flag is set; else start plus run time in elapsed hours (a stored end is ignored when run time is set); else the stored end, then the due date. The earlier assumption that "Send already sends the finish" is false in the stored sense (ADJ-WS06 2.c). Order Z: the first Send transmits Tue 02:00, 40 h earlier than SAP's finish (the direction depends on whether SAP's window is longer or shorter than the run time, 4.13.7). Under the new rule Send must read the stored placed finish and the remembered `sent_finish` must be that same value; children still roll up to the latest child end (4.7). Members skipped at Send (no end, queued) have no remembered finish, so their later echo resets (`sap_staging.py:2184-2188`, `2257`). Severity high.

#### 4.5.5 The midnight / L1 hole (systematic, needs no unusual SAP behaviour)

A real 00:00:00 and "no time" are indistinguishable by construction (`_parse_sap_time`, `sap_staging.py:184-207`); a date-only value is never converted back (`sap_to_plant_local`, `221-223`). Two cases (ADJ-WS06 2.e), and a third added by the second review (case 3 below):

- **M1**: the placed finish converts to exactly midnight in the SAP zone. Chicago plant on daylight time (UTC minus 5), SAP zone UTC (the unconfirmed default), placed finish Thu 22 Oct 19:00 plant-local is sent as Fri 23 Oct 00:00:00. SAP returns it unchanged; NIMBUS reads it as date-only, keeps Fri 00:00 plant-local, and the echo test fails on both branches (Fri 00:00 does not match Thu 19:00; the midnight branch compares Fri to Thu). Result: "dates" is raised and the order is reset **once for each distinct value SAP returns**: the upsert stores the returned finish as the new as-sent baseline in the same statement (`db.py:2836`), so the next unchanged snapshot equals its baseline and raises nothing. The reset is one placement wipe and it also clears the planner firm flag (`db.py:3664`). It recurs only if SAP later changes the start or the finish again, or the planner alternates finishes across the date boundary. After daylight time ends the finish is 18:00. The hygiene midnight rule also rewrites the same value afterwards. Exposure under the new rule: any placed finish on a window edge equal to SAP-zone midnight, which backward walks and planners produce far more often than scattered start-plus-elapsed values. The population is unknown from code (depends on `NIMBUS_SAP_SYSTEM_TZ` and window edges); the mechanism is certain.
- **M2**: a timed SAP finish that converts to plant-local 00:00 is rewritten by hygiene (`db.py:4006`) while the as-sent baseline keeps midnight, so the echo still passes but the due date column is corrupted.

- **Case 3, SAP discards the time of day [unverified: needs SAP Development]**: the Functional Specification lists an end time in both the export and the import (6.5, 7.2) but says nothing about whether SAP keeps it. If SAP stores planned-order dates without a time, every returned finish arrives as a bare date. The date-only branch then compares a date in the SAP zone with the date of the remembered plant-local sent finish (`db.py:2655-2659`), and a date-only value is never converted back (`sap_staging.py:221-223`). The false "changed" widens from one minute a day to every placed finish whose SAP-zone date differs from its plant date. Example: SAP zone UTC (the default), Chicago plant on daylight time. A placed finish Thu 22 Oct 17:00 is Thu 22:00 in SAP, returns as "Thu 22 Oct" and matches by date. A placed finish Thu 22 Oct 19:00 is Fri 00:00 in SAP, returns as "Fri 23 Oct" and does not match, so the order is reset; so is every finish from 19:00 to midnight plant time, which on a plant with evening-ending shifts is a large share of all placed finishes. A finish that does match by date still leaves a bare date as the stored due date, which hygiene then rewrites to start plus run time (4.5.6), so the due date O4 protects becomes a derived value again. Not measured: the only measured echo (validation plan S15) used a simulated SAP that kept the time of day.

**Where OQ23's reading comes from.** OQ23 (time of day of a date-only finish) was designed from two sample workbooks, which are Excel files with no time-of-day column (8.11), and from the code's date-only branch. It was not designed from the planned-order feed, whose specification does carry an end time. If the feed carries real times, OQ23 applies to the rows where SAP sends none. If SAP discards times, OQ23 applies to every returned finish and the echo branch above must compare dates in a common frame (the rule already stated at the end of this subsection). Appendix D, D.1 item 5, settles which.

The earlier example of a 19:30 finish crossing midnight (becoming 00:30) is safe. Rule to state: detect date-only where the time field is blank, before conversion; and compare dates in a common frame. Pinned (L1 quantified) in `docs/SAP_STAGING_VALIDATION_PLAN.md` S15 (5 of 5 engineered orders reset, 0 of 36 natural). Severity high.

#### 4.5.6 Hygiene rules and their inversion; requirements

| Rule today (`_date_hygiene_df`, `db.py:3941-4014`) | Anchor | Inverse under the new rule |
|---|---|---|
| Finish captured as sent before any repair | `3961` | keep (this is the due date as received); add the symmetrical as-sent start so `upsert_orders` never baselines a derived start (`db.py:3533`) |
| Missing finish filled with the start | `3962` | delete; a missing or unparseable finish is rejected or dropped with a warning |
| Run time defaulted to 1.0 h | `3975-3980` | keep; run time sets how far left the start goes |
| Finish at or before start becomes start plus run time | `3982-3988` | start missing or at or after the finish becomes finish minus run time (client calendar-aware); the finish is never rewritten |
| Unparseable start drops the row | `3990-3996` | unparseable or missing finish drops the row; a missing start is normal |
| Exact-midnight finish becomes start plus run time | `4005-4012` | cannot stay: a midnight can be a legitimate finish, and the substitute needs a start (OQ23) |
| Required columns: order, material, start | `db.py:4118`; staging `sap_staging.py:523-525` | finish required, start optional; the Excel path needs its own "reject missing finish" (it bypasses staging validation) |
| Malformed finish policy | staging rejects; Excel silently NaT, no warning (`db.py:3441-3442`) | one policy for both |

Pinned tests that flip: `tests/test_ingest_data_layer.py::TestApplyOrderDateHygieneRows`, `test_finish_dates_and_numeric_machine_normalised` (`:287-313`, pins a date-only Excel finish becoming start plus 2 h), `tests/test_sap_staging.py:216`, `286-287`.

Worked example. SAP sends finish Wed 21 Oct 00:00 (date only) with start Mon 19 Oct 00:00 and run time 10 h. Today hygiene writes the due date as Mon 19 Oct 10:00 (start plus 10 h); the baseline keeps Wed 00:00; the client then rewrote it to the close of Monday's window (4.6). Under the new rule the due date must be as received (Wed), plus a stated time of day for date-only finishes; the choices are: keep midnight literally, end of that date's working window, end of that calendar day, or reject the row. The ingest-derived start must also be assigned **after** duplicate-id sequencing (4.5.15).

#### 4.5.7 Reset fallback and running-order protection (blocker)

The SAP-change reset deletes segments and sets firm false, both planner dates NULL, status scheduled (`db.py:3660-3669`); the order then reads as a never-placed row: SAP start plus elapsed run time (the read rule of 6.2; under OQ33 B1 it sends nothing until a planner places it again). That is the right meaning under the new rule: a wiped placement leaves no placed finish behind, the bar shows today's served value, and no derived start has to exist in the interval between the reset and the next client save. (Only under OQ33 option A, where the fallback would be the SAP finish, would a stored derived start have to exist in that interval, because the server cannot walk working hours, 4.1.5; and after an echo that fallback would be the echoed placed finish, not the original due date, unless the due date is protected.)

"Running orders are never reset" (`_order_is_running`, `db.py:3216-3226`) fails in the unsafe direction in two ways, both valid:
- Approximated start (WS06): placed finish Wed 21 Oct 18:00, true derived start Tue 14:00 (splitting policy assumed; policy note in section 4), elapsed substitute Tue 22:00. At Tue 20:00 the order is on the machine; the test uses 22:00 and says idle; the reset wipes its slot and firm.
- Correct stored start but elapsed end (BLIND): placed finish Tue 20 Oct 18:00, true start Mon 14:00, test end Mon 14:00 plus 20 h = Tue 10:00. At Tue 12:00 the order is truly running (finish 18:00); the test says it is over.

Rule: protection works only if the test reads **both** a stored calendar-aware start **and** a stored placed finish (split orders already do: `db.py:3216`, `3219`). The same hazard sits in every copy of the elapsed end (`db.py:212-217`, `sap_staging.py:2211`, `backend/setup/data.py`), the resolver's running set and the vanish review flag. The resolver's own comment that a running order's re-derived run time "may move its end, never its start" (`resolver.py:612-613`) is the inverse of the held-finish rule for exactly the running orders (OQ3). Today the elapsed end and display agree, so the existing test is self-consistent; the hazard appears the moment bars become calendar-aware. Severity: blocker (data loss).

#### 4.5.8 Vanish predicate and start-less rows

The vanish test is `COALESCE(sap_basic_start_date, basic_start_date) <= visibility end + 1 day` (`sap_staging.py:709-710`, bound at `743`, `768`), one day wider than the read gate (`db.py:652-655`, design D8). A row with no start in both columns is exempt from the 25 percent safeguard denominator and from deletion. Latent today (both ingest paths reject or drop start-less rows), real if the new rule lets a start be absent. Which date SAP's export selects on is not in the repo (validation assumptions A5, A11) **[unverified: SAP-side fact]**. Keep the key on SAP's start as sent, add a finish fallback, confirm with SAP Development: a proposal, not a fact. Severity medium. The echo can also move the start baseline past the horizon edge.

#### 4.5.9 Time zones

Inbound converts SAP zone to plant zone (`sap_staging.py:210-227`, unknown plant zone means no conversion); outbound converts plant to SAP zone to the second (`230-242`); `sent_finish` is remembered plant-local (`2256`). The round trip is the identity except in the spring-forward gap (a nonexistent local time maps back one hour later) and the repeated fall-back hour; whether a backward walk can emit such times is 4.2. The SAP zone defaults to UTC "until SAP Development confirms" (`NIMBUS_SAP_SYSTEM_TZ`), which decides how often M1 occurs **[unverified: the real SAP zone is not known]**. A finish that SAP rounds by up to a minute (14:00:59 to 14:01) defeats the minute-precision echo [unverified].

#### 4.5.10 SAP's back-scheduled start: who reads it

It arrives and is stored (`sap_staging.py:392-394`, `db.py:2828`, `2835`) and is an input to the change test (`2639`). Readers (WS06): the bar start when no planner start exists (`db.py:553`); the visibility gate (`652-655`); production-version validity (`resolver.py:277`); the running-test fallback (`3216`, `3221`); the vanish predicate via the baseline copy (`sap_staging.py:710`). It is not used for placement once a planner start exists. Each of the first four needs an explicit decision under the new rule (OQ25 asks whether a start-only SAP change should reset a finish-anchored order at all). Severity medium.

#### 4.5.11 Routing-off plants (GAP01)

Plants with the routing switch off take their run time from the manual Excel file (since commit `621f81f`, Machine Hours when above 0, else the run-time column, else 1 h; on routing plants the upsert nulls it, `db.py:3507-3510`). SAP planned-order batches can never reach these plants: they are held "routing required" at validation and refused at apply even when confirmed (`sap_staging.py:728-734`, `1330-1332`).

| Trigger | Today | Under the new rule | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Excel re-upload on a routing-off plant changes an order's run time | run time rewritten (the difference is itself the write trigger, `db.py:2760-2761`); planner start and end untouched; **start held, end recomputed at read, calendar-blind, silently**; firmed and running orders included; no flag (only distribution children get one, `db.py:2847-2852`); the uploader sees a Machine Hours info line and a "changed by SAP" count that over-reports | placed finish is the intact stored end; the start must be re-derived; ingest needs a "start not re-derived" signal for every placed order whose run time moved | blocker |
| Run-time-only change and the SAP-change reset | run time is not one of the four judged fields, so no reset even for a firmed order (pinned `tests/test_ingest_data_layer.py:981-988`) | unchanged for run time; a firmed order whose run time grows gets its start moved with no un-firm (OQ4); pinned test flips or gains an assertion | high |
| Send to SAP | not routing-gated; sends the effective end, so a grown run time moves the finish SAP is given | with the finish held the sent value does not move | medium |
| Machine Hours of 168 h or more | not clamped; the 500-row chunk rolls back on `chk_orders_run_time_bounds`; earlier chunks stay committed; one generic HTTP 400, no row named (`db.py:3887-3892`, `schema.sql:117-121`) | the 168 h bound also caps the longest backward walk; per-row handling is an owner decision (OQ28) | high |

Worked example (GAP01 simulation). Routing-off plant, machine open Mon to Fri 08:00-20:00, Order placed Mon 19 Oct 08:00 to 12:00 (run time 4 h) and sent. The file now says Machine Hours 6 and no finish. Today: run time 6, ingest invents the due date as Mon 08:00 plus 6 = Mon 14:00 (the due date moved with the run time), the stored end Mon 12:00 is ignored, the bar becomes Mon 08:00-14:00, lateness 0, and the next Send moves the finish SAP holds from Mon 12:00 to Mon 14:00. With the finish held: finish Mon 12:00, start derived backward under a splitting policy as Fri 16 Oct 18:00 (pieces Fri 18:00-20:00 and Mon 08:00-12:00); under `never` no 6 h contiguous slot ends at 12:00, so the held finish is infeasible (4.2.3). If now were Fri 19:00 the walk would reverse.

**The second blocker-class item: derived due dates (GAP01-6).** For rows whose Excel finish is blank, date-only or not after the start, the stored due date **is** start plus the new run time at every ingest (`db.py:3982-3988`, `4005-4012`), so holding it re-creates start anchoring; holding the as-sent baseline fails because it is NULL (pinned `test_ingest_data_layer.py:1000-1009`) or a bare date; the old stored finish, end of the date-only day, or start-anchoring for these rows is an owner decision (OQ24). GAP01 rated this item high; it is treated as blocker-class here because O4 cannot be honoured for these rows without an owner rule. Whether real Excel exports carry finish times is not answerable from the repo **[unverified: depends on the real export]**. Whether SAP reschedules its own start when Machine Hours change is likewise unknown **[unverified: SAP-side fact]**.

#### 4.5.12 Production-version validity flips on an echo (GAP02)

Validity is judged on the raw SAP start column everywhere (`resolver.py:277`; save path reads the same column, `db.py:1295`, `1322`, `1444`, passed to `check_eligibility` whose parameter is merely named `sap_basic_start_date`; the client reads the raw start, `runtime-client.mts:192`). Design decision D8 says a drag cannot change validity, and that holds for drags. It fails for Send: the echo overwrites the start with SAP's back-scheduled value (`db.py:2828`), the finish echo suppresses the reset, and the resolver then re-judges the order on the new start (`resolver.py:575`; `db.py:3813-3817`).

Worked example (GAP02 simulation A). Version valid to Mon 19 Oct. Order Z starts Mon 19 Oct 06:00 and is valid; the planner places and firms it, then Sends. SAP back-schedules its start to Tue 20 Oct 14:00. The echo raises no reset. The resolver finds the version expired, holds the order and clears its slot, firm and pieces (`resolver.py:764-778`): sending a finish destroyed the placement. Reverse direction (simulation B): expired to valid silently changes the run time with no flag. Both happen today; the new rule makes the start a function of the planner's finish, which is what D8 tried to prevent. Options for the anchor (SAP start as received once; due date; placed finish; derived start is circular and was rejected by D8; current start flips on echo) are tabulated in GAP02; which date SAP itself uses to select a version is a question for SAP Development **[unverified: SAP-side fact]**. A running order's run time can also be rewritten by an echo with no running protection (variant A2). No test pins the echo-then-resolve flip. Severity high.

#### 4.5.13 Distribution false reset (GAP03, pre-existing)

Three routes put a non-SAP value into a child's as-sent finish baseline: re-weight, reset, reapply-defaults and repair rebuild children from the header's post-hygiene finish (`distribution/data.py:2696`, `785`, `1510`, `1376`); `_resolve_wc_codes` copies the plain order's possibly client-rewritten finish (`3656`) and deletes the true baseline and the sent row with the plain order (cascade); a concurrent re-weight rebuilds the ingest's own child rows without the as-sent key (`1296`, `1776`). The next upload then raises "dates" for the children and resets all siblings (not running orders, not orders with a matching remembered finish), although SAP sent nothing new. Timed finishes are unaffected; date-only, missing, not-after-start or client-rewritten ones are affected.

Worked example (GAP03 SIM-2). Date-only finish Fri 23 Oct, start Mon 19 Oct 06:00, run time defaulted 1 h. Header finish Mon 07:00, children baseline Fri 23 Oct 00:00. After a re-weight the baseline becomes Mon 07:00; the next unchanged snapshot sends Fri 23 Oct 00:00, `dates_differ` is true, no echo, so every child's slot is wiped once; the upload heals the baseline. Retiring the client rewrite does not remove this defect; the fallback at `distribution/data.py:1510` must go too, and the child upsert must not carry the due column on re-weight (`1355`). One bad child resets every sibling because dates have no parent-level judgement (`db.py:3631-3633`, `3644-3647`). Severity high (exposure exists before any rule change). Whether a header-level date judgement is wanted is OQ29.

#### 4.5.14 Purge selector, dead diagnostics, audit visibility (GAP12)

- Purge selector `COALESCE(scheduled_end, basic_finish_date)` (`db.py:1829`) becomes the date the board shows once the stored end is the placed finish. At an identity-preserving cutover the selection for run-time-set orders whose stored end differed can change between the day before and the day after. `planner_overridden` counts planner starts (`db.py:1850`) and under-warns if the start stops being stored. Pinned keep: `tests/test_integration_pg.py:632-731`.
- Purge preview and delete send different range ends: the preview sends a date only (midnight), the delete sends `T23:59:59` (`frontend/admin-ops/admin-ui.mts:1308-1318` versus `1534`), so the confirm count excludes the last chosen day after midnight; pre-existing, unpinned; placed finishes at window edges concentrate the effect (OQ45). Severity medium.
- The counters "dropped for no start" and "dropped, no finish filled" are declared and displayed but **nothing has ever incremented them** (`backend/admin_ops/diagnostics_state.py:30-31`; display `admin-ui.mts:783`, `894`, `968`). Their names invert under the new rule. Per-upload counts (rows dropped for no finish, derived starts, repaired finishes, reversals) belong in the per-batch warnings list, which the Excel Uploads card already renders (`db.py:3847-3877`, `admin-ui.mts:2657`, `2698-2703`); the SAP History tab shows only distribution warnings (`sap-interface-ui.mts:1511-1515`). The unparseable-date warning is effectively dead on Excel and staging paths (`db.py:3441-3442`). Deep stats: null counts and the date minimum flip meaning, the maximum already prefers the stored end (`db.py:2180-2189`). All display or admin tooling; none corrupts a schedule.
- Any new derived-start column built with timedelta arithmetic inside the hygiene frame needs the same data-type cast as `fcf041b` (`db.py:3988`, `4012`) or it re-opens the 500 on that pandas version.

#### 4.5.15 Duplicate-id sequencing rule (GAP13-7)

Rows of one order-and-material pair get plain and numbered ids in the order (start missing last, start, quantity, work center) of the as-sent SAP start (`db.py:3468-3482`). The id base does not change with a finish anchor. It would flip (a) if the tie-break were re-keyed to finish, or (b) if a missing start were derived from the finish **before** the sort: derived starts vary with run time and calendar, so a re-upload after a run-time or hours change would reorder the group and move the plain id between rows, silently swapping planner state. Rule: keep the tie-break on the raw as-sent start where present; for rows with no sent start use (finish, quantity, work center); derive after id assignment.

### 4.6 Due-date baseline retirement

#### 4.6.1 What the 2026-07 rewrite protected against

Commit `db4153c` (2026-07-06) added the relay (`POST /tasks/baseline-correct` to `db.correct_due_date_baselines`) because the due date "used to only exist correctly in memory between an order's ingest and its first save; every reload after that re-derived it from the DB's raw, never-updated" column. Commit `71b2233` (same day) states the cause: the old hygiene hardcoded a bad finish to start plus 1 h, "leaving 609/709 live orders stuck on a meaningless ~1am due time (and consequently flagged late)".

So the problem was not "SAP finishes that equal start plus run time". The ingest had thrown away SAP's due date (missing, not after the start, or exact-midnight finishes become start plus run time) and the client "repaired" the fabricated value by replacing it with the end of the start day's working window. The real finish survived only in `sap_basic_finish_date`, which the client never sees. Under O4 the raw-shape problem disappears for new rows if hygiene stops fabricating; a finish that equals start plus run time is then simply the due date. What the rewrite met by accident and still needs an answer: a date-only SAP finish arrives as midnight, which would read as due at the **start** of the due day, so a time-of-day interpretation applied where lateness is computed is required (OQ23).

How the rewrite behaves today (WS07, VERIFY-WS02c-4): it runs for every non-queued task with a machine and a raw start, gated only by "looks raw" (due missing, or equal to start, start plus run time, or start plus 1 h; `persistence.mts:1051-1054`), with no firmed, placed or moved guard. The new value is the close of the working window of the order's **start** day (`1077-1078`), not of the SAP finish day, so for a 20 h order it makes the due date earlier than SAP's own finish. It is relayed only after calendar hydration (`calendar-sync.mts:250-266`; the earlier pre-hydration call discards the result, `persistence.mts:578`); the server accepts it only when the row version matches and the stored finish still has a raw shape (`db.py:1753-1774`), otherwise a silent no-op. Queued orders are filtered out (`persistence.mts:916`) and keep the fabricated due forever.

The route has no admin-audit entry and requires only authentication, so any logged-in role, including a view-only one, triggers `UPDATE orders` at first load (500 rows per request), bumping xmin; removal also removes that unaudited write and xmin churn (WS07-8).

**Sequencing constraint (ADJ-WS15-R12):** the migration runs before the image roll and there is no server build-id gate, so a stale browser tab can still call the route after cutover. Neutralising the route in the same image as the cutover closes the stale-tab hazard (rows the migration touched are xmin-pinned no-ops by accident, not design); no earlier roll is required. In addition the local cache restore of the due date (`persistence.mts:890-891`) can mask a fresh server due date and must go; `/tasks/refresh` does not carry the due date at all (`db.py:839-849`, `models.py:170-194`, `persistence.mts:1731-1737`), so an open session would never learn a SAP-side change until a full reload; add it.

#### 4.6.3 Raw-shape consequences, with numbers

Calendar for both examples: Mon to Fri 06:00-22:00.

- **Date-only finish** (start Mon 19 Oct 00:00, finish Wed 21 Oct 00:00, run time 10 h, pull limit 1 day, push 0). Today: due date Mon 10:00 (hygiene), then Mon 22:00 (client rewrite). If the planner moves the bar to end Tue 20:00, lateness is 22 h although SAP's due was Wednesday; the planning window is floor Sun 18 Oct 00:00, ceiling Tue 20 Oct 00:00, so the bar is over the cap. Under the new rule (due as received, Wed 00:00): lateness 0; floor Tue 20 Oct 00:00, ceiling Thu 22 Oct 00:00. Side effect: Monday is now before the floor, so a pull-limited plant can no longer place this order on Monday.
- **Genuine finish equal to start plus run time** (start Mon 06:00, finish Tue 20 Oct 02:00, run time 20 h, push 0). Today the client treats it as raw and rewrites the due date to Mon 22:00 (4 h earlier than SAP's) and persists it; an order ending Tue 02:00 is 4 h late and 2 h over the cap. Under the new rule: due Tue 02:00, lateness 0, ceiling Wed 00:00.
- Echo coincidence: after case (c) of 4.5.1 the stored finish (Thu 12:00) equals start (Wed 16:00) plus 20 h, so the client heuristic would also be allowed to rewrite a genuine placed finish (WS06-14).
- Readers whose numbers move: lateness (`foundation.mts:641-647`, `696-707`), the late tile and lateness matrix (`insights-ui.mts:393`, `967-980`, `1087-1101`), the Late filter (`orders.mts:764`), optimizer windows (`engine.mts:1092`, `1118`, `1156`; `setup-scheduler.mts:6217-6229`), and sequencing in due-date mode: today all orders starting the same day share one end-of-shift due stamp so ties fall to policy and id; with as-sent dues ties break on real finishes (`setup-scheduler.mts:1196-1199` and its comparators). Windows use only the due date's calendar day, lateness the full timestamp (WS07-15). A queued order is measured against now, so a missing due is its only "not late" path (`foundation.mts:642`).
- Legacy rows: the as-sent finish is recoverable from `sap_basic_finish_date` where non-NULL; whether to repair them is an owner decision (OQ30). Profiling SQL (WS07 section 8) sizes fabricated and echo-contaminated dues.
- **If SAP's planned-order finish is not the customer due date.** Every reader that says "late" reads this one date (the late tile, the lateness matrix, the Late filter, optimizer planning windows and due-date sequencing, listed above) and O4 makes it permanent. In SAP a planned order's finish can be the date the planning run needs the material, not the customer's date **[unverified: needs SAP Development]**. Three consequences if so. An order SAP's own planning run could not place on time (its reversal pushed the finish later than the requirement) already has a finish later than the real need, and NIMBUS reads it as on time (lateness 0). An order whose finish SAP set earlier than the customer date to cover goods-receipt processing time reads as earlier than it needs to be (the Material Plant export carries that processing time in a staging-only column, `docs/SAP_STAGING_DESIGN.md:159`). And every "late" figure measures "late against SAP's plan", not "late to the customer"; the UI term "due date" (OQ43) would promise more than the data holds, and "planned finish (SAP)" would not. The fields that could answer the question already reach the staging table and nothing reads them: sales order, commitment date and committed quantity (`docs/SAP_STAGING_DESIGN.md:161`; a search of the Python, TypeScript and SQL finds them only in the schema files). Profile P5, read-only, on the latest applied planned-order batch per plant (staging keeps one batch per plant, design D11):

```sql
-- P5: for planned orders that carry a sales order, how does SAP's finish date compare with the commitment date?
-- Dates are raw text YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD; compare the first eight digits.
SELECT b.plant,
       count(*) AS rows_with_sales_order_and_commitment_date,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE left(replace(r.pedtr, '-', ''), 8) =  left(replace(r.gsbtr, '-', ''), 8)) AS finish_equals_commitment_date,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE left(replace(r.pedtr, '-', ''), 8) <  left(replace(r.gsbtr, '-', ''), 8)) AS finish_before_commitment_date,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE left(replace(r.pedtr, '-', ''), 8) >  left(replace(r.gsbtr, '-', ''), 8)) AS finish_after_commitment_date
  FROM sap_stage_planned_order r
  JOIN sap_stage_batch b ON b.batch_id = r.batch_id
 WHERE b.object_key = 'stage_planned_orders' AND b.status = 'applied'
   AND NULLIF(btrim(r.kdauf), '') IS NOT NULL
   AND replace(coalesce(r.gsbtr, ''), '-', '') NOT IN ('', '00000000')
 GROUP BY b.plant ORDER BY b.plant;
```
What the owner would read: a high share of "equals" supports treating the finish as the customer date; a large "after" share means NIMBUS shows as on time orders SAP itself plans late for a customer. What the commitment date means in SAP is itself a question for SAP Development (Appendix D, D.1 item 10).

#### 4.6.4 `impliedOriginalStart`

Today the helper returns due minus run time in elapsed hours (`foundation.mts:632-638`); readers are the Original Start column (`orders.mts:543`), the Inspector row (`2124`, `2213-2214`) and the variance badge (`2396`, current start minus the implied start); no test references it; locale keys exist in five locales. Under a calendar-aware backward walk the identity "badge equals finish minus due" no longer holds. Order Z with placed finish equal to due Wed 18:00: derived start Tue 14:00, implied original start Tue 22:00, badge shows 8 hours "early" although the order finishes exactly on time; the column shows the minute the line closes. Options raised: delete it (three call sites, one catalog entry, locale keys; the raw `original_start_date` itself must stay, it feeds `_overlayUserMoves`, the placement-snap guard and production-version validity); replace the badge with placed finish minus due; replace the column with the raw SAP start or with a calendar-aware latest start that meets the due date (needs a backward helper). The workstream's lean is to retire it, keep Original End and show finish variance; this is an option, not a ruling (OQ16).

### 4.7 Distribution (aggregate work-center orders and their sub-orders)

**What this area is.** SAP plans one aggregate order for a work center; NIMBUS splits it into per-machine sub-orders ("children", ids like `A-1000`) with percentage shares. The aggregate itself has no order row once split; it survives only as a header record (`order_distribution`). Everything below is read against HEAD `757dd86`.

**Headline.** Distribution is where the new rule changes the most visible numbers and where an existing defect (a false "SAP changed the dates" reset) sits underneath the project. Today every child of one aggregate starts together at SAP's start and ends apart (each child's bar is its own share of the hours). Under Reading A the natural default flips: every child ends together at the due date and starts apart. Nothing in the schema or the code requires either shape, so this is a default, not an invariant, and it is the subject of OQ11.

#### Impact table

| Surface | Today | Under Reading A | Severity | Anchors | Tests that pin it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| New children copy the aggregate's dates | both SAP start and SAP finish copied to every child; only run time is apportioned | the copied finish is already the due date (correct under O4). A placed finish does not exist yet and nothing is named to write it: the server has no calendar, so at ingest it could write a finish with no start, which is exactly the hybrid row the server predicates misclassify (4.7.10). The "children hold the parent's finish" default is therefore a decision (OQ58), not a given | high | `backend/distribution/data.py:784-786`; `db.py:553`, `559` | `tests/test_distribution.py` ingest fixtures |
| Unplaced children | no stored schedule; shown window = SAP start + own run time (start-aligned, ends spread) | must be given a placed finish and a derived start, which needs a calendar walk the server does not have; the read-time fallbacks disagree across the document (due date in 4.1.2 and 7.4, start plus run time in OQ33 option B and 6.2, neither in 6.1, browser snap in 8.3) until OQ33 and OQ58 are decided | high | `data.py:1419-1423`; `db.py:212-217` | distribution fixtures |
