#### 4.7.1 The parent-to-child date-flow table

The aggregate order is never an order row; its dates live on the header and are copied down. "Anchor today" is the edge the code holds; "Under A" is what must flip.

| # | Event | Child dates written, and from what | Anchor today | Under A |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | First ingest of an aggregate | every child's SAP start and finish := the aggregate's; run time := its share (apportioned in whole minutes); no planner dates; as-sent finish baseline := what SAP sent | start | the copied finish is the due date, but nobody writes a placed finish or a derived start at ingest (4.7.10): until the owner decides who does (OQ58), children keep no stored dates and the read rule for an unplaced row applies (OQ33). Two populations then coexist (section 4.7.9) |
| 2 | 1 to N anchor carry | child start := the plain order's start; child end := that start + own hours (raw elapsed time) | start | read the plain order's finish; store a calendar-aware finish, not start + hours |
| 3 | Re-weight (planner) | kept children: no date written, run time changes. New child: earliest sibling's start | start held | finish held, start re-derives; new child takes the common finish |
| 4 | Reset or reapply defaults | same engine as 3 | start held | same as 3 |
| 5 | Repair | same engine as 3 (never revives purged shares) | start held | same as 3 |
| 6 | N to 1 collapse | survivor takes the old child's start and end verbatim, plus firm, notes, planning state, production version; segments re-pointed | start | see 4.7.8 |
| 7 | Drag, keyboard, grid start edit | that child's start and end only | start | that child's finish only |
| 8 | Routing run-time change | run time only; the mismatch flag is set only at plant cutover | start held | start must re-derive for every child whose run time moved |
| 9 | SAP changes the aggregate dates | siblings: planner dates cleared, segments deleted, firm cleared, fallback to SAP start; running ones spared | start | reset siblings read as never placed (SAP start plus run time, nothing sent until placed; 6.2, OQ33 B1); spared sibling diverges |
| 10 | SAP changes the quantity | same reset when the total changed | start | same as 9 |
| 11 | Send to SAP | no dates written; side table only | latest end | see 4.7.5 |
| 12 | Aggregate read | none (read) | min start, max end | both flip |
| 13 | Resolve by machine or work-center code | machine: no date write; work-center codes: row 2 | start | row 2 |

Anchors: rows 1-6, 13 `backend/distribution/data.py:691-803`, `806-919`, `1326-1418`, `1477-1518`, `2802-2866`, `3052-3299`, `3625-3800`; row 7 `engine.mts:1208-1245`; rows 8-10 `backend/routing/resolver.py:673-679`, `db.py:3640-3672`; row 11 `sap_staging.py:2161-2287`; row 12 `data.py:2421-2518`.

**One vocabulary trap.** In the engine's reconcile function the word "parent" means the order versus its own split segments, not the distribution aggregate. Nothing in the optimizer or reconcile code reads a sibling or the aggregate when it places a child (`engine.mts:1259-1261`); the only distribution-specific guard on a drag is the machine lock (`db.py:1196-1199`).

#### 4.7.2 Siblings are start-aligned by construction

The ingest writes children with no planner dates (`data.py:1419-1423`), so each child shows SAP start + its own run time. Two children of 6 h and 8 h end 2 h apart and both end days before the due date. Nothing polices alignment except an after-the-fact alert that buckets by start. Dragging one child changes only that child (no sibling coupling anywhere, `engine.mts` has `PARENT_ORDER` branches only for alert scoping), so a shared finish under A is a default (read at display time and written on first placement, OQ58), never an enforced rule. When shares are equal and the work-center rate is the same, run times are equal and the two readings give identical bars; the readings differ only for asymmetric shares (60/40) or hand-typed hours.

#### 4.7.3 The 60/40 simulation: today versus a shared finish

Inputs (illustrative, not real data): aggregate quantity 1000, SAP start Mon 2026-10-19 06:00, SAP finish (the due date) Fri 2026-10-23 16:00. Shares 60/40 give C1 = 600 units, C2 = 400. For comparability with the earlier workstream tables C1 runs 6.0 h and C2 8.0 h. Caution: the code reaches unequal per-unit rates only through hand-typed run times or children on different routing work centers; placeholder run time is weight-proportional and routing run time uses one work-center rate for all siblings. Calendar: Mon-Fri 06:00-22:00, no blackouts, no setup, nothing running.

| Step | Today: C1 | Today: C2 | Today: aggregate read / what Send to SAP carries | Under A: C1 | Under A: C2 | Under A: aggregate read / Send |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| After first ingest (60/40, unplaced) | Mon 06:00-12:00 | Mon 06:00-14:00 | Mon 06:00 to **Mon 14:00** | Fri 10:00-16:00 | Fri 08:00-16:00 | Fri 08:00 to **Fri 16:00** (= due date) |
| Planner re-weights to 50/50 (C1 5 h, C2 10 h) | Mon 06:00-11:00 | Mon 06:00-16:00 | **Mon 16:00** (SAP's finish moved +2 h) | Fri 11:00-16:00 | Fri 06:00-16:00 | **Fri 16:00** (unchanged) |
| Planner drags C2 so that it sits Wed 08:00-18:00 | Mon 06:00-11:00 | Wed 08:00-18:00 | **Wed 18:00** | Fri 11:00-16:00 | Wed 08:00-18:00 | **Fri 16:00** (C1 is still the latest) |

What the owner should take from the table. Today, before any planner action, the first Send to SAP reports Mon 14:00 against SAP's own Fri 16:00 finish: NIMBUS compresses the aggregate's finish by four days and then moves it with every re-weight and every drag of the latest child. The "Under A" columns show what the owner wants ("the finish sent to SAP never moves") for share changes, **in the narrow case where the following all hold**; each condition is a separate way the finish moves:

1. **Somebody writes the shared finish.** Nothing does today (4.7.10). Without a writer the children are unplaced and Send behaviour is whatever OQ33 decides (its recommendation: unplaced rows send nothing).
2. **No reversal (O2).** If a child's derived start falls before now, it is placed forward from now and its finish is later than the due date (variant "Reversal" below): the roll-up follows the later finish.
3. **No infeasible finish (OQ13).** Under `never` and `overlong_only` a held finish may have no contiguous slot; the recommended answer moves the finish earlier, so Send reports an earlier value.
4. **No collapse to one child (OQ37).** Rule R2 carries "the end the planner sees today", which is start plus the full run time and so can differ from the finish SAP last saw (4.7.8).
5. **At least one sibling still ends at the held finish.** Send reports the latest end among the placed children (`backend/integration/sap_staging.py:2188-2189`), not the due date. A family whose latest child was dragged earlier reports that earlier finish; so does a family where a re-weight left only an earlier-ending sibling placed. The roll-up equals the due date only while some placed child sits at it.
6. **"Common finish" has a meaning.** When siblings already end at different times (after a drag, after a spared running sibling, after a cutover of an old spread family), "the common sibling finish" used for a new child (4.7.4 item 3, 4.7.1 row 3) is undefined: latest, earliest and the due date are three different answers. Example (illustrative): C1 ends Fri 16:00 and C2 was dragged to end Wed 18:00; a re-weight adds a third child C3. Latest gives Fri 16:00, earliest gives Wed 18:00, the due date gives Fri 16:00. Which one is OQ11's and OQ58's to settle; the document's lead recommendation for OQ11 ("a default, not an enforced rule") does not say.

Variants on the same inputs, one change each:

- **Spill across a day boundary.** Take the 30/70 split (C1 holds 300 units = 3.0 h; C2 holds 700 units = 14.0 h, at the example's 50 units per hour for C2; the 4.7.3 caution above explains why the rates differ). Walking back from Fri 16:00: Fri 06:00-16:00 yields 10 h, the remaining 4 h come from Thu 22:00 backward, so C2's start is **Thu 18:00**; C1 is Fri 13:00-16:00. The finish is equal but the start sits on a different day, so the start-bucket separation alert fires (4.7.9). (The first edition called the 700-unit child "C2 at 70/30"; at a 70/30 split the 70 percent child is C1, so the 30/70 labelling keeps C2 as the long child.)
- **Reversal (O2).** If "now" is Fri 10:00, C2's derived start (Fri 06:00) is in the past, so it is placed forward from now: Fri 10:00-20:00, 4 h after the due date. C1 (Fri 11:00-16:00) is unaffected. The aggregate roll-up becomes Fri 20:00 and SAP is told the later finish.
- **Drop on a closed edge.** Dropping C2 so its end reads Thu 06:00 gives a stored end of Thu 06:00 today (raw, no calendar); under A the bar is walked back through Wed 06:00-22:00 and visibly jumps left on release (start-anchored versus finish-anchored drag is OQ1, owned by the manual-placement section).

**Equal-rate case (what the code does by default).** The code gives every child the same per-unit rate: run time is weight-proportional (`backend/distribution/data.py:733-736`, `776`), and the design document's own assumption is "assume equal for now" (`aggregate_to_detail.md:658`). So at 60/40 the **60 percent child runs longer**, the opposite of the table above (which uses 100 and 50 units per hour only so that its numbers stay comparable with the earlier workstream tables). Same inputs, equal rates, total run time 14.0 h (illustrative):

| Step | Today: C1 / C2 / what Send carries | Under A (a writer exists): C1 / C2 / Send |
|---|---|---|
| After first ingest, 60/40 (C1 8.4 h, C2 5.6 h) | Mon 06:00-14:24 / Mon 06:00-11:36 / **Mon 14:24** | Fri 07:36-16:00 / Fri 10:24-16:00 / **Fri 16:00** |
| Re-weight to 50/50 (7.0 h each) | Mon 06:00-13:00 / Mon 06:00-13:00 / **Mon 13:00** (moved 1.4 h earlier) | Fri 09:00-16:00 each / **Fri 16:00** (unchanged) |
| Spill threshold | n/a | a spill needs one child above 10 h (the hours between Fri 06:00 and the 16:00 finish): 70/30 gives C1 9.8 h (Fri 06:12-16:00, no spill); 80/20 gives C1 11.2 h, start **Thu 20:48** (1.2 h taken from Thu 22:00 backward) |

At equal rates a symmetric 50/50 family never spills and never trips the separation alert; only asymmetric shares do, which bounds how often the alert misfire in 4.7.9 shows up.

**The same example with a date-only finish.** Both sample workbooks carry only date-only SAP dates (8.11: every one of 593 and 328 finishes is a bare date at midnight; the second workbook's start is also midnight and equals the finish for all 328 rows). The timed Fri 16:00 finish used above does not occur in either sample, and the shared-finish default, the Send value and the derived starts are undefined for a date-only finish: OQ23's reading ("end of that date's working window") is stated for where lateness is computed, not for placement. Illustrative inputs: SAP start Mon 2026-10-19 and finish Fri 2026-10-23, both date-only (stored as midnight); calendar Mon-Fri 06:00-22:00; shares 60/40 at the table's rates (C1 6.0 h, C2 8.0 h); nothing running; "now" before Mon.

| Reading of the shared finish | Finish written | C1 / C2 derived start | Aggregate read | Send value | What the planner sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Today (hygiene turns a midnight finish into start plus run time; nothing placed) | none; header finish = Mon 00:00 + 14 h = Mon 14:00 | Mon 00:00-06:00 / Mon 00:00-08:00 (raw, drawn before the plant opens; the browser's snap redraws from Mon 06:00, display only) | Mon 00:00 to Mon 08:00 | **Mon 08:00** (88 hours before SAP's date, Fri 23 Oct 00:00) | bars on Monday morning |
| (a) Literal midnight, as received | Fri 23 Oct 00:00 | the walk back starts at the last open minute before a closed instant, Thu 22:00: C1 **Thu 16:00**, C2 **Thu 14:00** | Thu 14:00 to Fri 00:00 (the bars' envelopes end in closed time) | Fri 00:00 (equals what SAP sent, so a first Send changes nothing) | every child lands the day before SAP's date |
| (b) End of that date's working window (OQ23's reading applied to placement) | Fri 22:00 | C1 **Fri 16:00**, C2 **Fri 14:00** | Fri 14:00 to Fri 22:00 | Fri 22:00 (22 h later than SAP's date-only value; the date-only echo clause treats an echo on the same date as an echo, `db.py:2655-2659`) | bars on the due date |

A re-weight to 50/50 leaves Send unchanged in (a) and (b) once a writer exists, as in the timed case. The second workbook's shape (finish equal to start at midnight) is the harsher case under (a): a literal midnight finish on Mon 19 Oct walks back from a closed instant to **Fri 16 Oct 22:00**, so C1 would sit Fri 16 Oct 16:00-22:00 and C2 Fri 14:00-22:00, both before SAP's own start; if that is before now, O2 places them forward from now instead. Which of (a), (b) or the hygiene alternatives of OQ24 applies is the owner's choice (OQ23 for the time of day, OQ58 for the shared-finish default and who writes it). Whether the pilot feed carries real times for planned orders is not answerable from the repository, and the two workbooks are manual extracts (the COOIS file is a production-order list dated 2026-08-17, 8.11) **[unverified: depends on the real feed]**.

#### 4.7.4 Share change becomes a derived start

Path today: re-weight, reset and repair rebuild the children from the header, apportion minutes by weight, and call the routing resolver for the plant, which writes run time only. The client then re-places any child flagged "run time changed" from that child's own start. Three facts matter for A:

1. **The trigger is incomplete.** The flag is set only for a placed child whose run time changed, or for a segmented child. A routing-source child keeps its old run time inside the upsert (so no change is seen), the resolver then rewrites it, and the flag is set only at plant cutover. For an unsegmented child the bar end silently changes on the server and nothing re-fits it. Under A every child whose run time moved needs its start re-derived, including never-placed children, so the trigger must be widened or replaced (cross-check the run-time section). `[unverified: traced statically, not run; INFERENCE]`.
2. **The reconcile function is blind to siblings and anchors on the child's own start** (`engine.mts:1259-1261`). It must walk back from the child's finish and is then the single place a share change re-derives a start. The pane's "resized" banner compares start or end (`distribution-pane.mts:1430-1436`) and would fire on every re-derived start with copy that says "resized".
3. **A new child anchors on the earliest sibling's start** (`data.py:2802-2824`) and is created already "scheduled" even when no sibling is placed. Under A the anchor is the common finish (latest or shared sibling finish, else the due date).
4. **The dry-run preview shows hours, not bars.** The preview a planner approves before a share change carries, per machine, the quantity and hours before and after, the outcome (new, removed, resized, unchanged), the effective percentage and the `scheduled`, `frozen` and below-minimum-lot flags (`backend/distribution/data.py:3147-3152`). It carries no derived start, finish or overlap, because the server has no calendar and the derivation happens only in the browser afterwards. So the planner approves "C2 grows from 5.6 h to 7.0 h" without seeing that C2's bar will grow left across a weekend or overlap its neighbour. Whether the pane should compute the derived bars client-side from the plan's hours before the planner confirms is an open design point (it can reuse the reconcile function).
5. **The reconcile ignores firm.** The reconcile that implements "run time changed" states that "Firmed is parent-level only and does not suppress this required runtime correction" (`frontend/optimization/engine.mts:1247-1251`). With a held finish, a firmed child whose share grows has its start re-derived leftward, possibly into the frozen window, with no protection and no prompt; OQ4's recommendation ("the firm protects the placed finish") covers the finish, not this start movement.
6. **The re-derived start exists only in the browser until "Save schedule".** The reconcile writes through `Store.updateMany(..., 'engine-runtime-reconcile')` (`engine.mts:1274`) and pushes nothing on the undo stack; until a planner saves, the server, the aggregate read and Send still use the old stored values, and a second tab or an admin sweep sees the stale ones.
7. **Server-only writers have no browser.** `reapply-defaults` and `resolve` run on the server for an admin with no planner session (`backend/distribution/CLAUDE.md`, the two admin-write routes), so nothing re-derives the starts of the children they rewrite. The next browser that loads the flagged rows re-derives them (`engine.mts:2777-2791`), and whichever tab saves first wins. This is the same question as "who re-derives a stored start" (OQ51).

#### 4.7.5 The outbound roll-up (Send to SAP)

Send groups children by aggregate and material, sends the latest child end plus the production version and firm flag, and every sent child remembers the group value as its "sent finish" (`sap_staging.py:2188-2189`, `2256`).

| Family state | What Send reports | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Untouched, shared finish (new under A) | the due date; Send is idempotent | SAP sees no change |
| Share change on a shared-finish family | unchanged | re-weights no longer move SAP's finish |
| One child dragged | the latest child's finish; moving an earlier-than-latest child is invisible to SAP | the maximum is the "slowest sibling" |
| Reversal (a late child) | the later finish | SAP is told the lateness |
| Running sibling spared by an SAP-change reset (4.7.8) | the due date; the spared child's own finish is hidden by the maximum | SAP stops seeing the running child's end (today it sees it) |
| Never-placed or queued child | skipped; a partly placed aggregate reports its placed members only | unchanged limitation |
| Old family cut over by identity (4.7.9) | nothing while its children are never placed (OQ33 B1); once a child is placed, the compressed finish (e.g. Mon 14:00 against a Fri 16:00 due date) | today's bars continue for old families |
| Frozen entry by the longest child (firm roll-up) | the group's firm flag is `X` when **any** placed child qualifies: a manual firm, SAP already firmed, or a derived start inside the frozen window (`backend/integration/sap_staging.py:2190-2191`, `2148-2158`) | under shared finishes the starts differ by design, so only the longest child may start inside the window, and the whole aggregate is firmed in SAP; the flag is add-only (an existing `X` always stays `X`) and the planner never firmed it |
| Reversal or infeasible finish (a child's finish later or earlier than the due date) | the later (or, for an infeasible finish, earlier) maximum | the "re-weights cannot move it" statement fails here (4.7.3 conditions 2 and 3) |
| Siblings with different finishes | the latest placed child end | the roll-up equals the due date only while some placed child sits at it; "the common sibling finish" is undefined (4.7.3 condition 6) |

Two defects are visible here. First, the aggregate read route and Send use two different end expressions (the plain one versus the one that returns the stored end while the mismatch flag is set), so one flagged child makes them disagree for the same aggregate (`data.py:2455-2458` versus `sap_staging.py:2211`). Second, SAP's echo of NIMBUS's own roll-up rewrites each child's due date and as-sent baseline unless ingest stops treating an echo as a new due date (4.7.6). Both collapse onto the single end expression the server section decides.

**The firm flag Send transmits is decided per aggregate by its earliest child.** Example (illustrative): frozen horizon 2 days, now Mon 19 Oct 12:00, so the frozen window ends Wed 21 Oct 12:00; calendar Mon-Fri 06:00-22:00; a family due Wed 21 Oct 16:00 with C1 14 h and C2 4 h. Walking back from Wed 16:00, C2 starts Wed 12:00 (not before the window end, so not frozen), and C1 starts Tue 18:00 (Wed 06:00-16:00 gives 10 h; the other 4 h come from Tue 22:00 back), which is inside the window. C1 alone qualifies, so the roll-up row is sent firm, SAP stops regenerating that planned order, and nobody in NIMBUS firmed anything. Today every child starts at SAP's start, so all children cross the frozen window together. Under OQ27's recommendation (frozen on the stored derived start) this is an intended behaviour; the point added here is that SAP-side firming is irreversible from NIMBUS and changes SAP's weekly regeneration of that order (`aggregate_to_detail.md:414, 475`), so it is a consequence the owner should accept knowingly, for single orders and for aggregates alike. It is the aggregate case of OQ54. Severity: medium on its own (blocker 4 already names the single-order form).

**Corrections to the "Under A" column of the roll-up table above.** Read the first two rows ("Untouched, shared finish: the due date" and "Share change: unchanged") as holding only under the five conditions of 4.7.3; the table's other rows already show how a drag or a reversal moves the roll-up.

#### 4.7.6 What can corrupt a child's baseline today, and the false-reset bug

Each child stores two copies of SAP's finish: the due date (wire name "original end date") and the as-sent baseline used to decide whether SAP changed anything. The next upload compares the incoming SAP finish with that baseline; a difference, unless NIMBUS remembers having sent that exact finish, wipes the planner's work on the child and on **every sibling** (slot, firm, segments), except a running one.

**This is today's bug, not a Reading A effect.** Three NIMBUS writes can put a non-SAP value into a child's baseline:

| Route | What is written | When it matters |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Re-weight, reset, reapply defaults, repair | the header's post-hygiene finish becomes the baseline (`data.py:2696` to `785` to `1510` to `1376`); the same statement also reverts the due column to the header copy (`1355`), undoing the client's due-date rewrite | whenever the header finish differs from what SAP sent: a date-only, missing or not-after-start finish, or one the client rewrote |
| (b) Resolve by work-center code | the plain order's due column (possibly the client's end-of-shift value) becomes the header finish and each child's due date and baseline; the plain order, with its true baseline and its "sent" memory, is deleted (`data.py:3656`, `1510`, `834`) | plants that configure a work center after its orders arrived |
| (c) Concurrent re-weight during an upload | the replan rebuilds the ingest's own child rows without the as-sent value (`data.py:1776`, `1296`) | race only (low) |

Worked example (illustrative): SAP sends the aggregate with finish Fri 23 Oct 00:00 (date only) and start Mon 19 Oct 06:00. Ingest hygiene replaces the stored finish with start + 1 h = Mon 07:00; the children's as-sent baseline holds Fri 00:00. The planner schedules both children and re-weights 60/40 to 25/75. The re-weight writes the header finish (Mon 07:00) into both baselines. SAP, still unchanged, sends Fri 23 Oct again on the next upload; the comparison reads Fri 00:00 against Mon 07:00, reports "dates changed", and both children plus all siblings lose their slots. The upload heals the baseline, so the damage is one wiped schedule per distribution write, and it never fires for timed finishes. If NIMBUS had Sent the children before the re-weight, the remembered sent finish vetoes the reset. No test pins any of this. How common it is depends on how many SAP finishes are date-only, and section 8.11 shows both sample workbooks carry date-only finishes in 100 percent of their rows (593 of 593 and 328 of 328). If the pilot feed resembles them, nearly every aggregate would be exposed on its first re-weight, reset or repair followed by an unchanged upload. Whether it does is `[unverified: the workbooks are stale manual extracts and the pilot feed is planned orders from SAP staging; not determinable from code]`.

**Why retiring the client rewrite does not fix it.** Under O4 the client due-date rewrite goes away, which makes routes (a) and (b) value-neutral for timed finishes. For date-only, missing and midnight finishes the header still holds hygiene's derived value, so route (a) still overwrites the baseline. The false reset therefore survives unless the fallback that fills the baseline from the header (`data.py:1509-1510`) is also removed, or hygiene stops inventing a due date.

**What the planner sees, and what records it.** The planner sees the schedule they built on an aggregate vanish on an upload they did nothing to provoke: both children's placed bars snap back to the SAP-start position (today: start plus run time from SAP's start, 4.7.3), firm flags clear, split pieces are deleted, and every sibling does the same, except a running one. There is no planner-facing message; the only record is the upload's admin warning of category `sap_changed` with a count (`tests/test_distribution.py:4669` pins the count for a genuine SAP change). The upload then refills the baseline, so the next upload is clean and the planner re-does the work once per distribution write. **No test covers the date-only case:** the re-weight-then-upload class builds its parent with a timed finish (`tests/test_distribution.py:4616-4621`, finish = start plus 10 h; the test at `4671` re-weights and uploads a timed parent), and the tests that do use a midnight finish (`1325-1349`, `1470-1539`) exercise the 1-to-N anchor carry only. Test group 6 in 10.5 is therefore a gap closer, not a regression guard. See 8.11, OQ29 and Phase 1 item 2.

**What must change under A (consequences, not designs):**

1. Stop writing the as-sent baseline from the header or the plain order; carry the plain order's baseline and sent memory onto children, or leave it empty (an empty baseline is only filled at the next upload, never judged).
2. Stop writing the due column in the child upsert on re-weight, reset and repair; insert only for a brand-new child.
3. One echo rule (the corrected predicate of 7.3 item 1: date-only detection before zone conversion) shared by the plain-order upsert, the child upsert and the header refresh. If O4's protection is added only at the plain-order writer (`db.py:2829`, `2836`), the child upsert (`data.py:1355`, `1376`) and the header refresh (`1173-1174`) stay independent overwriters, and a later re-weight copies the echoed finish from the header back to every child.
4. The replan path keeps the ingest's as-sent value.

#### 4.7.7 The header is a third (and fourth) stored copy of the due date

| Copy | Where | Written by | Echo-overwritten | Client-corrected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Due column on each order | `orders.basic_finish_date` (wire "original end date") | ingest, child upsert, client baseline correction | yes | yes |
| As-sent baseline on each order | `orders.sap_basic_finish_date` | ingest, child upsert | yes (after the first Send and echo) | no |
| Aggregate header | `order_distribution.basic_finish_date` (`schema.sql:181`) | ingest (every time, including an echo), resolve routes; never the baseline-correct route | yes | no |
| Wire alias and staging row | not stored | n/a | n/a | n/a |

The header is shown in the distribution detail pane, sorts and filters the list by its start, and is the source of every re-weight's child dates. It already behaves like O4's "due date, never rewritten", with one hole: an ingest that carries SAP's echo of NIMBUS's roll-up overwrites it, and then re-weights propagate that to every child. No new header column is needed for the placed finish; the anchor lives on the children (the roll-up is computed, never stored).

#### 4.7.8 N to 1 collapse, the firmed survivor, and the spared running sibling

**N to 1 collapse (a firmed survivor).** When a share goes to zero and one machine is left at 100%, the survivor is a brand-new bare-id child that takes the old lettered child's slot. Copied verbatim: start, end, firm flag, notes, planning state, production version, tooling; segments are re-pointed; run time does **not** travel unless a planner typed it. The old child is exempt from the "scheduled children" confirmation, so a firmed slot collapses with no prompt and the dry run shows a frozen marker but no firm warning (`data.py:2839-2866`, `3100-3102`, `3142`).

Today the copied end is partial-share and ignored; the visible end silently becomes kept start + the full run time. Example (illustrative; now Mon 10-19 12:00, frozen horizon 2 days, calendar Mon-Fri 06:00-22:00): the placed, firmed child of 6 h stored Wed 06:00-12:00; collapse makes the order 10 h.

| Rule | Held finish | Derived start | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Today | n/a (start held) | Wed 06:00 | visible end Wed 16:00; start kept, bar 4 h wider, may overlap the next order and nothing re-fits it |
| R1 carry the stored end verbatim (literal A) | Wed 12:00 | Wed 06:00-12:00 = 6 h, remaining 4 h from Tue 22:00 back = **Tue 18:00** | the firmed slot's start jumps 12 clock hours earlier, inside the frozen window, possibly onto the previous order |
| R2 carry the end the planner sees today | Wed 16:00 | **Wed 06:00** | identity with today; the finish SAP may have seen (Wed 12:00) moves 4 h later |
| R3 hold whichever edge was firmed | depends | depends | the firm flag does not record which edge it protected |

**R2 is identity only for same-day survivors.** The collapse copies the old child's start and end verbatim (`backend/distribution/data.py:2838-2841`), and today's visible end for the survivor is its kept start plus the full run time as plain elapsed time (`db.py:212-217`). Rule R2 ("carry the end the planner sees today") therefore reproduces today's bar only when the kept start plus the run time stays inside one working window, as in the Wed 06:00 example above. A survivor whose span crosses a close derives a different start under a calendar-aware walk. Example (illustrative; calendar Mon-Fri 06:00-22:00): the survivor's kept start is Mon 20:00 and its full run time is 10 h. Today's visible end is the elapsed Tue 06:00. Under R2 the held finish is Tue 06:00, and a calendar-aware walk back from it (Tue 06:00 is the window's opening instant, so the walk starts at Mon 22:00) gives Mon 12:00: the start moves **8 hours earlier** than the kept Mon 20:00, onto whatever sits before it. Under R3, or under a rule that holds the start for such survivors, the bar stays put. R2 should be tested with a survivor that crosses a close before it is called "identity with today" (OQ37); the 4.7.8 examples were all same-day.

A segmented survivor is flagged mismatched (pieces sum to less than the new run time) and the reconcile re-places it forward today; under A, backward allocation from the last segment end gives Wed 14:00, eight hours **later** than today although run time grew, because the old idle gap is not reproduced `[INFERENCE: depends on the backward allocator that does not yet exist]`. Two smaller facts: the pane hydrates the new survivor as unfirmed although the server just copied the firm (`distribution-pane.mts:129`; the optimizer would treat it as unlocked until reload; independent of this project, `[INFERENCE, not run]`), and the survivor's "sent finish" memory is keyed to the deleted child, so the next Send's echo veto is unavailable for it.

**A running sibling spared by an SAP change.** A change to any child pulls in every sibling. A running, genuinely placed sibling keeps slot, firm and segments; the others lose theirs (`db.py:3652-3669`). Example (now Mon 10-19 09:00; M1 6 h placed and firmed Mon 07:00-13:00, therefore running; M2 4 h placed Tue 06:00-10:00; SAP moves the finish from Fri 16:00 to Thu 10-22 16:00):

| | Today (fallback = SAP start) | Under A (fallback = due date; O2 reversal) |
|---|---|---|
| M1 (spared) | Mon 07:00-13:00, firmed | Mon 07:00-13:00, firmed (its own placed finish) |
| M2 (reset) | Mon 06:00-10:00, a start already in the past that reads as running although no slot exists | Thu 12:00-16:00 (4 h back from the new due date) |
| Start spread / finish spread | 1 h / 3 h | 3 d 5 h / 3 d 3 h |
| Roll-up reported to SAP | Mon 13:00 (three days before SAP's own finish) | Thu 16:00 (the running child's end is hidden by the maximum) |
| Day-bucket separation alert | no | yes (Mon versus Thu) |
| Anchors in the family | planner start (M1), SAP start (M2) | planner finish (M1), due-date finish (M2): two anchor kinds in one family |

If SAP instead moves the finish to Mon 12:00, M2's derived start (Mon 08:00) is before now, so O2 places it Mon 09:00-13:00, one hour late. A never-placed child that is "running" only by its SAP window is a harmless non-event today and under A (nothing to protect).

#### 4.7.9 Read routes, CSV and the cutover rule

**Read routes (all untyped dictionaries; the only typed distribution response has no date field, so no DTO or generated type changes).**

| Surface | Keyed on | Flips under A? |
|---|---|---|
| List and aggregate date filters, list sort, its index | header's SAP start (`data.py:2083-2088`, `2441-2446`, `2133`; `schema.sql:201-202`) | no mechanically; a meaning question only if the owner wants the window keyed on due date or placed finish |
| Date-only "to" = end of that day; "from" = midnight | parser `routes.py:124-145` | no; the rule is also correct for an end-keyed bound |
| Aggregate `start` / `finish` and per-child dates | earliest child start / latest child end | both flip; for a never-spread new family `start` can precede the header start by days |
| CSV | same values, `str(datetime)` space format (JSON uses ISO "T"); no due-date column | values flip; a reader cannot tell placed finish from due date once they differ |
| `children_summary.earliest_start`, editor "Current start" | raw stored start, else SAP start; not segment- or queue-aware | silently wrong for a finish-anchored child (shows SAP start); the editor column is displayed |
| `meta.scheduled_children`, 409 guard, dry-run `scheduled` and `frozen` | stored start (the count at `data.py:2336`; the guard `scheduled_removed` at `3107-3109` and the 409 raised under it at `3111-3112`; the dry-run flags at `3141-3142`; the frozen flag at `3102`) | a finish-only placed child counts as unscheduled and is deleted by a re-weight with no confirmation (full site list in 4.7.10) |
| Mismatch badge, "problems" bucket | a stored boolean in three mirrored places (`service.py:445-449`, `data.py:1970`, `2010`, pane) | follows the flag's fate in the run-time section |

Hidden coupling: the aggregate query qualifies the end expression with a regular expression over exactly five column names (`data.py:2455-2458`); any new placed-finish column added to the end expression must be added to that list or the query reads the header's same-named column.

**Cutover: existing spread families versus new shared-finish families.** The identity-preserving write sets only the placed finish, and only for placed, writable rows. Never-placed children (the usual state of an untouched family) cannot be written without flipping their "user placed" status, so they keep a read-time fallback of SAP start + own run time: every sibling keeps the finish it shows today, and **no sibling is made equal to another**. Old families therefore stay start-spread; new aggregates ingested after cutover are finish-shared. Numeric example (same inputs as 4.7.3; "now" Tue 10-13):

| Family state | C1 | C2 | Aggregate read | Send to SAP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S0 today, untouched (and after identity cutover; nothing written) | Mon 06:00-12:00 | Mon 06:00-14:00 | Mon 06:00 to Mon 14:00 | **Mon 14:00** with today's code; under OQ33 B1 nothing is sent until a child is placed |
| S1 C2 dragged to Wed 08:00 (stored 08:00-16:00) | Mon 06:00-12:00 | Wed 08:00-16:00 | Mon 06:00 to Wed 16:00 | Wed 16:00 |
| S2 old family after cutover, then re-weight to 50/50 (finishes held) | Mon 07:00-12:00 | Fri 10-16 20:00 to Mon 14:00 (8 h Mon 06:00-14:00, 2 h from Fri 22:00 back) | Fri 20:00 to Mon 14:00 | Mon 14:00 |
| N0 new family under A | Fri 10:00-16:00 | Fri 08:00-16:00 | Fri 08:00 to Fri 16:00 | **Fri 16:00** (= due) |
| N1 N0 after re-weight to 50/50 | Fri 11:00-16:00 | Fri 06:00-16:00 | Fri 06:00 to Fri 16:00 | Fri 16:00 |

S0 and N0 are the same SAP order; the only difference is when it was first ingested. Options (the owner's choice, OQ35): **leave spread**, which moves nothing at cutover but leaves S2-style behaviour permanently (a child growing into last Friday evening after a share increase, and, with today's code, SAP receiving the compressed finish until someone moves it; under OQ33 B1 an unplaced child sends nothing, so SAP keeps its own finish until a child is placed); or **re-align at cutover**, which would move every never-placed bar from Monday to Friday (C1 Mon 12:00 to Fri 16:00 = 4 d 4 h; C2 Mon 14:00 to Fri 16:00 = 4 d 2 h) and move the finish a Send reports by +98 h, from today's Mon 14:00 to SAP's own due date. Placed, running and firmed children cannot be re-aligned without overriding planner intent or running-order protection. The profiling query for this must group by plant, aggregate order **and material** (a family is that triple), compare ends at minute precision, and report end spread, header gap, class mix and exposure counts, not merely "do ends differ"; the corrected query is described in 8.12.

**Weekly regeneration changes how long "old families" last (pointer to 4.13).** At the pilot, SAP's planning run regenerates unfirmed planned orders every week: it deletes them and recreates them under new numbers (`aggregate_to_detail.md:475`; answered "Weekly", `:665`), and only the SAP firm flag stops that. A new number is a new order id here, so an unfirmed old family disappears and a new shared-finish family (the "N0" row above) takes its place with default shares, while the planner's weights are lost. Two consequences. First, OQ35's "families stay permanently compressed" holds only for **firmed** families; unfirmed ones self-heal within a week, so "leave spread" costs less than the table suggests for them. Second, the headline promise "the finish NIMBUS sent to SAP never moves" holds only for orders SAP does not regenerate, that is firmed ones; for an unfirmed order SAP replaces the order and the finish it holds. Section 4.13.1 states the three rules (an echo of our own Send, a genuine SAP change, a delete-and-recreate) and what each does to a placed finish.

**The distribution-separation alert misfire.** Both the alert (`nimbus-compute-core.js:541-543`) and the optimizer finding (`setup-scheduler.mts:6724`) bucket sibling starts by hour, day or week. Today unplaced siblings share a start, so the rule is trivially satisfied. With a shared finish and unequal run times the starts differ by design (the spill variant of 4.7.3: Thu 18:00 versus Fri), so the `hour` policy fires on every aggregate and `day` fires whenever the longer child's walk crosses midnight, with a perfectly aligned finish. The S2 spared-sibling family (Mon versus Thu) also fires under `day`. The policy must be re-based on finish buckets or the alert redefined; both hand-synced copies change together, and the optimizer finding is a warning only (never a blocker).

#### 4.7.10 Where the server decides "placed", and who writes the shared child finish

**The sites.** A child that carries only a placed finish (a stored end and no stored start) is the row the new rule needs for a shared finish. The board read treats it as user-scheduled (`USER_SCHEDULED` is true when the start **or** the end is stored, `db.py:559`) and reads its start as SAP's start (`db.py:553`, `COALESCE(seg.first_start, scheduled_start, basic_start_date)`) and its end as start plus run time, ignoring the stored end whenever a run time exists (the plain expression, `db.py:212-217`; the board's variant returns the stored end only while the run-time mismatch flag is set, `db.py:554`). The distribution code decides "scheduled" from the stored start alone, so it disagrees with the board. All sites (every anchor re-opened at HEAD):

| Site | What it does with a finish-only child | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `backend/distribution/data.py:3107-3109` (`scheduled_removed`) | lists a removed child as scheduled only if its start is stored or it has segments | the child is not listed |
| `data.py:3111-3112` | raises the 409 (`DistributionChildrenScheduled`) only when `scheduled_removed` is non-empty | the confirmation never fires; a re-weight that drops the child deletes its placed finish with no prompt |
| `data.py:3102` | frozen flag requires a stored start before the frozen end | a finish-only child is never "frozen" in the removal details |
| `data.py:3141-3142` | dry-run `scheduled` and `frozen` flags use the same tests | the preview the planner approves says "not scheduled" |
| `data.py:1383` | the child upsert sets the run-time mismatch flag only when a start is stored or segments exist | a share change on a finish-only child sets no flag, so the browser never re-fits it |
| `data.py:1555` (inside `_unscheduled_ids`, used at `1815`) | plan-time orphan cleanup deletes children with no stored start and no segments | a finish-only orphan is deleted at ingest; only upload-created orphans reach this path (low) |
| `data.py:2295`, `2388` | aggregate start and the editor's "Current start" use stored start, else SAP start | a finish-anchored child shows SAP's start |
| `data.py:2336` | the list's `scheduled_children` count requires a stored start | undercounts |
| `frontend/distribution/distribution-pane.mts:116` | `user_scheduled: child.scheduled_start !== null` | the pane hydrates a finish-only child as not user-placed, so the browser treats it as an unplaced row |

**Who writes the shared finish.** Nobody. At first ingest each child copies the aggregate's SAP start and SAP finish into the SAP date columns and receives no stored schedule (`data.py:784-786`; the upsert deliberately leaves `scheduled_start` and `scheduled_end` alone for a kept child, `1419-1423`). The only server code that writes a child's schedule today is the 1-to-N carry (`data.py:1426-1474`, start plus run time) and the N-to-1 collapse (`2836-2860`). A server that writes a finish and no start produces the hybrid row above; a server that also wrote a start would have to compute it without a calendar. The ways the gap can be closed, each with its cost (the choice is OQ58, not made here):

| Way | What it means for the planner | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| The browser writes it on first load of a never-placed family (placed finish plus derived start through a normal save) | the family appears on the due date; needs a planner session and flips each child to user-placed | every loading tab does it and the first save wins (OQ51); the 4.7.9 hybrid rows disappear |
| The server writes the finish and flags the child "stored start is stale" (the redefined mismatch flag, OQ34), the browser derives the start | same, with the server holding the finish from the start | the flag must be set for never-placed children too (4.7.4 item 1); the predicates above still need the finish-only fix |
| No stored write: a read-time rule (OQ33) | "shared finish" is a display rule, Send sends nothing until someone places the family | the headline promise needs a placement before it applies; minimum change |

Whichever is chosen, every server site above and the pane copy need a "has a placed finish" test (start or end stored, as the board already does at `db.py:559`) before a stored finish is trusted.

### 4.8 Optimizer under Reading A

**Scope of this section.** Reading A only: the optimizer keeps sequencing forward but its results must be expressed finish-first and survive later changes. Reading B (backward dispatch) is section 5. Anchors are in `frontend/optimization/` at `757dd86` unless stated.

**Headline.** Under Reading A the optimizer itself needs almost nothing: it already writes both a start and a finish for every order it places. The danger is everything that happens to its result afterwards. Today the optimizer's finish survives a reload only by coincidence (a continuous bar is exactly run-time long, and split orders keep their own segment rows). The coincidence breaks the day a run time changes.

#### Impact table

| Item | Today | Under A | Severity | Anchors | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output contract (what Apply writes) | start, end, segments, status, reason (five allow-listed keys) | the same five; the end is defined as the placed finish; no new key needed unless the server wants an explicit anchor marker | medium | `setup-scheduler.mts:33-36`, `6484` | `optimizer-worker.test.mjs` |
| Durability of the optimizer's finish | survives reload only because end minus start equals run time | breaks on a later run-time change: server read +2 h or client reconcile +18 h (simulation) | blocker (server side) | `db.py:212-217`; `engine.mts:1261`, `1174`; `setup-scheduler.mts:6534` | none |
| Pull-forward floor | measured on the START; re-checked on every run for every in-scope unprotected order | a finish-held growth can push the start below the floor; the next Optimize re-checks it and queues an incumbent that now violates it unless the search finds a compatible slot (4.8.4); manual moves ignore the floor today | medium | `engine.mts:1084-1104`; `setup-scheduler.mts:2847-2848`, `6532`, `6781-6788`, `7081-7085` | `engine.test.mjs:50-125` |
| Push-forward cap, over-cap | already measured on the FINISH | unchanged | low | `setup-scheduler.mts:3009-3010`, `6245-6248` | keep |

| Instability | keyed on START (minutes between old and new start) | should key on finish (or both): a right-shift or a finish-held re-derivation moves starts without moving finishes, and is scored as instability | low | `setup-scheduler.mts:2999-3000`, `7202-7203` | `setup-scheduler.test.mjs:5056` flips |

| Running protection | start <= now < end | a derived start before now makes an unstarted order "running" and protects it | high | `engine.mts:1024-1027`, `205-218`; `optimize-ui.mts:2118` | `optimize-ui.test.mjs:1629` |

| Dead legacy placement walk | unreachable for the four real modes | delete (O3: forward paths are replaced) | medium | `engine.mts:2122`, `2463`, `1859`, `1872`; `types.mts:467` | `engine.test.mjs:938`, `1167`, `147-180` |

#### 4.8.1 It needs no backward primitive (A-lite)

Every placement path in the optimizer walks a cursor forward from the planning start or a predecessor's end and emits start = first piece, end = last piece. The only end-to-start arithmetic is calendar-blind ordering math (`capAwareSequence` in `scheduler-contract.mts`, `orderedBySlack`), used to rank orders, never to place them (`setup-scheduler.mts:3765-3769`, `2047`). So "sequence forward, store the finish as the anchor" requires: (a) a statement that the end is authoritative and the server honors it; (b) the forward result stored verbatim; (c) every non-optimizer path that re-derives an end forward to stop doing so. The forward walk is also, already, O2's reversal: a placement can never start before the planning floor (`engine.mts:2046-2048`), so a finish pushed past its due date is simply late.

#### 4.8.2 The patch already carries both edges

A patch's changes are limited by the validator to five keys (`setup-scheduler.mts:6484`): start, end, segments, status, reason. Times are minute-exact (the store skips its 15-minute snap for any task carrying a planning status, `store.mts:909`, `914-915`). A new anchor key, if the owner wants one, must be added to that allow-list, to the persistence payload builder (`persistence.mts:1410-1430`), the server payload model and the task type. If the end is simply defined as the placed finish, nothing is added.

#### 4.8.3 The finish survives reload only by coincidence

The server's effective end is start + run time whenever run time is set and ignores the stored end (`db.py:212-217`). The optimizer's continuous bar is exactly run-time long (a validation finding enforces this, `setup-scheduler.mts:6534`) and split orders are held by segment rows, so the finish returns correct. Simulation 4.8.6 shows what happens when run time changes after Apply.

#### 4.8.3a The four live modes and the two evaluator labels nobody reaches

The Optimize dialog offers four strategies in a dropdown with a hint line (`frontend/index.html:2578-2583`; the type is `OptimizerMode = 'spt' | 'changeover' | 'duedate' | 'backlog'`, `frontend/platform/types.mts:467`). Section 4.8 and section 5 spoke of "the four real modes" without naming them, and **SPT appears nowhere else in this document**. What each does, what "due" means in it, and what happens to it under O3 and Reading A:

| Mode (hint the planner reads, `frontend/locales/en.js:1374-1377`) | Evaluator label sent by `runAndApply` (`engine.mts:2122-2123`) | How "due" enters | Direction | Under O3 and Reading A |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPT** (`spt`): "Shortest processing first, minimize average completion time" | `spt`; the setup-aware evaluator `evaluateSptWithSetup` (`setup-scheduler.mts:5586-5599`): run time seeds the order, setup is reserved after an order is chosen | not an objective; the due date reaches it through the pull floor (a start edge), the push ceiling (a finish edge) and the late tally | forward | stays forward and start-ordered; every row of 4.8.4 applies; the instability key (OQ20) changes its score the same way |
| **Min Changeover** (`changeover`): groups orders to cut setup; "due dates otherwise don't drive the sequence" | `min-changeover` | same two limits; lateness is scored below over-cap, uncovered edges, setup and priority (`frontend/optimization/CLAUDE.md`, "Admission and strategy objectives") | forward | stays forward; OQ14, OQ20 apply; this is why OQ48's option (d) "fold just-in-time into Min Changeover" contradicts a settled promise |
| **Due Date** (`duedate`): "lateness ranks first" | `due-date` | the only mode where lateness outranks setup grouping; due is read raw (`dueTimestamp`, `setup-scheduler.mts:1196-1199`) | forward | stays forward; its lateness is the number OQ23's time-of-day rule changes (4.10.4) |
| **Remove Backlog** (`backlog`): "shifts past-due scheduled orders forward without resequencing their line" | none: a separate function, `Engine.removeBacklog` (`engine.mts:1331-1459`) | ignores due dates, caps and setup | forward from now, in start order | stays forward; edges in 4.8.7, OQ56 |

**Two evaluator labels with no UI route.** The setup-aware seam `Engine.evaluateSetupAware` accepts five labels, `'due-date-first' | 'due-date' | 'spt' | 'min-changeover' | 'throughput'` (`engine.mts:871-872`), but `runAndApply` maps the three UI modes to `spt`, `due-date` and `min-changeover` only (`engine.mts:2123`). `throughput` (its own evaluator and thresholds, `engine.mts:890-893`) and `due-date-first` (the older Due Date flavour in which same-signature grouping outranks lateness, pinned by `tests/modules/setup-scheduler.test.mjs:4276-4372`) are not passed by any app code path. They are reachable by calling the public seam directly, and the tests exercise the underlying evaluators and comparator by name (`evaluateThroughput` at `tests/modules/setup-scheduler.test.mjs:579, 882, 3610`; the comparator loop over all five labels at `393`; `placeUnknownTail(..., 'due-date-first')` at `3836`). Both are forward, start-anchored evaluators. O3 says forward paths are replaced; these are forward paths that no planner can reach and tests still exercise, so the document must say what happens to them: keep and test them (cost: they stay start-anchored beside a finish-anchored world), or delete them with the dead legacy walk (4.8.10, OQ22). That is an owner confirmation, not an investigation gap; the lead recommendation of OQ22 ("yes", delete) was written for the walk only.

#### 4.8.4 Per-rule anchor-edge list

| Rule | Edge today | Under A |
|---|---|---|
| Pull-forward floor (due midnight minus N days, maxed with the frozen end) | START (setup start and productive start) | stays a start floor at placement **and is re-checked on every run** for every in-scope, unprotected order: an incumbent whose start is now below the floor, before now, or whose end is past its ceiling is not kept; its baseline patch is queued (null dates, `needs_planning`) and the order is rescued only if the search finds a compatible slot (`setup-scheduler.mts:7081-7085`, `6781-6788`, `6532`). Reinterpreting it as a finish floor changes the worker map's meaning (owner decision, OQ20) |
| Push-forward ceiling (due midnight + N + 1 days) | FINISH | unchanged |
| Over-cap tier | FINISH | unchanged; placed and flagged, never freezes a line |
| Frozen floor and frozen protection | START in [now, frozen end) | judged on the derived start; can flip on a run-time change (OQ4) |
| Planning-start floor | START | the forward walk is O2's reversal; no change |
| Running protection | START and FINISH | a derived start before now reads as running |
| Initial-anchor rule | START to pick, FINISH to start the next fragment | unchanged while start is stored; overlapping derived intervals can make "earliest start" and "ends last" diverge |
| Fragment boundaries, gap fill, tails | START bounds fragments, FINISH opens the next | unchanged (forward) |
| Lateness, late count | FINISH minus due | unchanged formula; due value flips (O4) |
| Instability | START | key on finish (owner choice, OQ20) |
| "Changed" (patches Apply writes) | START, END and SEGMENTS (`setup-scheduler.mts:6879`) | unchanged; already sees a finish move |
| Distribution separation finding | START bucket | misfires with shared finishes (4.7.9) |
| Validation: setup floor, setup calendar | START | setup must lie right before the derived start in working time |
| Validation: line chain order | START order (six places) | a bar that grows left past its neighbour's start reorders the chain, flipping setup pairs |

Validation findings by edge: start-keyed `date_window` (start side), `setup_floor`, `setup_calendar`, the chain sorts, `distribution_separation`; end-keyed `date_window` (end side), `setup_overlap`; both `invalid_schedule`, `calendar`, `capacity_overlap`; neutral the rest. Real exposures under A: setup relative to a derived start at a window edge, start-ordered adjacency when bars nest, and "running" by arithmetic.

**The pull floor stays live, which can unschedule a finish SAP already holds.** Example (illustrative): an order due Thu 10-22 with pull-forward 3 days has a floor of Mon 10-19 00:00, on a Mon-Fri 06:00-22:00 plant with a 1-day push limit. Its run time grows from 6 h to 90 h while the finish holds at Thu 18:00. Walking back (Thu 12 h, Wed 16 h, Tue 16 h, Mon 16 h, the previous Fri 16 h, then 14 h of the previous Thu) puts the derived start at Thu 10-15 08:00, in the previous week and below the floor. Nothing flags it between runs (manual moves ignore the floor today). The next Optimize does check it: unless the order is running, frozen or manually firmed, its stored bar now starts before the floor, so the incumbent is rejected and its baseline patch is queued; the search then looks for a slot between the floor and the push ceiling (Mon 10-19 to Sat 10-24: five open days, at most 80 working hours) and finds none that holds 90 h under a split policy that follows the calendar, so the order stays in Needs Planning with a reason and no dates, and the finish SAP was last told is on no bar. What protects a held finish today is only running, the frozen window and a manual firm (OQ4 decides whether the firm covers the finish); an unprotected finish-held bar is re-placed by any run, as 4.8.5 already says. Correction to a statement in the first edition of this document (E.3 row 12): it described the floor as "not re-checked ... silent"; it is re-checked every run, and the silence is only between runs.

**Setup at a window edge.** Test `setup-scheduler.test.mjs:4548` (window opens 08:00, 60-minute setup, expects productive start 09:00) pins the **keep-convention** rule: setup sits in the same free interval immediately before the stored start. It does not pin OQ2's "stored start becomes the setup start". The three options for OQ2 are (1) keep the rule and reserve setup inside the window during the backward walk, (2) relax the calendar check to allow setup across a closed gap, (3) redefine the stored start as the setup start (about 12 touch points). Under A with a held finish, a derived start at or within the setup minutes after a window open raises a setup-calendar error unless the walk reserves setup in-window (the finish must move earlier, or the order must split) or the check is relaxed.

#### 4.8.5 Where the optimizer is NOT the problem

Re-derivation paths other than the optimizer must hold the finish instead of moving it: the server effective-end expressions and their copies (distribution aggregate, write response, Send), the resolver's cutover signal, the client reconcile, `schedulePatchFor` and both manual patch functions with their callers (`gantt.mts:4389`, `4437`, `4489`; `orders.mts:1378`, `1517`, `2484`), the load-time snap, the one-click alert fix, and the auto-reflow cascade. These belong to their own sections; the optimizer is deliberately off the list because a run re-places every in-scope order and legitimately decides new finishes.

#### 4.8.6 The A/B/C simulation (hand-traced)

Inputs (illustrative): one machine, calendar Mon-Fri 06:00-18:00, no blackouts, no frozen horizon, split policy `never`, zero setup, nothing firmed or running. Orders: **A** 6 h due Wed 2026-10-21 18:00; **B** 4 h due Thu 10-22 12:00; **C** 8 h due Thu 10-22 18:00. Now Mon 10-19 08:00. Pull 3 days, push 1 day.

**Forward walk today (Due Date or Min Changeover, same result):** A **Mon 08:00-14:00**, B **Mon 14:00-18:00**, C **Tue 06:00-14:00**. Every order finishes 52, 66 and 52 hours before its due date. The placed finishes (Mon 14:00, Mon 18:00, Tue 14:00) become the anchors and what Send reports; the due dates stay untouched. Expressed finish-first, the derived starts equal the forward starts value for value (continuous, single-window, zero-setup case); they diverge only for split orders, 24/7 plants and setup crossing a window edge.

**After Apply and Save, B's run time changes from 4 h to 6 h:**

| Path | Result for B | Finish moved |
|---|---|---|
| Server read (resolver outside cutover, or a quantity change from SAP): start + 6 h on naive timestamps | Mon 14:00-**20:00**, 2 h past plant close | +2 h; the finish Send reports follows it |
| Client reconcile (cutover or mismatch path): forward search from Mon 14:00 for a 6 h slot | **Tue 06:00-12:00**, overlapping C (06:00-14:00) because the search ignores siblings | +18 h |
| Finish held (what A wants) | **Mon 12:00-18:00**, overlapping A (12:00-14:00) | 0; an overlap alert, resolved by the next optimize |
| Finish held, B grows to 12 h | derived start Mon 06:00 is before now: reversal, forward from now; 10 h left Monday under `never`, so **Tue 06:00-18:00** | +24 h, lateness shown as an alert |

The two re-derivations disagree with each other (Mon 20:00 versus Tue 12:00) and with the placed finish. That disagreement is the blocker for any held finish.

**Pull-floor variant (pull 0, push 1):** A lifts to Wed 06:00-12:00, B to Thu 06:00-10:00, C Thu 10:00-18:00 (finish equals due, not late). The floor binds as a start edge.

**Split order (min-segment rule, policy partial-allowed, minimum piece 30 min, order D 260 min, forward cursor Thu 14:00):** forward pieces Thu 14:00-17:50 and Fri 06:00-06:30; a finish-first fill from Fri 06:30 gives Thu 14:10-18:00 and Fri 06:00-06:30. Same finish, start 10 minutes later. A forward result is therefore **not a fixed point** of the finish-first derivation.

#### 4.8.7 Remove Backlog stays forward

Remove Backlog compresses orders whose start is before now by placing them forward from now, ignoring due dates, caps and setup, and is exempt from firmed, running and frozen protection (`engine.mts:1331-1459`; selection `1361`, cursor `1377`). Under A it is O2's reversal in bulk and needs no backward primitive; Reading B does not change it. Two meaning shifts: "backlog" becomes "derived start before now", so a run-time growth on an order with a future finish makes it backlog and pushes its finish later; and running orders are re-placed from now with their full run time (pinned by `remove-backlog.test.mjs:290`), which double-counts work already done (OQ3).

**Edges the document has not decided (pointer to OQ56).** Remove Backlog's own rules are start-keyed in four places: its window `[From, To)` selects an order by its start (`frontend/optimization/engine.mts:1361`), each line's orders are compressed in start order (`1373`), the pass stops at the first order whose start is not before now and that the compressed cursor has not yet reached (`1380`), and the dialog's default From is the earliest past start while To is the latest end, capped at four months ahead (`optimize-ui.mts:350-358`). Once a derived start moves by data, an order can enter or leave the window, change place in the compression order, or end the loop early with no planner action. Example (illustrative): two orders on a line, X derived start Mon 08:00 and Y derived start Mon 12:00, now Mon 10:00, window default. Today only X is backlog. If Y's run time grows with its finish held and its derived start moves to Mon 05:00, Y becomes backlog too, is re-placed forward from now with its full run time, and its finish moves later, although nobody touched it. The window, the sort key and the break rule are one decision (which edge defines "backlog"); it is OQ56.

#### 4.8.8 Worker contract: the shapes do not change, the envelope has no version

**What the request carries.** The worker request is `{runId, mode, snapshot, request, deadlineDurationMs}` (`frontend/optimization/optimizer-worker-contract.mts:4-12`). The `snapshot` holds whole tasks (so every order's `original_end_date` and stored start and end), the calendars, firmed ids and setup truth (`setup-scheduler.mts:378-398`); the `request` holds the clocks (`now`, `runNow`, `planningStart`, `placementStart`), the line scope, the horizon end and the firmed and calendar flags (`setup-scheduler.mts:434-459`). The two per-task maps, the start floor from the pull rule and the end ceiling from the push rule, are **not** in the request: the closures that compute them cannot be cloned, so the worker sends them back in its **response** (`notBeforeById` and `notAfterById`, `optimizer-worker-contract.mts:33-34`, built at `61-66`) and the main thread rehydrates them to validate Apply (`engine.mts:2856-2857`, `2896-2897`). The conclusion stands: no payload field is missing for forward sequencing with finish-first output; the snapshot already carries enough for a backward placement; the stale-candidate check compares the whole snapshot. A change arises only if the pull rule is reinterpreted as a finish floor (the map's meaning, or a second map) or if the response gains a field.

**There is no version on the envelope, so an old tab can pair with a new worker.** Neither the request nor the response carries a build or version identifier. Each preview starts a **fresh** worker from the server (`optimizer-worker-client.mts:48-51`, `65`: `new Worker(new URL('./optimizer-worker.mjs', import.meta.url))`), while the main-thread code that built the request and will rehydrate the answer is whatever the tab loaded earlier. After a cutover deploy, an old tab's main thread therefore talks to a worker running the new engine. Any added or renamed response field then throws on the old tab: the rehydration check rejects the whole answer with a "malformed validation metadata" error (`engine.mts:2849-2869`). This section's A-lite plan adds no field and is unaffected; A-strict, a due-instant map for OQ23, or Reading B's slack and missing-due request fields would each trigger it. The stale-tab protection decided for saves (OQ36: close-and-save, same-image route refusal, cache discard now; a version gate later) does not cover the optimizer path. Options for the optimizer path (no decision): carry a build id in both envelopes and refuse a mismatch with a toast that asks for a reload, or keep every new field optional and tolerated by the rehydration check.

#### 4.8.9 Undo restores run time too

Preview Apply pushes one entry restoring a clone of every task in the plant (`optimize-ui.mts:1357-1362`, `2125-2126`); the live path restores patched ids (`engine.mts:2216-2222`). Restoration is field-generic and includes run time. If run time changed after Apply, undo re-installs the old finish against a run time the server no longer has. A finish-first undo should restore the finish and re-derive the start. Persisting any new anchor field requires it in the save payload builder. The one-click overload alert fix pushes two undo entries today (`engine.mts:2219`, `insights/services.mts:472`), so two Ctrl+Z presses are needed; unchanged.

#### 4.8.10 The dead legacy walk

For the four real modes the old placement walk (about `engine.mts:2262-2619`), its policy dispatcher and its comparator are unreachable; only test code with a non-public mode string reaches them (`engine.test.mjs:938`, `1167`, plus the cap-aware group `147-180` that also covers a live helper). It is still reachable at runtime by any untyped mode string passed through the worker. O3 says forward paths are replaced, so leaving it means maintaining a second start-anchored path nothing exercises. Boundary of the dead block is stated differently by three reports (the block spans roughly 2262-2619); cite that range.

#### 4.8.11 A-lite versus A-strict (options raised, not a decision)

| Option | What it is | Optimizer cost | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A-lite** | define the end as the placed finish; store the optimizer's start and segments verbatim; re-derive only on triggers (run-time change, calendar change, machine move) | no backward primitive; about 60-120 source lines for the allow-list or anchor key, finish-keyed instability and "changed", and deleting the dead walk, **plus** the pieces earlier counts left out: a floor alert or a deliberate "queued" rule for an incumbent that falls below the pull floor (4.8.4), the start-keyed optimizer checks (`setup-scheduler.mts:6532`, `6579`, `7085`), and the OQ18 rounding at the placement edge (round up to the minute still un-runs an order for up to 59 s, and the 15-minute snap and the optimizer floor give three behaviours); 150-300 test lines; about 1 week for the original scope `[INFERENCE, no benchmark]`, more with the additions | stored state is stable; a split order's start may differ from a fresh finish-first derivation by up to a fragment's slack |
| **A-strict** | add a validation finding that every emitted (start, segments) equals the finish-first derivation | needs a backward placer over the optimizer's own merged intervals plus split normalisation, about 200-260 lines shared with the Reading B post-pass; +3-5 days `[INFERENCE, very low confidence]` | reproducible state; moves split-order starts by up to one fragment; must use the optimizer's interval definition (touching intervals merge across midnight on a 24/7 plant, the calendar engine does not). The A-strict placer is the same backward placer that section 5.7's post-pass needs; it is one component, costed once (here and in 5.3), not twice. |

#### 4.8.12 Preview staleness

The Optimize preview compares the entire task of every plant order while open (`optimize-ui.mts:1010-1012`, `1239-1254`) and the candidate check compares the whole snapshot. A new stored field is covered automatically; but any background re-derivation (the client reconcile, which fires on calendar change and on every refresh, `engine.mts:2779-2789`) while a preview is open will stale it and block Apply.

#### 4.8.13 A deadline-bound search gives different answers on different hardware, and under A those answers go to SAP

The optimizer's search stops at a 5-second deadline (`engine.mts:562`, `2176`) and visits lines alphabetically; a line the deadline reaches late is tail-placed forward without being searched. The optimizer plan says so plainly: on the 70-line, 30-orders-per-line shape the wall time ranged 2.2 to 4.9 s for Min Changeover, "the 5 s deadline sits inside that noise, so on a slower laptop the same plant gets a different answer", and "faster is not neutral for planners: on a slow machine the deadline today leaves late-alphabet lines unoptimized; a faster engine reaches them, so results shift toward the no-deadline answer" (`Optimizer_Update_10_06.MD:498, 505`); which lines get optimized when time runs out is one of its open owner questions (`:678`). Under today's rules a different answer is a different bar. Under Reading A the optimizer's finish becomes the **placed finish that Send reports to SAP**, so two planners with different laptops, or one planner before and after a hardware change, can send SAP different finishes for the same plant state. Example (illustrative): a plant of 70 lines; planner P's machine searches 55 lines before the deadline and tail-places 15; planner Q's machine searches all 70. The 15 tail-placed lines get forward finishes on P's plan and optimized finishes on Q's; both are Applied, saved and Sent. The convergence assumption this document relies on (an acceptable answer under A-lite regardless of where the deadline falls) is therefore not established; it is medium severity. What is needed before A-lite or B goes live, as questions rather than designs: the order lines are visited under a deadline (alphabetical, fair, most urgent first), what the preview says when lines were not searched (it already reports an incomplete search), and whether Send should warn when the plan it sends came from a deadline-hit run. (Measurement note: the trims T1 and T3 are in the code since 2026-10-07 and cut the large-shape median from 2.09 s to 1.16 s, `Optimizer_Update_10_06.MD:700`, which moves the boundary but does not remove it on a slower machine.)

#### 4.8.14 Interaction with the optimizer plan's Part 4 (line parallelism, cross-line and production-version moves)

`Optimizer_Update_10_06.MD` Part 4 sets rules for any future optimizer that fans lines out to parallel workers or moves orders between lines or production versions (`:643-669`): today the optimizer never moves an order's machine or production version, and `validateCandidate` rejects any patch that touches anything but the five schedule fields (`:646`; `setup-scheduler.mts:6484`); the choices that "keep the door open" are to partition by components, fan out only after an explicit assignment step, keep one post-merge finalize with a slot for cross-line re-checks, keep the serial reference path, and **not hard-code the five-field patch rule into the new Worker protocol** (`:664-669`). This document touches those rules in two places and did not engage them. (i) 4.8.2's option of a new anchor key would extend exactly that five-key allow-list; if it is added, declare it once in the allow-list constant so a later protocol can reuse the list instead of copying it. (ii) 5.3 and 5.6 treat line parallelism as "the deferred 5-7 day item" and size a backward placer per line; Part 4 says the finalize that judges "keep the new plan or revert" is plant-wide, so a per-line backward result has to survive that judgement, which is one reason full B is more than a mode literal (5.6). Neither point needs a decision now; both are inputs to OQ48 and OQ14.

### 4.9 Setup/changeover

**What happens today.** Setup (changeover) time is never stored. No order, segment or `orders` column holds a setup start, finish or duration (grep of the schema: only plant policy, machine compatibility, routing setup groups and the four setup tables). It is recomputed from the line on every read: the previous order on the line by START is the predecessor, and the setup bar is drawn immediately before the successor's first productive start. The stored start and finish are the PRODUCTIVE window; setup sits outside, ahead of the start (`engine.mts:493-494`; `setup-scheduler.mts:330-334`). The only persisted setup artefacts are matrix minutes, the machine's last asserted state, and override rows keyed to an exact (predecessor, successor) pair. There is nothing to migrate on the server.

**The one rule at HEAD (ruling XC-R2).** Stored start = productive start; setup = the minutes immediately before it, inside the SAME free interval (`setup-scheduler.mts:329-334`; validator `6577-6584`). Test 4548 (hours open 08:00-18:00, 60-minute setup, expected productive start 09:00) pins that rule. Some lane reports labelled it as pinning the owner's "setup inside the held-finish window" option; that label is wrong. The owner's three options therefore stand as: keep the rule, relax it across a closed gap, or redefine the stored start as the setup start.

**What the new rule breaks.** Under today's forward placement a violation cannot happen, because the placer puts the productive start at interval start + setup. A backward walk can land the start anywhere, including inside the changeover zone of the previous order.

#### Impact table

| Surface | Today | Under the new rule | Severity | Anchors | Tests pinning it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Setup stored? | Derived from adjacency, never stored | Unchanged; adjacency key (start order) moves with every run-time change | low | `engine.mts:434-437`; `setup/setup-domain.mts:467` | none |
| Gap between orders | 30 min legal with zero slack | Gap shrinks when a derived start moves left; alert, red bar, validator errors, nothing repairs | high | `engine.mts:363-378`; `nimbus-compute-core.js:862` | `compute-core.test.js` 178-211 keep |
| Window-open landing | Cannot occur from forward placement | Fires in every check (below) | high | `engine.mts:344, 375`; `setup-scheduler.mts:6577-6585` | none (no test of a start at a window open) |
| Manual placement | Setup-blind; no edit-time check | Same; backward result unprotected | high | `engine.mts:1169-1275` | none |
| Optimizer placers | Forward; setup at interval front | Forward stays (A-lite); backward twin only for A-strict | medium | `setup-scheduler.mts:307-374`; `calendar-engine.mts:603-616` | `setup-scheduler.test.mjs` 930-1010, 4548 keep |
| "Enough changeover" definitions | Three coexist (wall-clock gap; contiguous in-window time; span coverage) | Disagree on a hand-placed order after a closed gap | medium | `engine.mts:2668-2669, 320-379`; `setup-scheduler.mts:6581, 7009` | engine tests 673-745, 1648-1770, 3686 |
