## 7. Phased migration plan

This section turns the sequencing constraints found in sections 4 to 6 and 8 into phases. It is evidence-backed sequencing, not a schedule and not code: no effort estimate exists for Phases 1 to 4 (the fleet sized only the optimizer options, 4.8.11 and 5.3), and every phase lists the gate it must pass and how it is rolled back. Two kinds of gate appear. A **test gate** is a group of new or flipped tests from section 10 (the 33 NEW-NEEDED groups of 10.5 are numbered there); the code team can close it alone. An **owner gate** is a decision in section 12 that the code cannot settle; the phase must not start its affected work until the owner has decided it.

### 7.1 Shape of the plan

Owner decision O3 replaces every forward path in one release for all plants. That fixes the shape: only Phase 1 can reach production on its own, because it moves no bar for orders that have a run time or a stored end (7.3 states the exception for orders with neither). Phases 2 and 3 are build phases: their work is merged and tested but is released only together with Phase 4, in one image (8.13 step 4). Shipping the new read rule without the derived-start writers would show wrong bars, and shipping the writers without the read rule would lose the placed finish on reload, because the server read still discards it (4.1.2). Phase 5 (Reading B) is separately decidable (section 5).

**"Released only together with Phase 4" is an intention that nothing in the repository enforces.** Every deploy ships all of `main`. The deploy skill says "Deploys build from the working tree, so nothing else stops a red or untested commit from shipping" (`.claude/skills/promote-azure/SKILL.md:49`); the build is `az acr build ... .` of the whole tree (`SKILL.md:69`); and once started it builds and rolls straight through with no pause (`SKILL.md:19`). Under O3 there is no flag that keeps new code dormant. A Phase 1 deploy therefore carries whatever is merged: any Phase 2 or 3 work that has reached `main`, and code already on `main` that moves dates, namely the SAP staging apply and Send to SAP and the Machine Hours run-time rule (commit `621f81f`, a third date-moving event, 8.9). A deploy has in fact happened since both were merged: `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:197` records a roll of image v113 on 2026-10-13, and `621f81f` is an ancestor of the commits that followed it, so the live image probably carries both **[unverified: the commit built into v113 and the live `NIMBUS_BUILD_ID` have not been compared with `git log`; Phase 0 does this, 1.5 item 3]**. "Phase 1 alone" therefore needs a named release mechanism (7.1.1). Until the owner chooses one, the phase table below describes the content of each phase, not what a deploy will contain.

| Phase | What ships | Reaches production alone? | Test gate | Owner gate | Rollback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 Facts, decisions, profiling | No code. Profiling SQL results, SAP Development answers, backup confirmation, a five-minute browser check, owner decisions | n/a | Local Postgres test environment working (`NIMBUS_TEST_DB=1`) | Blocks Phase 1 (Phase 1 gates): OQ23, OQ24, OQ28, OQ29, OQ30, OQ31, OQ45, a release mechanism (7.1.1), and OQ10 and OQ61 before the first live Send. Decide during Phase 1 (Phase 2 gates; they block Phase 2, not Phase 1): OQ1, OQ2, OQ3, OQ4, OQ5, OQ7, OQ13, OQ15, OQ32, OQ33, OQ34, OQ50 to OQ54, OQ59. The Appendix D answers (blocker 18) given, or accepted by the owner in writing as an assumption, before the first production Send and in any case before Phase 4 | n/a |
| 1 Protect the due date | Due-date guard at the three write sites (or the in-memory patch) using a corrected echo predicate (the SAP-zone midnight case, 4.5.5), as-sent start baseline, distribution baseline-write fixes, hygiene inversion of the finish side, the client date-only lateness read rule, retirement of the client rewrite and the baseline-correct route, due date on `/tasks/refresh`, legacy due-date repair for never-sent orders only, and the independent fixes (purge preview range, dead date counters) | Yes, once a release mechanism exists (7.1.1); moves no bar for orders that have a run time or a stored end (7.3); changes lateness numbers | Groups 6 (including the distribution false-reset case and the cross-zone exact-midnight echo case) and 13 (hygiene part); flipped ingest hygiene tests | OQ23, OQ24, OQ28, OQ29, OQ30, OQ31, OQ45 (and OQ10 and OQ61 for the first live Send); OQ28 decided and the per-row handling shipped or the rule held (blocker 16) | Previous image; the repair, if run, is reversible only from the pre-repair snapshot; a rollback re-enables the overwrite, the fabrication and the client rewrite (7.3) |

#### 7.1.1 How "Phase 1 alone" can be made real (options for the owner)

Two real options and one that O3 rules out. The owner chooses; this section does not.

| Option | What happens | Concrete example | Cost or risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. A release branch for each releasable step | When Phase 1 is merged and has passed its gate, cut `release/phase-1` from that commit and build from it in a clean checkout. Phase 2 and 3 work keeps merging to `main`. | Phase 1 lands on Monday; the first Phase 2 merge lands on Wednesday; Thursday's deploy is built from `release/phase-1`, so the image holds no Phase 2 code. | The skill builds whatever tree is checked out (`SKILL.md:49`, `69`), so the operator must build from that branch in a clean worktree. CI runs only on pushes to `main` and on pull requests (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:6-9`), so a release-branch commit has check-runs only through a pull request or an edit to the trigger list, and the skill's CI gate wants check-runs for the exact commit (`SKILL.md:49-61`). Fixes made on `main` must be carried over by hand. Code already on `main` (staging, Machine Hours) is inside the branch unless it is cut from an earlier commit. |
| B. Keep Phases 2 and 3 on a feature branch until Phase 4 | Phase 2 and 3 work merges into a feature branch (name illustrative, `feature/backward-scheduling`), never into `main`. `main` receives only Phase 1 and unrelated fixes, so every deploy from `main` is Phase-1-only. The branch merges to `main` as one step at the start of Phase 4. | The calendar work stays on the feature branch for weeks; the pilot is redeployed from `main` twice for unrelated fixes and neither image contains any backward-scheduling code. | A long-lived branch against a trunk that also receives commits from other sessions; merge drift grows with time. CI reaches the branch only through a pull request (`ci.yml:9`), so a draft pull request is needed. The words "merged and tested" in 7.1 and the "revert the branch" rollbacks of 7.4 and 7.5 describe this option. |
| C. One image with the new code switched off | New code ships dormant behind a switch and is turned on at the cutover. | n/a | Ruled out by O3 (forward paths are replaced, not kept behind a switch). Listed only so it is not proposed again. |

Whichever option is chosen:

1. Deploy only from a clean tree or a pushed commit (`SKILL.md:49`). The repository root currently has modified and untracked files.
2. Before any Phase 1 deploy, list what the image would contain: `git log <commit of the live image>..HEAD`, with the live image identified by `az containerapp show` (`SKILL.md:32`) and the `NIMBUS_BUILD_ID` in the served page. The owner accepts each date-moving item in that list.
3. Code on `main` that moves dates and has already merged needs its own decision before a Phase 1 deploy: OQ28 for Machine Hours (7.8 item 6) and OQ10 for staging.

#### 7.1.2 What actually stops a Send to SAP, and the owner check before any admin presses it

Phase 1 must be live "before the first Send to SAP reaches production" (1.5, 7.8 item 3, OQ10). Nothing in code enforces that order.

- **The code gate is only a role.** The route is `@router.post("/sap/staging/send/{plant}", dependencies=[Depends(require_api_key), Depends(require_admin)])` (`backend/integration/routes.py:875`): an API key, the admin role and plant scope. Inside, the only refusal is an invalid `NIMBUS_SAP_SYSTEM_TZ` (`backend/integration/sap_staging.py:2236-2237`). The default `UTC` is a valid zone, so the unconfirmed default does not stop a Send. No configuration flag or plant flag was found in the route or in `queue_send_to_sap` (`sap_staging.py:2218-2262`).
- **What a click does.** It writes `ready` rows into `sap_stage_planned_order_out` and remembers the sent values in `order_sap_sent`. SAP's dates change only when Mulesoft reads those rows and SAP imports them.
- **The real brake is outside NIMBUS and manual.** The runbook says nothing flows until the Mulesoft role exists, Mulesoft has network access and the poll interval is set (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:35`). The role is created by hand (`migrations/manual/2026-10-08-nimbus-mulesoft-role.sql`, which the deploy runner never applies), its firewall rule belongs to the platform operator, and Mulesoft chooses its own read cadence (`docs/NIMBUS_INTERFACE_ARCHITECTURE.md:619`). The state of all three on the pilot is **[unverified: not visible from the repository; the owner's record says the role and password were created on 2026-10-08 and the firewall addresses, SAP time zone and poll interval were still open]**.

**Owner check before any admin presses Send** (each item answered in writing by one named person):

1. Phase 1 is live on the pilot image: the live `NIMBUS_BUILD_ID` maps to a commit that contains the due-date guard, the corrected echo predicate and the as-sent start baseline (7.3).
2. The as-sent baselines are snapshotted (8.13 step 2) and the snapshot is restorable.
3. `NIMBUS_SAP_SYSTEM_TZ` holds the value SAP Development confirmed, not the default, and the test of assumption A9 (4.13.8: send one unfirmed order, one firmed order and one order whose finish puts SAP's own start in the past, export them from SAP and compare every field; Appendix D) has been run for the pilot plant and answered in writing by SAP Development.
4. The outbound queue is in the expected state: profile Q11d (8.12) reviewed.
5. The read-only Send preview (profile Q11c) has been reviewed: it shows how far the first Send would move SAP's finishes (under today's rule the first Send moves them early where SAP's window is longer than the run time and late where it is shorter, 4.13.7; which case the pilot's planned orders fall in is unprofiled, 2.2).
6. Every admin who can press Send has been told by the owner that the button stays off limits until this check is signed.

Option, not a decision: a code gate, for example a system setting that defaults to off and makes the route refuse for a plant until the owner switches it on. It is a small change, but it is a change, and it would ship in Phase 1.

### 7.2 Phase 0: facts, decisions, profiling (no code)

The owner's tasks for this phase are listed once, in 1.5 (decisions, release mechanism, live image, baseline snapshot, dump and rehearsal, the SAP echo test, the profile queries and where each runs, the caller list, the platform-operator facts, named roles and abort thresholds). They are not repeated here.

Gate: the Phase 1 gate decisions of 1.5 item 1 taken (the Phase 2 gate decisions are decided during Phase 1 and gate Phase 2, not Phase 1); the live image identified; the part 1 rehearsal numbers reviewed by the owner (G-10, part 1); the Appendix D answers (including the A9 test of 4.13.8) given, or accepted by the owner in writing as an assumption before Phase 4 (blocker 18); OQ28 decided (blocker 16). Rollback: not applicable.

### 7.3 Phase 1: protect the due date and retire the rewrite

Why first: O4 is violated by existing code before any new rule exists (the first echo overwrites the due date), the first live Send would make it permanent for every sent order (4.5.3, R6 in section 9), and everything later assumes a due date that means what SAP sent.

Preconditions: a release mechanism (7.1.1) and the owner check of 7.1.2 before any Send. The items below follow the recommendations of OQ23, OQ24, OQ29, OQ30 and OQ31; if the owner decides otherwise the matching item changes.

What ships:

1. **The due-date guard at all write sites** (the order upsert, the child upsert, the distribution header refresh, and the in-memory alternative, 4.5.3), plus the symmetrical as-sent start baseline so that a NIMBUS-derived start can never land in a baseline (4.5.6). A guard at only one writer is not enough (4.7.6, item 3). **The guard cannot reuse the existing echo predicate as it stands.** At SAP-zone midnight the predicate fails on both branches (case M1 of 4.5.5): a placed finish of Thu 22 Oct 19:00 plant-local is sent as Fri 23 Oct 00:00:00 in a UTC SAP zone; SAP returns it; NIMBUS reads it as a date-only value and keeps Fri 00:00; the minute comparison (`db.py:2653`) sets Fri 00:00 against Thu 19:00 and the same-date comparison (`db.py:2655-2659`) sets Fri against Thu, so both fail and a guard built on them would take the echo for a genuine SAP change and overwrite the due date. Phase 1 therefore delivers the rule that 4.5.5 states: detect a date-only value where the time field is blank, before zone conversion, and compare in one frame (the SAP-zone value that was transmitted against the value received). Without it, test group 6's cross-zone case has nothing to pass and the echo-reset half of blocker 7 has no deliverable in any phase. Case M2 (a timed finish that converts to plant-local midnight and is rewritten by hygiene) is covered by item 3.
2. **The distribution baseline-write fixes** (stop writing the as-sent baseline and the due column from the header or the plain order on re-weight, reset, repair and work-center resolve; OQ29). This removes a false reset that already exists (4.7.6).
3. **Hygiene inversion, finish side only:** stop filling a missing finish with the start, stop turning a finish at or before the start or at midnight into start plus run time, apply the date-only rule (OQ23) and the no-usable-finish rule (OQ24) (4.5.6). The start-required rule stays until Phase 2, because the forward path still needs a start.
4. **The client date-only lateness read rule** (the OQ23 recommendation, moved here from Phase 3). Retiring the client rewrite (item 5) removes the value that kept date-only rows from reading as late. `Util.sapDueDate` returns the raw `original_end_date` (`frontend/platform/foundation.mts:611-613`) and `Util.latenessHours` compares the finish with it literally (`foundation.mts:641-647`): for a date-only due of Wed 21 Oct 00:00, an order that ends Wed 18:00 reads 18 hours late (4.6.3). Every row of both sample workbooks is date-only (593 and 328 rows, 8.11). After Phase 1 without this rule every such row reads up to 24 hours late, which is the July 2026 symptom the rewrite was written to hide (4.6.1). The rule ships in the same release as the retirement: read an exact-midnight due as the end of that date's working window at the lateness readers listed in 4.6.3. Two points the OQ23 recommendation leaves open must be settled first: the window on a closed date and on a 24/7 plant, and the fact that a real 00:00:00 cannot be told from "no time" (4.5.5). If the owner ships the retirement without the rule, the interim effect stated above must be announced.
5. **Retire the baseline-correct relay:** the client phase, the relay, the cache restore of the due date, the route, its models, the server function, the tests and the docs (the removal list of 4.6.2); add the due date to `/tasks/refresh`. A stale tab calling the removed route is harmless (8.6, ruling R12 of Appendix C).
6. **Legacy due-date repair, for orders never sent only** (OQ30), run once from the as-sent baseline: only orders with no row in `order_sap_sent`, only where `sap_basic_finish_date` is not NULL and differs from the due date. The restriction matters. The upsert writes the due column and the baseline from the same incoming value (`db.py:2829`, `db.py:2836`), so after an echo the baseline holds NIMBUS's own sent finish, not SAP's original. Repairing a sent order from it would stamp the planner's finish as the due date wherever hygiene or the client rewrite had made the two columns differ, which breaks O4. Sent orders have no recoverable original (4.5.3); they keep their value and are listed for the owner. Profile Q8, joined to the sent table, sizes the repairable set. Without the repair, retiring the client rewrite re-exposes the problem the rewrite was written to hide in July: 609 of 709 live orders then showed a meaningless early-morning due time and were flagged late (4.6.1; a commit-message count, **[unverified: not re-measured]**). The as-sent baseline is NULL for rows written before 2026-10-06 or when SAP sent no finish (6.4), so some rows stay on a fabricated due date until an owner rule covers them.
7. **Independent fixes** that are cheap now and costlier later: the purge preview range (OQ45) and the dead date counters (4.5.14). The Machine Hours handling (OQ28) is not optional: blocker 16 needs OQ28 decided and either the per-row handling shipped or the rule held until it is (7.2, 7.8 item 6).

**What "moves no bar" means.** It holds for orders that have a run time or a stored end: their served end is start plus run time or the stored end (`db.py:212-217`), and Phase 1 touches neither. For an order with a NULL run time and no stored end (routing-held orders have a NULL run time) the served end falls to the last branch of that expression, `basic_finish_date`, which is the column the hygiene inversion and the repair change. Those bars can move at their right edge in Phase 1. Profile Q1 (`has_stored_end` false with `run_time_unknown` true) sizes them; Phase 1 does not start until the owner has seen that number or accepted the exposure.

**Phase 1 is its own release event.** The repair is an UPDATE, so it needs the discipline of Phase 4 at smaller scale:

- A quiet window picked from profile Q12 in plant time, and a notice to save and close tabs. Every row the repair writes gets a new row version (the version is the database's transaction stamp; `db.py:1136` also sets `updated_at`), so a planner with an unsaved edit on a repaired row gets a stale answer on the next Save.
- A snapshot first: `basic_finish_date`, `sap_basic_start_date`, `sap_basic_finish_date` and `order_sap_sent`, in a snapshot file that contains none of the runner's listed words (8.13 step 2). The repair is reversible only from it.
- The runner: the repair file contains UPDATE, so it is blocked unless `-AllowDestructive` is passed, and that flag releases every pending destructive file (8.5). Read each pending file first.
- A ledger-guarded file whose only statement is the repair, named so that it sorts after the snapshot file under any sort (8.13 step 3).
- Where Phase 1 ships no migration (code only), the notice is the only part needed.

What the owner will see: no bar moves for the class above. Lateness figures, the late tile, the planning windows of the optimizer and due-date-mode ties move, because the due date becomes the value SAP sent (4.6.3); the read rule of item 4 keeps date-only rows from reading as up to 24 hours late. This must be announced, or it will be read as a regression (R37 in section 9).

Gate: test groups 6 (including the distribution false-reset case and the cross-zone exact-midnight echo case) and 13 (hygiene part); the flipped hygiene tests (`tests/test_ingest_data_layer.py` hygiene class, `tests/test_sap_staging.py:216`, `286-287`) and the deleted baseline test (`tests/test_ingest_data_layer.py:840-856`); the as-sent baselines snapshotted before the repair and before any Send (8.13 step 2); the owner check of 7.1.2 signed before the first live Send; a release mechanism chosen (7.1.1); OQ23, OQ24, OQ29, OQ30 and OQ31 decided; OQ28 decided and the per-row handling shipped or the rule held (blocker 16). Rollback: the previous image restores the code; rows written by the repair return only from the snapshot. A rollback re-enables the due-date overwrite, the hygiene fabrication and the client rewrite, so if any Send has happened in the interval the overwrite resumes for those orders (R6 in section 9).

What is built:

1. **Placed-finish store and read rule** (OQ32): the stored placed finish wins, and for an order never placed the read rule of 6.2 applies (pending OQ33; start plus run time under the recommended option B); the two end-formula fragments collapse into one and the start fragment becomes shared (4.1.1, 4.1.7); the setup observer, the purge selector, the conflict scan, Send and the running test read the same stored values (4.1.2, 4.5.7). If the owner chooses a new column, its additive migration needs a dedicated run of the deploy runner (8.5).

4. **Manual placement and every run-time trigger path** (the 25 sites of 4.3 and the trigger matrix T1 to T12 of 4.4): the patch functions take a finish; a machine move, a production-version edit or a manual run-time edit holds the finish (OQ7); the reconcile holds the finish, with guards for firm, running, frozen and now (4.4); the mismatch flag redefined (OQ34); an ingest signal for routing-off plants.

### 7.7 Phase 5: Reading B (separately decidable)

Reading B is a separate decision (O1). It depends on Phase 2's server contract, because a just-in-time result has zero slack and any run-time drift converts straight into lateness (5.8). The evidence-backed order is the right-shift post-pass first (about 500 to 650 source lines, 3 to 5 days **[unverified: effort inferred, no prototype]**), which cannot worsen any objective and equals the full backward result in the traced case, and the full just-in-time search only if the owner wants sequence freedom beyond that (3 to 5 weeks plus line parallelism at the 70-line scale, inference, low confidence; 5.3, 5.7). Gate: test groups 20 and 27, the benchmark digests and the performance harness (10.7); OQ9, OQ48, OQ49 and OQ60. Rollback: switch the option or mode off; finishes already stored stay.

## 8. Global cutover plan

### 8.1 What "identity-preserving" means

Notation for this section: a bare R followed by a number (R1 to R12) names a ruling of the cutover adjudication (Appendix C, items 23 to 34), not a risk id of section 9; a risk is always written "R" with its section 9 row (for example "R6 in section 9").

Decision O3 replaces every forward placement path in one release for all plants at once. The question this section answers is what happens to the orders that already exist on that day. "Identity-preserving" means: at cutover, each existing order's **placed finish** is set to the finish the planner sees today, so that no bar moves, no lateness figure changes, and the finish that Send to SAP would transmit is the same as before the release, for placed rows; never-placed rows follow OQ33 (6.2), and under the recommended option B they send nothing until placed. It is the lead recommendation under OQ5 (owner question 5, the cutover rule for every existing slot); this section describes what it can and cannot deliver and what it costs. It does not decide OQ5.

Why it is not simply "copy the stored end": today the server ignores the stored `scheduled_end` whenever an order has a run time. It computes the finish as start + run time (elapsed hours, no calendar). So the stored end of an existing order is a historical leftover, not the finish anyone sees. Example: a planner dragged an order on 2026-09-02 when its run time was 6 h, so the browser saved start Mon 06:00 and end Mon 12:00. Run time was later raised to 8 h by a routing change. The board shows Mon 06:00 to Mon 14:00 (start + 8 h); the stored end still says 12:00. The identity cutover must write 14:00, not keep 12:00, otherwise the bar shrinks on release day.

What the stored end historically means is not knowable from code. Five provenance classes exist and none can be told apart per row: the browser's start + duration at save time (stale after a later run-time change); the width of an edge-resize that the read side ignored; a flat SAP-window width from the first pilot days; a split order's segment envelope; and rows saved before 2026-07-07 with a client time-zone shift. Writers of the stored end: the save path (`db.py:1107-1112`), the distribution anchor carry (`backend/distribution/data.py:1457-1461`) and the collapse copy (`data.py:2839-2840`); NULL writers are the SAP-change reset (`db.py:3663-3667`), the routing hold, the zero-open-quantity flag and queued saves (R: ADJ-WS15 Q15.2; BLIND-WS15). Its content on live data is **[unverified: needs the owner to run profile Q2/Q2b]**. Consequence: the only trustworthy anchor at cutover is the finish the server serves today (R: ADJ-WS01 variant V1/V2), rewritten over the stored value.

**Rows saved before 2026-07-07 carry a shifted pair, and the identity rule freezes it.** The fifth provenance class above has a consequence beyond the stored end. `docs/MIGRATION.md:984-989` says that rows persisted before the save fix by a non-UTC client are shifted by that client's offset, that the offset was not recorded so no per-row correction exists, and that any correction would be a separate, explicitly approved one-off migration against a backup. The identity cutover takes the served finish as the anchor (the paragraph above), so for those rows it writes the shifted finish as the placed finish, and the first Send transmits it. Phase 1's repair does not touch them (they hold a planner start or end, not a fabricated due date). The window is short: the pilot went live on 2026-06-30 and the fix landed on 2026-07-07, so only edits made in that week by a non-UTC editor can be shifted **[unverified: the roll date of the first image that carried the fix; the cut-off in profile Q14 must be set to it]**. Profile Q14 (8.12) counts rows with planner dates whose last write predates the fix. It undercounts, because any later write to a row (a re-upload, a firm toggle) moves `updated_at` and leaves the stored dates as they were. If Q14 is non-zero the owner decides one of: accept the shifted dates (the planners re-place the few affected bars); or correct them by a separate approved file before the cutover, assuming a single site offset as `docs/MIGRATION.md:986-987` describes (an extra step in 8.13 step 3). The document does not choose.

### 8.2 Which row classes a SQL migration can and cannot preserve

A single ledger-guarded SQL migration can make identity for every order that has a stored planner start and is not queued, split or flagged (R1). It cannot for orders that were never placed, because the Gantt shows a calendar-dependent browser snap for those rows and SQL has no calendar (no calendar-aware helper exists in `db.py`, `brain.py`, `master_data.py` or `backend/`; GAP07-7).

| Row class | Identity by SQL? | Why | Anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Queued (Needs Planning) | Nothing to preserve | A database rule forbids stored dates on queued rows; a write raises error 23514 and aborts the whole migration file | `schema.sql:1969-1976`; `db.py:553-554` |
| Split, 2+ segments | Already identity | Served end is the last segment end; the save path stores the envelope in the parent and rejects a disagreeing parent edge | `db.py:554`, `1533-1537`, `1543-1549` |
| Placed (stored start), run time > 0, not flagged, not split, target finish after stored start | **Yes** (the only class where server value = Gantt value) | Planner-placed rows skip the browser snap | `db.py:212-217`; `persistence.mts:953` |
| Placed, run time 0, or target not after stored start | No write possible | The range check would reject it; served end is already at or before the start | `schema.sql:94-97` |
| Placed, run time unknown, stored end present | Already identity | The effective end falls through to the stored end | `db.py:212-217` |
| Placed, run time unknown, no stored end | Writable, rare | The SAP finish becomes the stored end if after the start | profile Q7 |
| Mismatch-flagged (placed) | Not needed on the server; **not identity on the Gantt** | Server already serves the stored end; the browser regenerates the bar from its start on every calendar load and marks it dirty, so "today's Gantt" is calendar-computed | `db.py:258-263`; `engine.mts:1259-1268`, `2777-2781` |
| Hybrid: stored end, no stored start | Writable (the range check is vacuous), already counted as user-scheduled | Excluded by one report for caution, counted by the other; owner may include after profiling | `schema.sql:94-97`; `db.py:559` |
| **Never placed** ("SAP slot": no stored start or end, no segments, not queued) | **No** | Gantt shows a client snap (changes whenever a calendar changes); writing any stored date here would also flip the "user-scheduled" flag, switching the browser snap off, flipping the resolver re-place test (`resolver.py:675-679`), the upsert rule (`db.py:2849-2850`) and running protection (`db.py:3655`) | `db.py:559`; `persistence.mts:953`, `975-977` |

**Merged exclusion list (E1 to E9).** The identity write touches only the stored finish (truncated to the second) and `updated_at`. It never writes `scheduled_start`, `basic_*`, `sap_basic_*`, run time fields, the mismatch flag, segments, the sent-to-SAP memory, `manual_firmed` or planning fields (R2). E1 to E9 are all part of the predicate; E9 was a note in the first draft and Appendix C ruling 24 already counts it.
