### 8.3 Never-placed rows need a read-time fallback (options raised, no decision)

Because SQL cannot reproduce the browser snap, identity for never-placed rows can only come from a rule the new read path applies when no placed finish is stored. Who is affected: a never-placed row is any SAP-sourced order nobody has dragged. The browser today snaps only part of that population: those with a machine, valid dates, not firmed, not split, not flagged, whose served end equals SAP start + run time to the millisecond, and for which `nextAvailable` finds a slot, i.e. run time no longer than the longest single working window (GAP07-2, -3, -4). Long orders (longer than the window) and orders with fractional-second run times are never snapped; they show the raw server value. In the COOIS sample (median Machine Hours 281.7 h, 461 of 593 rows at or over 168 h) almost every row is in the unsnapped class; the Sequence_Testing sample (1-3 h) is the snappable class (GAP07-4, -3; R8). Two further facts shape any option: the snapped position is not a pure function of server data (the second load pass starts from the first pass's result, so two planners with different cached hours can see different bars for the same order, GAP07-5), and today's bar and today's Send value already disagree for snapped rows (GAP07-7).

Shared example E1 (short, snappable): line open Mon-Fri 07:00-19:00; SAP start Thu 2026-04-30 00:00, run time 2.0 h, date-only SAP finish. Today: bar 07:00-09:00, Send queues 02:00, lateness 0. Shared example E2 (long): order 1976489455, start 2026-07-05 00:00, run time 283.436 h. Today: bar 07-05 00:00 to 07-16 19:26:09 (wire-truncated), Send the same value.

| Option raised | Fallback placed finish for a never-placed row | E1 bar | E2 bar | Lateness | Send value | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | The due date (SAP finish as stored), start derived backward | Before the due-date client rewrite: end 02:00 (equals today's served end, not today's snapped bar). After a planner's first load rewrote the due date to 19:00: 17:00-19:00 elapsed, +10 h right of today's 07:00-09:00 | End = rewritten due date (Mon 07-06 19:00); start about Wed 2026-06-24 23:34, roughly 10 days left of today's bar | End = due for every such row, so 0 for all (today E2 shows about 264 h) | The due date as stored instead of today's start + run time | Identity only for rows still holding the hygiene value; the as-sent finish is recoverable only from the baseline column for never-echoed rows (R5) |
| B | SAP start + run time computed at read time (today's served end) | 00:00-02:00 if the walk is elapsed (moves 7 h left, outside shifts, would raise an out-of-hours alert); if calendar-aware, Wed 04-29 17:00-19:00 with the finish in closed time | Identical to today | Same as today for unsnapped rows, smaller for snapped by the snap delta | B1 (recommended): nothing until the row has a placed finish; B2: identical to today for every never-placed row | Identity for the bar of every unsnapped row; the snapped class shifts to the unsnapped value; Send is B1 or B2 (6.2) |
| C | Keep the browser snap as the fallback | Identical to today (history-dependent) | Identical (unsnapped) | Same as today | Server and Send still differ for snapped rows (bar 09:00, Send 02:00) | Keeps a forward, start-anchored walk alive, which O3 says to replace; the first save by any planner writes that tab's snapped values as a placed finish (GAP07-6) |
| D | Client-assisted freeze: dirty-mark every snapped row and save once per plant | Writes per-tab snapped values | Not snapped, written as served | n/a | Becomes stored | Needs an authorized planner session per plant; one unchunked POST; flips the user-scheduled flag, the resolver predicate and running protection for every row written; nothing triggers it today |
| E | Compute the snap in SQL or Python | not available | not available | | | No server calendar exists (GAP07-7) |

Anchors: GAP07-1 to -11; `db.py:4005-4012`, `persistence.mts:1077-1099`, `calendar-engine.mts:256-322`, `sap_staging.py:2210-2211`. A further fact for any option: once any planner action dirties a never-placed row (a post-load snap move, a drag, an alert Fix, an optimizer Apply, a machine or production-version edit, or even a firm toggle), the next explicit Save stores that tab's start and finish and the row becomes a placed row (GAP07-6, TL4; the scheduling `CLAUDE.md` statement that a firm-only row sends only the firm flag is not what the snapshot code does).

### 8.4 The write precision rule, version consequence and old-code neutrality

**Precision rule (R10).** The wire carries second precision (`backend/scheduling/routes.py:194`, the browser save writes seconds), but run time is a decimal number of hours. A fractional run time makes start + run time carry fractions of a second. The identity write and its "already identical" test must both use the finish truncated to the second. Example: run time 0.354 h from 00:00 is 00:21:14.4 on the server, 00:21:14 on the wire; an untruncated write would store a value no planner saw, and an untruncated equality would never match a stored second-precision value, touching rows that need no change.

**Version consequence.** Every row the write touches gets a new row version (`base_version` is the database's transaction stamp). Any planner with unsaved edits to those rows gets a "stale" answer on the next Save and loses the local edit; the browser's cached-edit overlay skips rows whose version moved (`persistence.mts:885`). The exclusion E8 keeps untouched rows out of this. Re-running the migration through its ledger does nothing the second time.

**Neutrality for old code during the migration-before-roll window (R11).** For the restricted write set (a stored start is required, so the user-scheduled flag does not change) old code displays the same finish. Three old-code readers of the stored end see a difference for rows written: the by-date purge selector (`db.py:1829`, membership near range edges can change), the SAP-change slot-echo test (`db.py:2641-2642`; a row whose stored end was NULL becomes eligible, harmless), and the diagnostics date range (`db.py:2189`). An unrestricted write that included never-placed rows would flip the user-scheduled flag and stop old tabs snapping them, a visible bar move.

**Re-purpose or new column.** If the placed finish lives in the existing stored-end column, the migration writes that column and no schema change is needed; if it gets its own column, the same predicate targets the new column, an additive ALTER trips the runner's filter (8.5), and the existing range check does not cover the new column (R4). Either way every end-formula copy still changes (`db.py:212`, `258`, `1049`, `1056`, `1282`; `backend/distribution/data.py:2457`, `3027`; `sap_staging.py:2211`; independent copy `backend/setup/data.py:497-511`). Section 6 owns that choice.

### 8.5 The deploy runner, `-AllowDestructive`, and the range check

| Fact | Mechanism | Anchor |
|---|---|---|
| Destructive test | Regex over the whole file text, case-insensitive: ALTER, DROP, DELETE, UPDATE, TRUNCATE, RENAME, GRANT, REVOKE. Comments and string literals count; `updated_at` does not match (word boundary), but the word "update" in a comment does | `.claude/skills/promote-azure/scripts/apply-migrations.ps1:67`, `74-76` |
| Release | `-AllowDestructive` is one switch for the whole invocation; it releases **every** pending file that matches, not only the intended one. Already-applied files are skipped first, so the flag cannot re-run old files | same script, loop near `122-135` |
| Apply | Each file runs in one transaction together with its own ledger row; any error rolls the file back and stops the run | script `:137`; `schema.sql` is refused outright (`:129`) |
| Location | The runner lists `migrations/` non-recursively, so `migrations/manual/` is never auto-applied | script; `tests/test_schema_idempotent.py:113-121` pins the exact contents of `manual/` |
| Dry run | `-DryRun` (no database connection) lists **every** `*.sql` file in `migrations/`, applied or not, in apply order, labelled "additive (auto)" or "DESTRUCTIVE -> blocked unless -AllowDestructive"; its last line says that at real apply time only files not in the ledger will run. It never reads the ledger, so **it cannot show the release set**: today it lists 36 files, 30 of which match the destructive text test | script `:80-92` |
| Ledger | The data change is double-recorded: a named id in `schema_migrations` and the filename in `migration_files_applied`; precedent `migrations/2026-09-25-routing-production-version-backfill.sql:11-19` | ADJ-WS15 Q15.1 |

| Fact | Mechanism | Anchor |
|---|---|---|
| Pending set | The ledger is `migration_files_applied` (file name, `applied_at`), created by the runner and absent from `schema.sql`. Pending files are the dry-run list minus the ledger's file names. A read-only query gives the second list: `SELECT filename, applied_at FROM migration_files_applied ORDER BY filename;` (profile Q0 reads its tail). The operator compares the two lists before passing the flag | script `:109-114`, `:123-125` |
| A blocked file does not stop the run | A destructive file without the flag is skipped with a warning and the loop continues: later additive files are applied, and the run exits 3 at the end. A blocked cutover UPDATE therefore does not prevent a later additive file from applying before it. Treat exit code 3 as "stop and read the summary" | script `:131-134`, `:151` |
| File order | The runner sorts with `Sort-Object Name` (`:71`); the CI smoke script sorts with Python's `sorted` (`scripts/schema_bootstrap_smoke.py:302`); the repository has already been caught once by the `-` before `.` trap (`migrations/2026-09-26-orders-run-time-bounds-validate.sql:3-10`). Three files are needed in a fixed order, snapshot then column then identity, so name them with a calendar date later than every existing file or with an explicit numeric stem (for example `<date>-1-order-snapshot.sql`, `<date>-2-placed-finish-column.sql`, `<date>-3-identity.sql`), and confirm the order with `-DryRun`, which prints apply order | script `:71`, `:83`; smoke `:302` |
| Defaults point at the live pilot | The connection parameters default to the pilot host and the pilot admin user, and the connection string requires SSL, so a rehearsal against a local copy must pass `-PgHost`, `-Port`, `-Database` and `-User` explicitly | script `:56-59`, `:68` |

Consequences: the cutover UPDATE and any new column (ALTER) are "destructive" by text; read every pending file before passing the flag; a snapshot file consisting only of create-table-as-select or insert statements with none of the listed words anywhere (comments included) would pass unattended; choosing the manual folder for the cutover SQL edits the pinned test and the bootstrap smoke script.

**The range check exists only in `schema.sql`.** `schema.sql:94-97` drops and re-adds `chk_orders_sched_range` as "not valid"; no file in `migrations/` mentions it. Inference (high confidence, nothing in the repo proves it): the pilot database was bootstrapped with `schema.sql` on 2026-06-30 and carries it unvalidated (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:135-137`); profile Q0 reads its validation flag. A not-valid constraint is still checked on every UPDATE of a row (E7). A new placed-finish column would not be covered; it needs its own check and a validating step in a later-dated file, following the 2026-09-25/26 pair. A database built only from `migrations/` would lack the constraint (test databases differ, low).

### 8.6 First-load client paths, and what must be dead server-side first

On the first page load after cutover the browser runs four paths that re-derive or rewrite dates. Under O3/O4 each must be removed or re-anchored in the same image.

| # | Path | What it does at first load | Must change | Anchor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Placement snap loop | Runs twice per load (before and after calendar hydration); skips queued, firmed, split, flagged and user-scheduled rows; snaps the rest forward and re-derives the end from the snapped start. Post-hydration moves are marked dirty and persist at the next explicit Save; autosave only writes browser storage | Retire or restrict to rows with no placed finish; decide its fate with OQ5 | `persistence.mts:578`, `941-989`; `calendar-sync.mts:250-258`; `application-shell.mts:2257`; `persistence.mts:2012-2016` |
| 2 | Due-date baseline phase | Rewrites each unscheduled order's due date to the close of the start day's working window and relays it to the server | Remove (O4); the route and database function go with it | `persistence.mts:1099`, `calendar-sync.mts:266`; `backend/scheduling/routes.py:621`; `db.py:1657` |
| 3 | Run-time reconcile | Regenerates every mismatch-flagged order from its start and marks it dirty | Re-anchor on the finish; decide the flag's fate (E3 rows) | `engine.mts:1259-1268`, `2777-2781` |
| 4 | Cache overlay | Skips rows whose version moved, replays the rest, including a cached client-rewritten due date | Add a discard on the online load path, or tighten the overlay | `persistence.mts:541-568`, `884-891` |

**What must be dead server-side first (R12).** The migration runs before the image roll, so "dead before any data step" is impossible and unnecessary. The hazard is a stale tab posting a baseline correction after the new server is live while rows still have a raw shape; refusing the route **in the same image** closes it. Rows the migration touched are protected by the version pin (an accident of the pin, not a design). Before the roll the route is today's behaviour and not a new hazard. Related server-side items named by the blind pass (BLIND-WS15 Q15.4): the mismatch-flag path and the save-shape gate must be handled in the same image; the save path must accept a placed finish (both edges or segments, with a seconds tolerance). What exactly changes in each is decided in sections 4.1 and 4.4.

**`Config.SCHEMA_VERSION` does not flush the online cache (GAP07-13; this corrects ADJ-WS15's Q15.4 wording).** The version comparison lives only in the offline fallback `_loadCache()` (`persistence.mts:1210-1214`, called only when the backend is unreachable, `:670`). The normal `load()` reads the same browser-storage key with no version check and replays the user-move overlay (`:541-568`). A bump therefore does not stop pre-cutover unsaved edits from replaying where the version still matches, and an already-open tab never re-reads the constant. **No client-version gate exists** anywhere on the server: no middleware reads a client build, `/health` and the `/tasks` metadata carry no build id (GAP07-12; `brain.py` middleware inventory; grep of `build_id` finds only the frontend log sink, `backend/admin_ops/routes.py:419-454`). The page-load cache-bust guard compares a build id once at load (`frontend/app-entry.mjs:132-145`); only `.mjs` files are served no-cache (`brain.py:549-554`); the corporate proxy's URL-keyed caching can serve a pre-roll page (root `CLAUDE.md`).

#### 8.6a Does the cutover image bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`? (a decision to state, with its consequences)

The constant is 6 (`frontend/platform/foundation.mts:144`; its comment says to bump it whenever the saved cache fields change; the storage key itself must not change, `:143`). `_loadCache()` discards a cache whose `_schemaVersion` differs from it (`frontend/scheduling/persistence.mts:1210-1215`), and the function is read only when the backend is unreachable (`:670`); once the backend returns, the page reloads from the server (`:798`). A bump therefore matters in exactly two situations:

- **During the roll.** The backend is briefly unreachable and a tab falls back to its cache. Without a bump, a tab running the new build accepts a cache written by the old build (same version) and replays pre-cutover dates. With a bump the cache is discarded and the tab loads from the server once it is back.
- **After a rollback.** Old code (version 6) meets a cache written by the new build. With a bump (version 7) the old build discards it. Without a bump the old build reads a cache whose fields have the new shape.

Options for the code team and owner (not decided): (a) bump in the cutover image, at the price that every planner loses the offline fallback once; (b) do not bump and rely on the online-path discard of 8.13 step 4, which cannot help the offline fallback. A bump never flushes the online path (the paragraph above), so it complements the online discard and does not replace it. A tab that is already open never re-reads the constant.

### 8.7 Stale-tab hazards

An open planner tab contacts the server only on Save, reload, plant switch, optimize, calendar load or manual refresh; nothing polls and the shell has no "new version available" element (GAP07-16). Protection that exists: the version pin on save and on the baseline relay; the "stale" reconcile; the overlay's version skip; the unsaved badge. Rows the cutover did not touch keep their old version, so the pin does not stop old tabs from writing to them.

| Old-tab action after cutover | Row class affected | Result | Anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Saves a drag or a post-load snap move | Never-placed, flagged, split, run time 0, hybrid, already identical | Pin passes; server stores the tab's start and an end = start + run time as of that tab's load, which is not the finish a calendar-derived start would produce | `persistence.mts:1416-1417`; `db.py:1107-1112`; `engine.mts:1225-1228` |
| Regenerates a flagged order forward and saves | Flagged (E3) | Finish moves right with the new run time, the opposite of the new rule; the flag clears | `engine.mts:1259-1268`; `db.py:1585` |
| Reloads with cached unsaved edits | Any row whose version still matches | Old client-rewritten due date is replayed, contradicting O4, and saved as a placed finish | `persistence.mts:886-891` |
| Switches to another plant | Raw-shape rows of that plant | Runs the old load, snap, baseline relay and reconcile against the new server; closed only by refusing the route in the new image | `application-shell.mts:2128`; R12 |
| Toggles a firm flag then Saves | Never-placed | Writes the tab's snapped dates (a firm-only row still sends start and end) | `db.py:1355`, `1107-1112` |

Mitigation is operational (planners Save and close tabs; one quiet window) or a new mechanism (version gate); neither exists. **[unverified: whether the proxy re-serves a stale `index.html` after the roll.]**

#### 8.7a Persisted Time Machine snapshots survive the cutover

Each browser keeps up to 200 Time Machine snapshots in IndexedDB (database `nimbus-intel`, store `snapshots`: `frontend/nimbus-intelligence.js:386-396`; cap `TM_MAX_SNAPSHOTS = 200`, `:1333`; loaded at start-up, `:1357`). Each snapshot stores every task's `start_date` and `end_date` (`:1368-1372`). They are separate from the cache of 8.6a, so `SCHEMA_VERSION` does not touch them, and the identity migration cannot reach them (they live in the planner's browser, not on the server). A planner can restore a snapshot taken before the cutover; the restore puts forward-rule start and end pairs back on the board, and a Save then writes them as a placed finish. Example: a planner restores "Data loaded" from the week before; the bars return to start-anchored positions with ends of start plus the run time of that day; Save stores those ends as placed finishes under the new rule.

Options (not decided): (a) accept, and disclose in the planner notice ("do not restore a snapshot dated before the cutover"); (b) have the cutover image clear the `snapshots` store on first load (a code change; the database version would need a bump, or a clear call after open); (c) stamp each snapshot with a rule version and refuse a restore across versions (a code change; old snapshots need a default stamp); (d) ask planners to clear this site's data after the roll (this also discards the cache of 8.6a and any unsaved edit). Option (a) costs nothing and depends on planners reading the notice; (b) and (c) are the only ones that do not.

### 8.8 Rollback reality

| Scenario | What restores | What is lost |
|---|---|---|
| Image fails before any planner saves under the new rule | Previous image tag only (`SKILL.md` step 5); identity-written ends are inert to old code for the restricted write set (8.4) | Nothing visible |
| Planners have saved under the new rule, then image rolls back | Nothing in the database restores | Old code ignores the stored placed finish, shows start + run time and Send transmits that; the placed finish is silently lost to old code; no order-date history exists (the sent-to-SAP table holds only the last finish) |
| Data rollback wanted | A snapshot taken before the migration (none exists in the repo) | Every post-cutover planner edit; the restore is itself an UPDATE (blocked by the runner's text filter, bumps versions) |
| Finishes already sent to SAP | Cannot be recalled | n/a |

No backup or point-in-time-restore procedure is documented: the only mentions are `docs/MIGRATION.md:988`, `1008`, `1091`, `schema.sql:416`, `docs/SAP_STAGING_VALIDATION_PLAN.md:199` (a local rehearsal restore) and an unrelated comment at `db.py:1765`; `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` has none. The cloud platform's own automated backup is a platform feature **[unverified: not visible from the repo; the operator must confirm enablement and retention]**. Under O3 the practical rollback unit is "previous image plus pre-cutover snapshot restore", both manual, the second losing every post-cutover edit. Severity: high.

#### 8.8a The return trip: roll-forward after a rollback, and the outbound queue

The matrix above is the one-way case, new code then old code. Two things were missing.

**Roll-forward.** While old code is back, planners' saves write only the legacy start and end columns, because old code does not know a placed-finish column; the new column keeps the value it had at the moment of rollback. When new code returns, the read rule says the placed finish wins (4.1.2), so the stale column silently overrides the fresher legacy edits made in between. The one-time identity write cannot repair this: its named id is spent in `schema_migrations` (the rule that one-time data changes are ledger-guarded is stated at `schema.sql:10-18`) and its file name is recorded in `migration_files_applied`, which the runner skips (`apply-migrations.ps1:130`). Under the re-purpose option (no new column) there is no second column to go stale, but old code's saves overwrite the one stored end with old meaning, which is the "silently lost" row of the matrix. Options for the operator before new code returns (none decided): (a) a new dated, ledger-guarded "re-identity" file with a new id that rewrites the placed-finish column from the served finish for rows whose `updated_at` is later than the rollback time (old code's saves set `updated_at`, `db.py:1136`); (b) set the column to NULL for those rows so they fall back as OQ32 and OQ33 decide; (c) restore the pre-cutover snapshot, which loses every edit since. All three start from the same step: record the rollback timestamp when the image is rolled back.

**The outbound queue on rollback.** Rows queued under the new rule (a Send pressed during the window) stay `ready` after an image rollback and Mulesoft reads them; old code would then send a different finish for the same order at the next Send. Retire them as in 8.13 step 1 before or at the rollback. Rows already `sent` cannot be recalled (matrix row 4).

### 8.9 Ship with or after SAP staging, and the Machine Hours third event

Three date-moving events are pending and none has run on the live data: (1) the cutover; (2) the first planned-order apply per plant from SAP staging; (3) the first Excel re-upload after the Machine Hours rule (commit `621f81f`, pushed to remote main 2026-10-13, not deployed per the owner record **[unverified: the 2026-10-13 v113 roll was built from `757dd86`, which contains the staging code; the owner must confirm which image is live]**), which rewrites run time on routing-off plants for every row whose Machine Hours differ from the stored run time, bumps every such row's version, and widens bars to the right; it has no 168 h clamp, and the 168 h database bound fails a 500-row chunk with a bare HTTP 400 while earlier chunks stay committed (GAP01-3, -9; WS15-15, -18).

SAP staging code ships dormant in one respect only: the poll interval defaults to 0 (`brain.py:430`). Apply and Send are manual and admin-gated by the routes themselves (apply at `backend/integration/routes.py:771-772`, Send at `routes.py:875`, each an API key plus the admin role), but nothing in the deployed code keeps them off (7.1.2), and a poll with an object on automatic apply can apply a validated batch on its own (`backend/integration/sap_staging.py:829-832`). The first apply per plant rewrites the SAP date columns, fills the as-sent baselines, moves every row's version, runs the slot reset (`db.py:3663-3667`) on every order whose baseline differs from SAP's incoming dates (keeping running orders) and removes in-horizon vanished orders. The decision that matters is the order of the first apply per plant versus the cutover, not the order of shipping code (R7).

| Order | What happens | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Cutover first, staging enabled later | No bar moves at deploy (identity); at each plant's first apply the reset nulls the stored placed finish wherever SAP's dates differ, so those orders fall back to the never-placed read (SAP start plus run time, OQ33 B1) and send nothing until placed again: the deliberate move happens once per plant at staging enablement for firmed orders and orders SAP's planning run leaves alone; for unfirmed orders it recurs at each weekly planning run (4.13.1) | The due-date restore source is populated by that apply but is the as-sent finish only until the first Send and echo (R5) |
| Staging first, cutover later | Apply and reset run under the forward rule; the cutover then freezes the post-reset state (two transitions, the second preserving the first); Sends in the interval send start + run time and rely on the finish-only echo rule | Two windows |
| Same shift | One quiet window | Movement from the three events is unattributable |

Staging apply on a plant also requires routing runtime to be on (design D23). An owner edit to `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` (committed as `0317dd8` after the investigation began) says "confirmed 2026-10-13 on the v113 roll" (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:197`), so an image was rolled on 2026-10-13; what it contains, and whether the staging-writing code is already live, is **[unverified: ADJ-WS15 treated the image rollout as unchecked]**. This is evidence for OQ10; no decision is implied.

### 8.10 Distribution families at cutover (GAP11 Part 2)

New children copy the parent's SAP start and finish and receive only their share of run time, with no stored schedule (`backend/distribution/data.py:784-786`, `1419-1423`). An untouched family is therefore start-aligned: one shared start, ends spread by run time. After an identity cutover no sibling is made equal to another: each keeps the finish it shows today (never-placed children via the read-time fallback; placed children via the write).

| Family state (60/40 split of 1,000 units, SAP start Mon 2026-10-19 06:00, SAP finish Fri 10-23 16:00, run times 6 h and 8 h, hours Mon-Fri 06:00-22:00, now Tue 2026-10-13) | Child bars | Send to SAP |
|---|---|---|
| Untouched today (and after identity cutover; nothing written) | C1 Mon 06:00-12:00; C2 Mon 06:00-14:00 | Today's code would report Mon 14:00, 98 h before SAP's own finish (regime-dependent: here SAP's window is longer than the run time; where it is shorter the first Send moves SAP's finish later, 4.13.7); under the new rule (OQ33 B1) an unplaced child sends nothing until placed |
| After identity cutover, then re-weight to 50/50 (5 h and 10 h), finishes held | C1 Mon 07:00-12:00; C2 starts Fri 2026-10-16 20:00, ends Mon 14:00 | Mon 14:00 unchanged |
| New family under Reading A, shared finish = due date | C1 Fri 10:00-16:00; C2 Fri 08:00-16:00 | Fri 16:00 (the due date) |
| Flagged child (re-weight raised its run time to 10 h) | Aggregate route shows Mon 16:00 (start + 10 h); Send and write response show the stale stored Mon 14:00 | Mon 14:00 |

Reading for the owner: the "leave spread" rule moves nothing at cutover but leaves old families compressed (permanently only for firmed families: an unfirmed family is replaced by SAP's weekly planning run and starts again from the default within a week, 4.13.1; today's code sends the earliest-possible finish, not the due date, while under OQ33 B1 an unplaced child sends nothing until placed; and a later share increase pushes a child's derived start days to the left of the family); a "re-align at cutover" rule would move every unplaced old bar from Monday to Friday (about 4 days) and the finish a Send reports by +98 h (from today's Mon 14:00), and cannot touch placed, running or firmed children without overriding planner intent (OQ3, OQ4, OQ11). The header's two date columns stay as the SAP window (nothing a planner does writes them). The aggregate route reads the plain end while Send and write responses read the flag-aware end, so one flagged child makes them disagree; an end-formula qualifier list at `data.py:2456` hard-codes five column names and must be extended if a new column enters the formula (GAP11-4, TL1). The first-draft family query (Q10) needs the correction given in 8.12.

### 8.11 Sample-workbook numbers

Both samples carry only date-only finishes (midnight); neither has a time-precise finish. Independent re-profile (R8):

| Figure | COOIS extract (sheet `Cleaned`) | Sequence_Testing |
|---|---|---|
| Rows | 593 | 328 |
| Finish at midnight | 593 | 328 (start also midnight) |
| Finish == start | 26 | **328 (all)** |
| Machine Hours / Run Time | min 0.354, median 281.670, max 595.268; 461 rows at or over 168 h | Run Time 1.0-3.0 h, median 2.0 |
| Median span (finish - start) | 144.0 h (6 days) | 0 |
| Span shorter than Machine Hours | **585 of 593** (a derived start before the SAP start under an elapsed backward walk) | n/a |
| Derived start before 2026-10-13 among 507 rows with SAP finish on or after that date | 9 | n/a |

Worked examples (corrected): order 1974495910, Machine Hours 38.492: forward finish 2026-07-05 14:29:31 against a backward start 2026-07-03 09:30:29, 14.5 h before the SAP start. Order 1976489455, Machine Hours **283.436** (the earlier report's 595.447 appears in no row): forward finish 2026-07-16 19:26:10, backward start 2026-06-30 04:33:50 from the SAP finish 2026-07-12, i.e. 115.4 h (4.8 days) before the SAP start. Caveats: the figures use the as-sent finish; the stored due date after hygiene is start + run time and after the client rewrite the close of the start day's shift, so a live database may not hold these finishes; the file is a stale extract dated 2026-08-17 (starts 2026-07-04 to 2027-12-11; 91 starts and 86 finishes already before 2026-10-13), so any reversal count from it understates reality; the `Raw` sheet holds invalid date serials and is not ingest-ready. That the COOIS Machine Hours look like sums across parallel machines (span / Machine Hours about 0.5) is an inference only **[unverified: the Machine Hours unit needs SAP Development]**. Machine Hours up to 595 h exceed the 168 h run-time bound: 461 of 593 rows would hit it on a routing-off plant.

### 8.12 Profiling SQL for the owner (SELECT-only; never executed by the fleet)

Merged from the two cutover reports and adjudicated (ADJ-WS15 "Profiling SQL"), then corrected after the second review. Run each block against the pilot database inside its own read-only transaction (`BEGIN READ ONLY; <block>; ROLLBACK;`), one plant at a time where noted, preferably on the restored pilot copy of 8.13 step 0a so the live database carries no load.

**One block per transaction.** In Postgres a failing statement aborts the rest of its transaction, and several of these objects may be absent: `migration_files_applied` is created by the deploy runner and is not in `schema.sql`; `schema_migrations` once had a filename-keyed shape with no `id` column on the live database (`apply-migrations.ps1:24-29`); `order_sap_sent` and the staging tables exist only after the staging migrations. A missing object must not hide the other results. The base block is a `WITH` prefix: paste it above every query marked "needs the base"; a query that starts with a comma continues that `WITH` list.

Order timestamps are naive plant-local. `updated_at` is a naive timestamp stamped by `NOW()` in the database session time zone (`schema.sql:58`, `db.py:1136`), so Q12 converts it. "Now" is converted with the plant's time zone; frozen is approximated (no roll hour). If Q0 shows a column missing (for example the SAP baseline columns), drop that column from the base block. Changes since the first version are marked `-- CHANGED`: the base block (two columns added), Q0, Q7 (class `09b` for E9), Q7b, Q8, Q10, Q11 (now Q11a to Q11e), Q12, and the new Q13 to Q17 (Q15 to Q17 were added by the fix pass after the second review). Every statement is SELECT-only and uses only columns that exist in `schema.sql` (each was checked against it); none has been executed.

```sql
-- ===== Q0  Environment (each statement is its own block; no base needed) =====
SELECT current_database(), now(), current_setting('TimeZone') AS db_session_timezone;          -- CHANGED: the zone updated_at is stamped in
SELECT to_regclass('order_sap_sent') AS order_sap_sent, to_regclass('sap_stage_planned_order_out') AS outbound_queue,
       to_regclass('sap_stage_batch') AS stage_batch, to_regclass('migration_files_applied') AS file_ledger,
       to_regclass('machine_calendar') AS machine_calendar;                                      -- CHANGED: which objects exist
SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns
 WHERE table_schema = current_schema() AND table_name = 'orders' AND column_name IN
   ('sap_basic_start_date','sap_basic_finish_date','manual_firmed','planning_status','run_time_source',
    'runtime_schedule_mismatch','parent_production_order','firming_indicator')
 ORDER BY 1;
SELECT conname, convalidated, pg_get_constraintdef(oid)
  FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'orders'::regclass
   AND conname IN ('chk_orders_sched_range','orders_planning_state_check','chk_orders_run_time_bounds');
SELECT filename, applied_at FROM migration_files_applied ORDER BY applied_at DESC LIMIT 15;     -- own block: table is created by the runner
SELECT * FROM schema_migrations LIMIT 50;                                                        -- CHANGED: was SELECT id, applied_at; the live table once had no id column
SELECT plant, routing_runtime_enabled, split_order_policy, frozen_horizon_days,
       visibility_horizon_days, timezone
  FROM plants ORDER BY plant;

-- ===== BASE block (needs the base: paste above every query below that says so) =====
-- Mirrors db.py _ORDERS_SELECT / _EFF_END_SQL (V1) / _EFF_END_WITH_RUNTIME_MISMATCH_SQL (V2).
-- CHANGED: o.production_order AS prod_order and o.material_number AS mat added (Q10, Q11b, Q11c need them).
WITH seg AS (
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS seg_n, MIN(scheduled_start) AS seg_first, MAX(scheduled_end) AS seg_last,
         SUM(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (scheduled_end - scheduled_start)) / 60.0) AS seg_min
    FROM order_schedule_segments GROUP BY order_id
), b AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.production_order AS prod_order, o.material_number AS mat,
         o.plant, o.machine, o.planning_status, o.manual_firmed, o.firming_indicator,
         o.parent_production_order, o.run_time, o.run_time_source,
         COALESCE(o.runtime_schedule_mismatch, FALSE) AS mm,
         o.basic_start_date AS bs, o.basic_finish_date AS bf,
         o.sap_basic_start_date AS sbs, o.sap_basic_finish_date AS sbf,
         o.scheduled_start AS ss, o.scheduled_end AS se, o.updated_at,
         COALESCE(s.seg_n, 0) AS seg_n, s.seg_first, s.seg_last, s.seg_min,
         COALESCE(s.seg_first, o.scheduled_start, o.basic_start_date) AS disp_start,
         COALESCE(o.scheduled_start, o.basic_start_date) + o.run_time * INTERVAL '1 hour' AS start_plus_run,
         -- V1 (plain effective end)
         COALESCE(COALESCE(o.scheduled_start, o.basic_start_date) + o.run_time * INTERVAL '1 hour',
                  o.scheduled_end, o.basic_finish_date) AS eff_end_v1,
         -- what /tasks and Send to SAP serve (segments, mismatch flag, then V1)
         COALESCE(s.seg_last,
                  CASE WHEN COALESCE(o.runtime_schedule_mismatch, FALSE) THEN o.scheduled_end END,
                  COALESCE(o.scheduled_start, o.basic_start_date) + o.run_time * INTERVAL '1 hour',
                  o.scheduled_end, o.basic_finish_date) AS disp_end,
         (now() AT TIME ZONE COALESCE(pl.timezone, 'UTC')) AS now_local,
         pl.frozen_horizon_days
    FROM orders o
    LEFT JOIN seg s ON s.order_id = o.id
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT timezone, frozen_horizon_days FROM plants WHERE plant = o.plant LIMIT 1) pl ON TRUE
   WHERE TRUE /* AND o.plant = '1085' */
)

-- ===== Q1  Population by stored-schedule presence (needs the base) =====
SELECT plant, planning_status, (ss IS NOT NULL) AS has_stored_start, (se IS NOT NULL) AS has_stored_end,
       (seg_n >= 2) AS split_order, (run_time IS NULL) AS run_time_unknown, mm AS mismatch_flag,
       (parent_production_order IS NOT NULL) AS distribution_child, COUNT(*) AS orders
  FROM b GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 ORDER BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8;

-- ===== Q2  Stored end vs V1 end (sizes the provenance classes; needs the base) =====
SELECT plant,
       CASE WHEN planning_status = 'needs_planning'        THEN '0 queued'
            WHEN seg_n >= 2                                 THEN '1 split (stored end = envelope)'
            WHEN se IS NULL                                 THEN '2 no stored end'
            WHEN run_time IS NULL                           THEN '3 run time unknown (stored end IS the end)'
            WHEN mm                                         THEN '4 mismatch flag set (served end = stored end)'
            WHEN abs(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (se - eff_end_v1))) <= 60 THEN '5 stored = start + run time (+-1 min)'
            WHEN se > eff_end_v1                            THEN '6 stored LATER than start + run time'
            ELSE                                                 '7 stored EARLIER than start + run time' END AS relation,
       COUNT(*) AS orders,
       percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (se - eff_end_v1)) / 3600) AS median_diff_h,
       MIN(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (se - eff_end_v1)) / 3600) AS min_diff_h,
       MAX(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (se - eff_end_v1)) / 3600) AS max_diff_h
  FROM b GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;
-- Q2b  histogram of (stored end - (start + run time)) in 4 h buckets for rows with both (needs the base)
SELECT width_bucket(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (se - start_plus_run)) / 3600.0, -48, 48, 24) AS bucket_4h,
       MIN(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (se - start_plus_run)) / 3600.0) AS from_h,
       MAX(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (se - start_plus_run)) / 3600.0) AS to_h, COUNT(*) AS orders
  FROM b WHERE se IS NOT NULL AND start_plus_run IS NOT NULL AND seg_n < 2 AND planning_status <> 'needs_planning'
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

-- ===== Q3  Raw shape of basic_finish_date vs the as-sent baseline (is the due date recoverable? needs the base) =====
SELECT plant,
       CASE WHEN bf IS NULL THEN 'a NULL'
            WHEN bf = bs THEN 'b = start'
            WHEN run_time IS NOT NULL AND bf = bs + run_time * INTERVAL '1 hour' THEN 'c = start + run time'
            WHEN bf = bs + INTERVAL '1 hour' THEN 'd = start + 1 h'
            WHEN bf = date_trunc('day', bf) THEN 'e midnight, other'
            ELSE 'f other (SAP time of day, or client-corrected end of shift)' END AS finish_shape,
       CASE WHEN sbf IS NULL THEN 'baseline NULL (unknown)'
            WHEN sbf = bf THEN 'as-sent = basic'
            WHEN sbf = date_trunc('day', sbf) THEN 'as-sent is date only (midnight)'
            ELSE 'as-sent has a time of day, differs from basic' END AS vs_as_sent,
       COUNT(*) AS orders
  FROM b GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3;
-- Shapes b/c/d are exactly what correct_due_date_baselines (db.py:1757-1773) and the client baseline phase treat as "raw".

-- ===== Q4  Running / frozen (approximation) / firmed (needs the base; depends on now(): run on the live database too) =====
SELECT plant, (planning_status = 'needs_planning') AS queued,
       (disp_start <= now_local AND now_local < disp_end) AS running_now,
       (frozen_horizon_days IS NOT NULL AND frozen_horizon_days > 0
         AND disp_start < (now_local::date + frozen_horizon_days)::timestamp) AS in_frozen_window_approx,
       manual_firmed AS planner_firmed, (COALESCE(firming_indicator, '') <> '') AS sap_firm_flag_display_only,
       COUNT(*) AS orders
  FROM b GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6 ORDER BY 1,2,3,4,5,6;

-- ===== Q5  Segments: counts, parent-vs-envelope, minutes vs run time (needs the base) =====
SELECT seg_n AS segments, COUNT(*) AS orders,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ss IS DISTINCT FROM seg_first) AS parent_start_ne_first,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE se IS DISTINCT FROM seg_last)  AS parent_end_ne_last,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE run_time IS NOT NULL AND abs(seg_min - run_time * 60) > 0.5) AS minutes_ne_runtime,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE seg_n >= 2 AND mm) AS flagged_mismatch
  FROM b WHERE seg_n > 0 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

-- ===== Q6  Served end vs stored due date (how far the Gantt is from basic_finish_date; needs the base) =====
SELECT plant, COUNT(*) AS orders,
       percentile_cont(ARRAY[0.05,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.95]) WITHIN GROUP
         (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (disp_end - bf)) / 3600.0) AS hours_p05_p25_p50_p75_p95,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE disp_end > bf) AS shown_later_than_due,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE disp_end = bf) AS shown_equals_due,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE disp_end < bf) AS shown_earlier_than_due
  FROM b WHERE planning_status <> 'needs_planning' AND bf IS NOT NULL AND disp_end IS NOT NULL
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
-- same against the as-sent finish: replace bf with sbf and add AND sbf IS NOT NULL

-- ===== Q7  Identity-write sizing: every class of R1/R2, counted (needs the base) =====
SELECT CASE
         WHEN planning_status = 'needs_planning'                       THEN '01 queued (E1)'
         WHEN seg_n >= 2                                                THEN '02 split 2+ segments (E2)'
         WHEN mm                                                        THEN '03 mismatch-flagged (E3)'
         WHEN ss IS NULL AND se IS NULL                                 THEN '04 never placed / SAP slot (E4, client snap)'
         WHEN ss IS NULL                                                THEN '05 hybrid: stored end, no stored start (owner decides)'
         WHEN run_time IS NULL AND se IS NOT NULL                       THEN '06 run time NULL, stored end already served (E5)'
         WHEN run_time = 0                                              THEN '07 run time 0 (E6)'
         WHEN eff_end_v1 IS NULL OR eff_end_v1 <= ss                    THEN '08 target not after stored start (E7)'
         WHEN se IS NOT DISTINCT FROM date_trunc('second', eff_end_v1)  THEN '09 already identical (E8)'
         WHEN run_time >= 168                                           THEN '09b run time >= 168 h (E9)'     -- CHANGED: E9 is a class
         ELSE                                                                '10 WOULD WRITE scheduled_end' END AS cls,
       COUNT(*) AS n,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE parent_production_order IS NOT NULL) AS distribution_children,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE manual_firmed) AS manually_firmed,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE disp_start <= now_local AND now_local < disp_end) AS running_now
  FROM b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
-- Q7b  size of the change for the rows that WOULD WRITE (class 10; needs the base)
SELECT plant, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE se IS NULL) AS from_null,
       percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY abs(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (se - eff_end_v1))) / 3600) AS median_abs_change_h,
       MAX(abs(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (se - eff_end_v1))) / 3600) AS max_abs_change_h
  FROM b
 WHERE planning_status <> 'needs_planning' AND seg_n < 2 AND NOT mm AND ss IS NOT NULL
   AND NOT (run_time IS NULL AND se IS NOT NULL) AND run_time IS DISTINCT FROM 0
   AND (run_time IS NULL OR run_time < 168)                                                          -- CHANGED: E9 in the predicate
   AND eff_end_v1 > ss AND se IS DISTINCT FROM date_trunc('second', eff_end_v1)
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC;
-- Q7c  rows already violating chk_orders_sched_range (NOT VALID leftovers; any UPDATE of them re-checks the constraint; no base)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS inverted_rows FROM orders
 WHERE scheduled_start IS NOT NULL AND scheduled_end IS NOT NULL AND scheduled_end <= scheduled_start;

-- ===== Q8  Due-date restore feasibility, joined to the sent table (needs the base) =====
-- CHANGED: "never sent" is now measurable. After an echo the baseline holds NIMBUS's own finish, so only never-sent rows are restorable.
SELECT b.plant, COUNT(*) AS orders,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.order_id IS NULL) AS never_sent,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sbf IS NOT NULL) AS as_sent_finish_present,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sbs IS NOT NULL) AS as_sent_start_present,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.order_id IS NULL AND sbf IS NOT NULL AND bf IS DISTINCT FROM sbf) AS never_sent_restorable_and_different,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.order_id IS NOT NULL AND sbf IS NOT NULL AND bf IS DISTINCT FROM sbf) AS sent_baseline_differs_not_restorable,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sbf IS NOT NULL AND sbf = date_trunc('day', sbf)) AS as_sent_date_only_midnight,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sbf IS NOT NULL AND sbf <= COALESCE(sbs, bs)) AS as_sent_not_after_start,
       MIN(b.updated_at) FILTER (WHERE sbf IS NOT NULL) AS oldest_row_with_baseline,
       MAX(b.updated_at) AS newest_row_write
  FROM b LEFT JOIN order_sap_sent s ON s.order_id = b.id
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

-- ===== Q9  Run time shape (168 h bound, zero, source; needs the base) =====
SELECT run_time_source, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE run_time IS NULL) AS rt_null,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE run_time = 0) AS rt_zero, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE run_time >= 100) AS rt_ge_100,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE run_time >= 168) AS rt_ge_168, MAX(run_time) AS rt_max
  FROM b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC;

-- ===== Q10  Distribution families: shape, class mix, end spread, header gap (runnable; continues the base's WITH list) =====
-- CHANGED: replaces the first-draft query and the unrunnable sketch. A family is plant + parent order + material
-- (header key schema.sql:195). Ends and starts are compared to the minute.
, kids AS (
  SELECT b.*,
         CASE WHEN planning_status = 'needs_planning'  THEN '01'
              WHEN seg_n >= 2                           THEN '02'
              WHEN mm                                   THEN '03'
              WHEN ss IS NULL AND se IS NULL            THEN '04'
              ELSE                                           '05+' END AS cls
    FROM b WHERE parent_production_order IS NOT NULL
), fam AS (
  SELECT plant, parent_production_order AS fam_order, mat,
         COUNT(*) AS children,
         COUNT(DISTINCT date_trunc('minute', disp_end))   FILTER (WHERE planning_status <> 'needs_planning') AS n_ends,
         COUNT(DISTINCT date_trunc('minute', disp_start)) FILTER (WHERE planning_status <> 'needs_planning') AS n_starts,
         MAX(disp_end) FILTER (WHERE planning_status <> 'needs_planning') AS max_end,
         MIN(disp_end) FILTER (WHERE planning_status <> 'needs_planning') AS min_end,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cls = '04')                    AS never_placed,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cls IN ('01','02','03'))       AS excluded_1_3,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE disp_start <= now_local AND now_local < disp_end) AS running,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE manual_firmed)                 AS firmed
    FROM kids GROUP BY plant, parent_production_order, mat
)
SELECT f.plant,
       CASE WHEN f.n_ends = 1 AND f.n_starts = 1 THEN 'both_aligned' WHEN f.n_starts = 1 THEN 'start_aligned'
            WHEN f.n_ends = 1 THEN 'finish_aligned' ELSE 'spread' END AS shape,
       CASE WHEN f.excluded_1_3 > 0 THEN 'has_flagged_split_or_queued' WHEN f.never_placed = f.children THEN 'all_never_placed'
            WHEN f.never_placed = 0 THEN 'all_placed' ELSE 'mixed' END AS class_mix,
       COUNT(*) AS families,
       percentile_cont(ARRAY[0.5,0.95]) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (f.max_end - f.min_end)) / 3600) AS end_spread_h_p50_p95,
       percentile_cont(ARRAY[0.5,0.95]) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (hd.basic_finish_date - f.max_end)) / 3600) AS header_gap_h_p50_p95,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE f.running > 0) AS with_running, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE f.firmed > 0) AS with_firmed
  FROM fam f JOIN order_distribution hd
    ON hd.plant = f.plant AND hd.production_order = f.fam_order AND hd.material_number = f.mat
 WHERE f.n_ends >= 1
 GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3;

-- ===== Q11  SAP staging state, sent-vs-shown, Send preview, outbound queue (empty before the staging release is live; each is its own block) =====
-- Q11a (no base)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS remembered_sends FROM order_sap_sent;
-- Q11b  CHANGED: sent finish is kept to the second (sap_staging.py:2256) and a Send transmits the GROUP's latest end,
--       so compare the truncated group end, not the member's own end (needs the base; continues its WITH list)
, g AS (
  SELECT b.id, b.plant,
         MAX(b.disp_end) FILTER (WHERE b.planning_status <> 'needs_planning' AND b.disp_end IS NOT NULL)
           OVER (PARTITION BY b.plant, COALESCE(b.parent_production_order, b.prod_order), b.mat) AS grp_end
    FROM b
)
SELECT g.plant, COUNT(*) AS orders_sent_once,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.sent_finish = date_trunc('second', g.grp_end)) AS sent_equals_would_send_now,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.sent_finish <> date_trunc('second', g.grp_end)) AS shown_has_moved_since_send
  FROM g JOIN order_sap_sent s ON s.order_id = g.id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
-- Q11c  NEW: read-only Send preview. What one Send per plant would queue, and how far it differs from the as-sent finish.
--       This is the only preview there is (the Send function writes). Needs the base; continues its WITH list.
, grp AS (
  SELECT plant, COALESCE(parent_production_order, prod_order) AS plnum, mat,
         MAX(disp_end) FILTER (WHERE planning_status <> 'needs_planning' AND disp_end IS NOT NULL) AS send_end,
         MAX(sbf) AS sap_finish, COUNT(*) AS members
    FROM b GROUP BY plant, COALESCE(parent_production_order, prod_order), mat
)
SELECT plant, COUNT(*) AS planned_orders_a_send_would_queue,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sap_finish IS NOT NULL AND send_end <> date_trunc('second', sap_finish)) AS differs_from_as_sent_finish,
       percentile_cont(ARRAY[0.05,0.5,0.95]) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (send_end - sap_finish)) / 3600.0)
         FILTER (WHERE sap_finish IS NOT NULL) AS hours_p05_p50_p95_vs_as_sent_finish
  FROM grp WHERE send_end IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
-- Q11d  NEW: outbound queue (no base). Rows still 'ready' are read by Mulesoft at its own cadence (8.13 step 1, gate G-11).
SELECT plant, row_status, COUNT(*) AS queue_rows, MIN(queued_at) AS oldest_queued, MAX(queued_at) AS newest_queued,
       MAX(sent_at) AS last_status_change
  FROM sap_stage_planned_order_out GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;
-- Q11e  (no base)
SELECT object_key, status, COUNT(*) FROM sap_stage_batch GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;
SELECT object_key, apply_mode FROM sap_sync_config ORDER BY 1;

-- ===== Q12  Quiet-window gauge in PLANT time (rows written by plant, weekday and hour, last 14 days; no base) =====
-- CHANGED: updated_at is naive in the database session zone (see Q0); convert to UTC-aware, then to the plant zone.
SELECT x.plant, EXTRACT(dow FROM x.lt) AS dow_plant, EXTRACT(hour FROM x.lt) AS hour_plant, COUNT(*) AS rows_written
  FROM (SELECT o.plant,
               (o.updated_at AT TIME ZONE current_setting('TimeZone')) AT TIME ZONE COALESCE(pl.timezone, 'UTC') AS lt
          FROM orders o
          LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT timezone FROM plants WHERE plant = o.plant LIMIT 1) pl ON TRUE
         WHERE o.updated_at > now() - INTERVAL '14 days') x
 GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_updated_last_24h, MAX(updated_at) AS last_write
  FROM orders WHERE updated_at > now() - INTERVAL '24 hours';

-- ===== Q13  NEW: machines and plants that would derive on the engine default calendar (no base) =====
-- The engine default is Monday to Friday 07:00 to 19:00, weekends off (frontend/platform/foundation.mts:133-134), applied by
-- Store.ensureCalendar for a line with no calendar row and Store.ensurePlant for a plant with none (store.mts:457-465, 494-503).
-- Only machines that have orders are counted.
WITH ord AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT o.plant, o.machine,
         EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM machine_calendar mc
                  WHERE mc.plant = o.plant AND mc.machine = o.machine AND mc.work_hours IS NOT NULL) AS has_line_calendar
    FROM orders o WHERE o.plant IS NOT NULL AND o.machine IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT ord.plant, (pl.work_hours IS NOT NULL) AS plant_has_hours,
       COUNT(*) AS machines_with_orders,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT ord.has_line_calendar) AS machines_without_line_calendar
  FROM ord
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT p.work_hours FROM plants p WHERE p.plant = ord.plant LIMIT 1) pl ON TRUE
 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;

-- ===== Q14  NEW: rows that may carry the pre-2026-07-07 client-offset shift (needs the base) =====
-- docs/MIGRATION.md:984-989. REPLACE the literal with the roll timestamp of the first image that carried the save fix; a later
-- cut-off widens the set. updated_at moves on ANY write, so this undercounts (a re-uploaded row drops out).
SELECT b.plant,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ss IS NOT NULL OR se IS NOT NULL OR seg_n > 0) AS with_planner_dates,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE (ss IS NOT NULL OR se IS NOT NULL OR seg_n > 0)
                          AND b.updated_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-07-07 00:00:00') AS planner_dates_not_rewritten_since_fix,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE (ss IS NOT NULL OR se IS NOT NULL OR seg_n > 0)
                          AND b.updated_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-07-07 00:00:00' AND s.order_id IS NULL) AS of_which_never_sent,
       MIN(b.updated_at) FILTER (WHERE ss IS NOT NULL OR se IS NOT NULL OR seg_n > 0) AS oldest_planner_date_write
  FROM b LEFT JOIN order_sap_sent s ON s.order_id = b.id
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

-- ===== Q15  NEW: plants with no time zone, or a zone Postgres does not recognise (no base; OQ52, 4.13.4 profile P2) =====
-- Each statement below is its own block (its own read-only transaction). Columns: plants.plant, plants.timezone (schema.sql:274).
SELECT COUNT(*) AS plants_total,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE timezone IS NULL OR btrim(timezone) = '') AS plants_with_no_zone,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE timezone IS NOT NULL AND btrim(timezone) <> ''
                          AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_timezone_names n WHERE n.name = plants.timezone)) AS plants_with_unrecognised_zone
  FROM plants;
SELECT p.plant, p.timezone, COUNT(o.id) AS orders
  FROM plants p LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.plant = p.plant
 WHERE p.timezone IS NULL OR btrim(p.timezone) = ''
    OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_timezone_names n WHERE n.name = p.timezone)
 GROUP BY p.plant, p.timezone ORDER BY p.plant;

-- ===== Q16  NEW: overlong orders per line (needs the base; continues its WITH list; OQ50, blocker 3) =====
-- An order is overlong when its run time in hours is longer than the longest single working window of its line.
-- Window source: the line's own row in machine_calendar (schema.sql:1071-1081; work_hours JSON shape {"0".."6": [open_hour, close_hour] | null}),
-- else the engine default of 12 hours (Monday to Friday 07:00 to 19:00; the same default as Q13).
-- Approximations, stated so nobody over-reads the numbers: a window is read as close hour minus open hour inside one day (a window
-- that crosses midnight is read as negative and ignored); the plant-hours clamp on a line is not applied, so a line clamped by
-- narrower plant hours is undercounted. A line with no row of its own in machine_calendar is assumed to use the 12 h engine
-- default even where its plant has its own hours, so such lines may be mislabelled (line_on_engine_default shows which). The split policy is shown because `never` and `overlong_only` treat an overlong order differently.
, cal AS (
  SELECT b.plant, b.machine, b.run_time, pw.split_order_policy,
         (mc.work_hours IS NULL) AS line_on_engine_default,
         CASE WHEN mc.work_hours IS NULL THEN 12
              ELSE (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(e.v) = 'array' AND jsonb_array_length(e.v) = 2
                                     AND jsonb_typeof(e.v -> 0) = 'number' AND jsonb_typeof(e.v -> 1) = 'number'
                                    THEN (e.v ->> 1)::numeric - (e.v ->> 0)::numeric END)
                      FROM jsonb_each(CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(mc.work_hours) = 'object' THEN mc.work_hours ELSE '{}'::jsonb END) AS e(k, v))
         END AS longest_window_h
    FROM b
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT m.work_hours FROM machine_calendar m
                        WHERE m.plant = b.plant AND m.machine = b.machine AND m.work_hours IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1) mc ON TRUE
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT p.split_order_policy FROM plants p WHERE p.plant = b.plant LIMIT 1) pw ON TRUE
   WHERE b.run_time IS NOT NULL AND b.run_time > 0 AND COALESCE(b.planning_status, '') <> 'needs_planning'
)
SELECT plant, machine, MAX(split_order_policy) AS split_policy, BOOL_OR(line_on_engine_default) AS line_on_engine_default,
       MAX(longest_window_h) AS longest_window_h, COUNT(*) AS orders_with_run_time,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE run_time > longest_window_h) AS overlong_orders,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE longest_window_h IS NULL) AS orders_on_a_line_with_no_open_window
  FROM cal GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;

-- ===== Q17  NEW: orders carrying the run-time mismatch flag (needs the base; OQ53, OQ34, 4.4) =====
-- How many orders the cutover would re-derive in bulk, and so how many could reverse at once. Columns from the base block:
-- mm is orders.runtime_schedule_mismatch (schema.sql:50), planning_status, ss, se, seg_n, parent_production_order.
SELECT plant, planning_status, COUNT(*) AS flagged_orders,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ss IS NOT NULL OR se IS NOT NULL OR seg_n > 0) AS flagged_and_planner_placed,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE parent_production_order IS NOT NULL) AS flagged_distribution_children
  FROM b WHERE mm GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;
```

**Corrections and additions recorded after the adjudication and the second review.**

- **Q8 (R3-15):** joined to `order_sap_sent`. Its first version counted rows already echoed as "restorable"; the baseline of a sent order holds NIMBUS's own finish, so only the `never_sent_restorable_and_different` column sizes the Phase 1 repair (7.3 item 6).
- **Q10 (R3-17, GAP11-6):** the first-draft query grouped by plant and parent order only, compared microsecond ends and answered only "do ends differ"; the 8.12 sketch that replaced it had a `<Q7 CASE>` placeholder and a column (`mat`) the base lacked, so neither ran. The version above is complete: one row per plant, family shape (both aligned, start aligned, finish aligned, spread) and class mix, end spread and header-gap percentiles, and running and firmed exposure. Its class labels follow Q7 classes 01 to 04 only; classes 05 and above are folded together. G-2 uses this version.
- **Q11 (R3-16):** the sent finish is kept to the second (`sap_staging.py:2256`), so Q11b truncates, and it compares the group's latest end because a Send transmits one end per planned order and children roll up to the latest (`sap_staging.py:2188-2189`). **Before the first Send `order_sap_sent` is empty, so Q11b returns no rows and gate G-7 passes vacuously**; G-7 means something only after a Send. Q11c is the read-only substitute: it shows how far the first Send would move SAP's finishes, per plant, and is part of the owner check of 7.1.2. Q11d is the outbound queue for G-11.
- **Q7 and E9 (R3-18, R5-27):** E9 is now a Q7 class (`09b`) and part of the Q7b predicate, matching 8.2 and Appendix C ruling 24.
- **Transactions (R3-19):** every block is its own transaction (above); Q0's ledger reads are separate blocks because the runner creates `migration_files_applied` and the live `schema_migrations` once had no `id` column.
- **Q12 (R3-20):** converted to plant time by plant. It still cannot see an open browser tab: a planner who has the board open with an unsaved edit writes nothing until they Save, so the number of open sessions is unknown to every query in this section; the planner notice of 8.13 step 1 is the only control.
- **Q13 (T4, R3-12):** counts machines and plants that would derive on the default. Under O3 every plant goes in at once, so a real 24/7 line with no calendar row would get 12-hour weekday starts and no weekend starts. A non-zero count is a stop for G-2 until the owner has chosen the derived-start rule for such lines (OQ62); this section does not choose it. The time-zone count has its own query, Q15, and G-2 reads both.
- **Q14 (R3-14):** rows with planner dates whose last write predates the 2026-07-07 save fix (8.1).
- **Q15 (OQ52, G-2):** the number of plants with no time zone, and of plants whose zone Postgres does not recognise. OQ52 gates the cutover on the first being zero; it is the same test as profile P2 of 4.13.4 in count form. Columns checked against `schema.sql:274` (`plants.timezone`, nullable).
- **Q16 (OQ50, blocker 3):** overlong orders per line (run time longer than the longest single working window of the line), with the split policy beside each line. It uses the line's own calendar row or the 12-hour engine default, so it carries the approximations written above the query. Columns checked against `schema.sql:1071-1081` (`machine_calendar`) and `schema.sql:293` (`plants.split_order_policy`).
- **Q17 (OQ53, OQ34):** orders with the run-time mismatch flag set, by plant and status. This is the "profiling count" that OQ53 said was missing. Column checked against `schema.sql:50`.
- **Never-placed split (GAP07, Q15.7 addition, described, not written as SQL):** per plant, the count of never-placed rows (Q7 class 04) split by whether run time x 3600 is a whole number of seconds and by whether run time exceeds that plant's longest nominal working window in hours (supply the window per plant, SQL cannot know it). These sizes predict how many never-placed rows the browser snaps at all.
- **Routing-off plants (GAP01):** count orders where Machine Hours > 0 and differs from run time, and orders with Machine Hours >= 168, grouped by plant on routing-off plants; the first re-upload after `621f81f` rewrites the first set, and the second set cannot be uploaded.
- **Not answerable by SQL:** the Gantt's snapped start and end for never-placed rows, the number of open browser sessions, whether Mulesoft has read an outbound row (only its `row_status` update shows it, and only if Mulesoft writes status back, `docs/NIMBUS_INTERFACE_ARCHITECTURE.md:615`), and anything inside the segment table beyond what Q5 reads.

### 8.13 Runbook (evidence for the migration, not a decision)

Every step is conditional on OQ5 (cutover rule and never-placed fallback), OQ10 (staging order) and the decisions of sections 4-6. No code. G-n = gate (stop unless true); R-n = rollback point. Updated from the adjudicated runbook for the later findings and for the second review.

Named roles, placeholders the owner fills before Phase 4: **decider** `<name: says go or no-go, and abort>`, **deploy operator** `<name: runs the skill>`, **platform operator** `<name: backup, restore, firewall>`, **dump owner** `<name: takes the pilot dump for the rehearsal>`, **watcher** `<name: reads the Admin Cockpit logs and planner reports during the first shift>`, **capturer** `<name: takes the pre-roll numbers>`.

0. **Pre-conditions (no writes).**
   - G-1: profile Q0 reviewed (required columns, the three constraints and their validation flags, which objects exist, the database session time zone, ledger tails, plant switches).
   - G-2: profile Q1, Q2, Q5, Q7 (with class `09b`), Q8 (joined to the sent table), Q9, the runnable Q10, **Q13 (machines and plants with no calendar row), Q15 (plants with no time zone; OQ52 gates the cutover on this count being zero), Q16 (overlong orders per line; OQ50), Q17 (orders carrying the mismatch flag; OQ53) and Q14 (rows saved before the 2026-07-07 save fix)** reviewed by the owner (write-set size, never-placed, flagged, split, hybrid, zero run time, inverted rows, parent-versus-envelope mismatches, family shapes); owner chose the never-placed fallback (8.3), the flagged-row rule and the distribution-aggregate rule (leave spread or re-align), **and the derived-start rule for lines with no calendar row (a non-zero Q13 count is a stop until it is decided; OQ62)**.
   - G-3: SAP staging state per plant known (**profile Q11a to Q11e: remembered sends, outbound queue, batches, apply modes**); if a Send has happened, the as-sent due-date column is already overwritten for those orders (R5).
   - G-4: owner chose re-purpose or new column; **if a new column: whether the cutover keeps an eager backfill of the identity population or lets NULL fall back (OQ32(b) and OQ5 differ on this, 8.4)**; whether stored-end history is snapshotted; **whether the cutover image bumps `SCHEMA_VERSION` (8.6a) and what is done about Time Machine snapshots (8.7a)**.
   - G-5: platform backup / point-in-time-restore window confirmed by the platform operator.
   - G-8: per-plant counts of never-placed rows by snappable class (whole-second versus fractional run time; shorter or longer than the longest window).
   - G-9 to G-12 are defined in steps 0b, 0a, 1 and 5.

0a. **Pilot-copy rehearsal (G-10), merged with SAP staging Track 6.** The only track that tests our data rather than fixtures is `docs/SAP_STAGING_VALIDATION_PLAN.md` section 6, "restore a recent `pg_dump` of `pgdb-nimbus-dev/nimbus` into local Postgres" (`:199`), and its exit criterion 4 reads "Not met: Track 6 not run" (`:380-383`). Do it once for both purposes. No repository document gives a dump procedure (8.8 lists the only backup mentions): the dump owner takes the dump and records how. The dump holds real order data and user rows; handle it under the owner's data rule (not decided here).
   - **Part 1 (Phase 0).** Restore; run profile Q0 to Q17 on the copy; run the Track 6 first-apply rehearsal (its 6.2: reset count, vanish count, timings) and its 6.3. `now()`-based queries (Q4, Q12) describe the moment of the dump.
   - **Part 2 (just before Phase 4, from a fresh dump).** Apply the snapshot, column and identity files to the copy in the final order and name; compare `/tasks` for the identity population before and after (the step 5 check, run against the copy by a local server); run each file twice to prove the ledger guard; time them; record the count that G-6 will compare.
   - **The runner and the copy.** The runner's connection defaults are the live pilot host and user (`apply-migrations.ps1:56-59`) and the connection string requires SSL (`:68`). Pass `-PgHost`, `-Port`, `-Database` and `-User` explicitly, and record how a local server without SSL was handled **[unverified: whether the local server accepts `sslmode=require`; the alternative is `psql --single-transaction -f` per file plus the ledger insert the runner appends, `:137`]**.
   - **Pass bar (G-10):** the first-apply reset count is known and accepted by the owner; the second apply is a no-op; the G-6 count equals profile Q7 class 10 on the copy; every difference in the `/tasks` comparison is explained; the timings fit the quiet window.

0b. **Build the image and pass CI before the migration (G-9).** The skill's text runs the migration first, then the CI gate, then the build, then the roll (`SKILL.md:37-76`), and runs build and roll straight through (`SKILL.md:19`). For the cutover, run it in this order instead: preflight and rollback tag (`SKILL.md:27-35`), the CI gate for the exact commit being built (`:48-65`), the image build under a fresh tag (`:67-72`; `az acr build` builds and does not roll), and only then step 3 and step 4 below. Reason: with the old order, old code serves planners on migrated data for the whole build (minutes), rows saved by old code in that gap are outside the one-shot write, and the new revision briefly overlaps the old **[unverified: Container Apps revision overlap is platform behaviour, not in the repository]**. G-9: image `nimbus:vN` exists (`az acr task list-runs` shows Succeeded), CI is green for its commit (or an `-OverrideCi` reason is written into the deploy note), local `npm test` and `npm run check:static-assets` pass, the tree is clean or the build is of a pushed commit (`:49`), and the previous tag is recorded as the rollback target (`:32`). The operator holds the roll until step 5 of this runbook is reached.

1. **Quiet window, notice, flows stopped (G-11).**
   - Pick the window from profile Q12 (plant time). No query can see an open browser tab.
   - **Planner notice**, sent ahead and again at the start: the date and time; save and close every tab before the window; do not restore a Time Machine snapshot dated before the cutover (8.7a); after the roll, hard reload (Ctrl+F5), and if the page looks unchanged clear this site's data for the address (this removes the offline cache and local snapshots; save first, because unsaved local edits are lost); what will look different although no bar moved (the new late warning fires at once for every late order, and the tiles and utilization figures use the new rules, 4.10); whom to tell about a moved bar and how; and that the old behaviour cannot be restored once planners have saved, so "report, do not retry" (8.8).
   - **Staging poll off.** Confirm `NIMBUS_SAP_STAGING_POLL_SECONDS` is 0, the default (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:52`; `brain.py:430`), or set it to 0 before the window; changing an environment variable creates a new revision **[unverified: platform behaviour]**, so do it before the window starts, not inside it. Set every object to manual apply (`sap_sync_config.apply_mode`, default `manual`, `schema.sql:1554`; Q11e shows it). A poll with an object on automatic apply applies a validated batch by itself (`backend/integration/sap_staging.py:829-832`) and rewrites order rows inside the window.
   - **Excel uploads frozen.** Tell every uploader. No code switch was found in the files read **[unverified]**. An upload rewrites rows and run times, and the staging section already says no Excel uploads on a plant that receives SAP snapshots (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:85`).
   - **Retire the outbound `ready` queue.** Profile Q11d lists it by status. A `ready` row holds a finish computed under the rule that was live when it was queued, and Mulesoft reads such rows at its own cadence (`docs/NIMBUS_INTERFACE_ARCHITECTURE.md:619`), so any left would reach SAP after the roll. The only code that retires them is a new Send click, which also queues new rows. To retire without queuing, the database administrator, with the owner's explicit go, runs the statement the application itself runs (`sap_staging.py:2245-2246`): `UPDATE sap_stage_planned_order_out SET row_status = 'error', error_text = 'requeued', sent_at = now() WHERE plant = '<plant>' AND row_status = 'ready'`. It is an operator-run write outside the runner and outside this document's SELECT-only profiling. Rows Mulesoft has already read (`sent`, `error`) cannot be recalled (8.8). **G-11:** poll confirmed 0, objects manual, uploads frozen, `ready` count zero for every plant.
   - **Pre-roll capture of the consumer numbers (capturer).** The cutover image ships the new alert, tile and utilization rules in the same release (4.10), so these figures change although no bar moves, and no server-side history exists to compare against (`schema.sql` has no KPI or history table; the only persisted series is each browser's Time Machine). For every plant, from the old image, record: alert counts by type and in total; the dashboard tile values (including Late and Capacity Headroom 7D); the utilization matrix by line and day for the next 14 days; the Orders grid Late filter count. By screenshot or export, filed with the identity sheet.

2. **Snapshot (R-1).** A restorable copy of the order and segment tables with the timestamp recorded; a snapshot of id, stored start and end, flag, status, due-date column, as-sent baseline and `order_sap_sent` in a separate migration file containing none of the runner's listed words (comments included; 8.5), named so that it sorts first (step 3b); capture `/tasks` per plant (id, shown start and end) as the identity baseline (the server value; the snap for never-placed rows is not in it). Snapshot the as-sent baseline columns before the first Send.

3. **Data migration through the runner, as its own run.**
   - **3a. The pending set.** The dry run lists every file in `migrations/` (36 today, 30 matching the destructive text test) and never reads the ledger (`apply-migrations.ps1:83-90`), so it cannot show what is pending. Read the ledger (`SELECT filename, applied_at FROM migration_files_applied ORDER BY filename;`, read-only) and subtract it from the dry-run list. The pending list must be exactly the cutover files: any other pending file is applied in the same run (additive) or released by the flag (destructive).
   - **3b. The files, in this order.** (i) The snapshot file (step 2). (ii) If OQ32 chooses a new column, the column file: an ALTER, destructive by text and additive in effect, its own file ahead of the identity file (7.8 item 9). (iii) The identity file: ledger-guarded, one UPDATE with exclusions E1 to E9, finish truncated to seconds, `IS DISTINCT FROM`, `updated_at`. If the column is new and OQ32(b)'s "a NULL falls back" is chosen with no backfill, there is no mass write: (iii) and G-6 disappear and the snapshot and column files remain; if the new column is backfilled for the identity population (OQ5), the UPDATE targets the new column. The three names must sort in that order under any sort (8.5): for example `<date>-1-order-snapshot.sql`, `<date>-2-placed-finish-column.sql`, `<date>-3-identity.sql`, with a date later than every existing file; confirm with `-DryRun`, which prints apply order. A new column or ledger id must also be mirrored in `schema.sql`, or the CI smoke fails (10.6).
   - **3c. Review and release.** `-AllowDestructive` is one switch for the whole run (8.5): read every pending file in full, comments included (the filter counts the word "update" in a comment, and passes a file that has none of the listed words). The skill gates the real apply on the operator's explicit go (`SKILL.md:20`). A blocked file does not stop the run: it moves on, applies later additive files and exits 3 (`apply-migrations.ps1:131-134`, `:151`); treat exit 3 as stop.
   - **3d. Apply.** G-6: the row count equals profile Q7 class 10 for the same window (E1 to E9 in the predicate). R-2: one transaction per file; if the migration succeeds and the roll fails, old code displays the same ends (residual readers in 8.4 only).

4. **Roll the image (already built under G-9; O3: forward paths replaced in one image).** Read rule, save path, ingest, resolver, distribution, optimizer and client changes together; refuse the baseline route and retire the snap and baseline phase for orders with a placed finish in the same image (R12); add an online-path cache discard if cached pre-cutover edits must not replay; the `SCHEMA_VERSION` decision of G-4 (8.6a). `az containerapp update` with the built tag (`SKILL.md:74-77`); poll health on the skill's 15-second cadence with cache-busted requests (`:80-99`). **A corporate proxy may re-serve a stale `index.html` after the roll** (8.7): verify with a cache-busted request for the page and compare the `NIMBUS_BUILD_ID` it carries with the built tag **[unverified: whether the proxy caches the page]**.

5. **Verify (cache-busted requests), with planners still out.** `/tasks` per plant against the step 2 capture; gate: zero differences for the identity population; every difference explained by an owner-chosen exception. Then compare alerts, tiles and utilization with the pre-roll capture of step 1: every difference must be explained by a named rule change (4.10). **G-7:** the finish a Send would transmit equals the finish last sent for unchanged orders (profile Q11b). Before the first Send `order_sap_sent` is empty and Q11b returns no rows, so G-7 passes vacuously and says nothing; profile Q11c (the read-only Send preview) is the only check on what a first Send would do, and there is no other preview because the Send function writes (`sap_staging.py:2218-2262`).
   **G-12, the go/no-go.** True only when G-1 to G-11 are true, step 5 has passed, and the decider has said go in writing. Only then tell planners they may resume. The first planner save under the new rule ends the clean rollback (8.8), so the all-clear is never announced before G-12.

6. **Post-roll watch (first shift), with abort criteria.** The watcher reads backend errors in the browser as an administrator (Admin Cockpit, Logs); the log route returns 401 to an anonymous request and to a bare session cookie, and that is not a failed deploy (owner edit committed as `0317dd8` to `.claude/skills/promote-azure/SKILL.md` and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`). The numbers below are for the owner to set before Phase 4; the starting values are suggestions, not decisions.

   | Signal | Source | Abort (roll back the image) if | Suggested starting value (owner sets) |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | Identity population differs from the capture | Step 5 | Any difference no rule explains | 0 unexplained |
   | Stale and conflict notices | `schedule.conflicts`, planner reports | More than N in the first hour | N = `<owner>` |
   | Planner reports of a moved bar | Reports to the watcher | Any report no rule explains, or more than N | N = `<owner>` |
   | Server errors on `/tasks` or on a save | Admin Cockpit, Logs | Any sustained error | Any error lasting more than `<owner>` minutes |
   | `ready` outbound rows appear | Profile Q11d | Any (nobody should press Send) | 0 |

   The abort decision belongs to the decider, who must know what an abort costs: it is image-only before the first planner save, and after the first save the placed finishes cannot be recovered (8.8); a late abort is a fix-forward decision, not a rollback.

7. **SAP staging first apply per plant (OQ10; its own window).** Snapshot the as-sent baselines first; record the slot-reset count against the identity sheet and against the rehearsal's count (G-10); the poll is switched on, or an apply is pressed, only inside this window.

8. **Rollback matrix (R-3).** Per 8.8, with three additions. (i) Retire any `ready` outbound rows queued under the new rule, as in step 1. (ii) Send the planner notice again: hard reload and clear site data, and do not restore snapshots dated after the cutover. (iii) Record the rollback timestamp; if new code later returns, 8.8a applies.
