### OQ48 Reading B: decide or defer, and in what form

- **Options.** (a) Defer B entirely. Example (5.2, case 1): the forward plan keeps its 128.5 hours of earliness and each order finishes well before its due date, as it does today. (b) The right-shift post-pass as an "align to due dates" option on existing modes. Example (5.2, case 1): forward earliness 128.5 hours becomes 22.5 hours (a saving of 106 hours) with the same late count and setup. (c) A fourth optimizer mode with a full backward search. Example: it also changes the alternate-plan table, which runs each mode. (d) Fold just-in-time into Min Changeover. Example: two same-family orders due four days apart, which Min Changeover now runs back to back, would be pulled apart toward their due dates; this contradicts the settled promise that due date is not an objective there.
- **Evidence.** The post-pass traces identical to full B in case 1 and gives nothing when every order is already late (case 2); full B is about 2,100 to 3,000 lines and 3 to 5 weeks with line parallelism needed at scale (5.3, 5.6, inference, low confidence **[unverified: effort inferred, no prototype]**); the post-pass hooks in after gap fill (`engine.mts:884-889`); B depends on Phase 2's server contract (5.8).
- **Fed by.** 5.
- **Recommendation.** Defer full B. Build the post-pass (b), after Phase 4, only if OQ60 confirms that finished-goods inventory is a goal; otherwise defer B entirely (a). (c) only if the owner also wants sequence freedom for earliness.

### OQ49 Reading B: due instant, and a missing or beyond-horizon due date

- **Options.** (a) Due instant per OQ23; a missing due stays at its forward position; clamp only a far due date to the horizon end. Example: the push cap uses due midnight plus N plus 1 days, so a due date at 00:00 reads as the previous evening. (b) Place a missing-due order at the horizon end. Example: it lands far from any due date. (c) Leave it queued.
- **Evidence.** The beyond-horizon ceiling reintroduces uncapped day walks (ruling XC-R1); default horizon is 35 days from the planning start (5.6, 5.10).
- **Fed by.** 5.5, 5.6, 5.10.
- **Recommendation.** (a). Reason: it reuses the one due-instant rule of OQ23, so Reading B never needs a second reading of a date-only due date; an order with no due date has nothing to align to, so leaving it at its forward position changes nothing for it; and clamping only a far due date to the horizon end keeps every day walk inside the index span (ruling XC-R1), where placing a missing-due order at the horizon end (b) would put it far from any due date and leaving it queued (c) would remove it from the plan B is meant to align.
- **Depends on.** OQ23, OQ48.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Accepted with the block of smaller questions (recommendation taken as written).

### OQ50 Overlong orders under the never policy: what does the backward walk do?

- **Question.** When an order's run time is longer than the longest working window of its line and the plant policy is `never`, what does the walk from the held finish produce? The shared Order Z example of section 4 silently assumes a split.
- **Options.** (a) A continuous elapsed bar anchored on the held finish, the mirror of today's continuous bar. Example: Order Z (run time 20 h, machine open 06:00 to 22:00 Monday to Friday, longest window 16 h, finish held Wed 21 Oct 2026 18:00): start = Tue 20 Oct 22:00, one bar Tue 22:00 to Wed 18:00, which spends its first 8 hours in the closed night. A later forward re-derivation from that start (any path not yet converted) snaps the start to the next window open, Wed 06:00, and ends Thu 02:00, eight hours after the held finish. (b) Walk back through working time only, as if the order could be split for this purpose. Example: Wed 06:00 to 18:00 (12 h) plus Tue 14:00 to 22:00 (8 h), start Tue 14:00 with two pieces, although the plant policy promises none. A later forward `never` re-derivation from Tue 14:00 gives one continuous bar Tue 14:00 to Wed 10:00, eight hours before the held finish. (c) Refuse: the order goes to Needs Planning with a reason such as "longer than any working window" and no bar, until an admin changes the plant policy to a splitting policy. Example: Order Z shows no bar and no finish; the same order today shows Mon 19 Oct 06:00 to Tue 20 Oct 02:00. (d) Keep overlong orders start-anchored, an explicit exception to the headline rule. Example: Order Z stays Mon 19 Oct 06:00 to Tue 20 Oct 02:00 and its finish follows run time, so the finish SAP is told is not the placed finish for this class (a cost under O4, which names the placed finish as the anchor).
- **Evidence.** The schema default is `never`: `schema.sql:293` `ALTER TABLE plants ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS split_order_policy TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'never';`. The forward helper refuses an overlong order: `calendar-engine.mts:277` `if (longestWindowMs <= 0 || durationMs > longestWindowMs) {` ... `return null`. The allocator does not refuse it: `calendar-engine.mts:432` `findContiguousSlot` returns `{ kind: 'overlong', start: operatingStart }`, and `calendar-engine.mts:541-545` reads `if (!('start' in slot)) return { kind: slot.kind };` then `end: new Date(slot.start.getTime() + durationMs)`, so an overlong result (which carries a `start`) becomes a continuous elapsed bar from the next operating instant, not a refusal. The run time is bounded at `schema.sql:117-121` (`run_time < 168`). Sample data: Section 1.2 records a median Machine Hours of 281.7 h, 461 of 593 rows at or over 168 h (so at least those exceed any single window), and 585 of 593 rows whose SAP span is shorter than their Machine Hours (a related but different test). The sample is a production-order extract and the Machine Hours rule applies to the routing-off Excel path only, so the share for the pilot's planned-order feed is unknown **[unverified: pilot planned-order run times not profiled; needs a profiling query counting orders longer than their line's longest window]**.
- **Fed by.** 4.2.3, 4.2.4, 4.4, 4.11 (the "continuous elapsed bar" exception), 8.11.
- **Recommendation.** (a). It keeps today's contract for overlong orders (one continuous bar, no splitting, no queueing of most of the sample) and changes only which end is held, so the finish the planner or SAP holds does not move; every path that re-derives an overlong order must then walk backward, and the document's worked examples must each name the policy they assume. Run the overlong count per line (profile Q16 in 8.12) before the owner accepts (a) or (c).
- **Depends on.** OQ13, OQ15, OQ28, OQ47.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** DIFFERS from the recommendation. Option (c): an order longer than the longest working window on a "never split" plant is refused to Needs Planning. When a planner releases it, it is drawn as one continuous bar ending at its held finish and marked as an approved exception (the marker is shared with OQ63; 1.6, consequence 4).

### OQ51 Who re-derives a stored start, and how is staleness detected?

- **Question.** Once a start is stored, four things can make it wrong without a run-time change: a calendar edit, a derive-and-save done before the calendar loaded or after the fetch failed, a second browser tab, and any other writer. Who re-derives, when, and what tells the system that a stored start is stale?
- **Options.** (a) The browser re-derives only rows flagged stale (OQ34), and only after this plant's calendar has loaded from the server in this session; calendar edits stay alert-only; the first save wins. Example: a blackout Thu 22 Oct 06:00 to 18:00 is added on Mon 19 Oct 14:00 to a line open 06:00 to 18:00 holding order Y (8 h, stored Thu 10:00 to 18:00). Nothing re-derives; Y sits on the blackout and the `blackout` alert fires. At Y's next trigger the walk from the held Thu 18:00 finds no free time on Thursday and moves the finish to Wed 21 Oct 18:00 (OQ13). If the tab's calendar fetch timed out (8 s), derive-and-save is paused for that plant and a flagged order keeps its stored bar. (b) Stamp a calendar revision. The server keeps a per-plant revision that every calendar write increments; hydration returns it; a save that carries a re-derived start also carries the revision it used and is refused when that is not the current one. Example: hours edited at revision 7 to 8 on Mon 09:02; the tab loaded at 09:00 derives against 7 and its save is refused, while a tab loaded at 09:05 saves. A tab that fell back to default hours carries no revision and is refused too. (c) A planner-confirmed re-fit after a calendar edit. Example: after the blackout is saved the calendar screen lists "1 order on this line now sits in a blackout: Y, Thu 10:00 to 18:00 would become Wed 10:00 to 18:00", with a Re-fit button that re-derives the listed orders as one save and one undo entry. (d) The server re-derives, from a Python port of the walk, inside the calendar write. Example: the same blackout rewrites Y to Wed 10:00 to 18:00 in the request that saves the blackout; every open tab sees it at the next refresh.
- **Evidence.** The code states the policy: `frontend/optimization/engine.mts:2772-2776` "Reconciliation is intentionally *not* subscribed to ordinary calendar edits or policy changes: those must alert existing schedules rather than silently rewrite them." It runs on a hydrated calendar (`engine.mts:2777-2779`) and again on any refresh of tasks (`engine.mts:2780-2790`, the `tasks:bulkUpdate` source `refresh` branch calls `Engine.reconcileRuntimeSchedules(plant)` whatever the calendar state). The fetch: `calendar-sync.mts:96-97` `{ signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000) })`; on failure only `ErrorLog.warn` and `Toast.show(Util.t('toast.calendar_offline_cache'), 'info')` (`:102-104`); `calendar-sync.mts:231-233` "The initial ingest snap (Persistence._snapToWorkingHours at load) ran against default/stale hours". Default hours: `foundation.mts:133-134` `DEFAULT_SHIFT: [7, 19]`, `WEEKEND_OFF: true`. The load snap never touches placed orders: `persistence.mts:948` `if (t.firmed || (t.scheduleSegments?.length ?? 0) >= 2 || t.runtime_schedule_mismatch) continue;` and `:953` `if (t.user_scheduled) continue;`. The server cannot check a continuous order's width: `db.py:1551` `if new_start is not None and new_end is not None and new_end <= new_start:` is the only span check (a missing edge is borrowed at `db.py:1494-1495`). The calendar payload has no revision: `master_data.py:2839-2846` returns only `plant`, `subnetwork`, `plant_work_hours`, `line_work_hours`, `machine_blackouts`, `plant_blackouts`; the calendar write routes never touch orders (`backend/calendars/routes.py:32-47`). Cost at scale is not sized: a calendar edit on a 70-machine plant touches every placed order on those lines **[unverified: no count of placed orders per line]**.
- **Fed by.** 4.1.2, 4.2.2, 4.3, 4.4, OQ34.
- **Recommendation.** (a) now, with the pause on a failed or pending calendar made visible (the existing offline toast plus a banner that says schedule changes are paused for the plant); keep (c)'s notice half through the existing `blackout` alert; take (b) as a follow-up if the pilot shows calendar edits while planners have tabs open. Reason: calendar edits are rare admin acts and already alert, the hydration pause removes the one silent wrong-input path, and (b) and (d) each add a mechanism with no owner yet. The residual risk of (a) is a tab holding an older calendar that saves first, which nothing detects; say so in the release notice.
- **Depends on.** OQ34, OQ36, OQ46, OQ52.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Accepted as recommended.

### OQ52 One "now": which clock and zone decide reversal, running and frozen?

- **Question.** Reversal (O2), the running test and the frozen test all read "now". Today six code paths read it from three different clocks. Which one clock and zone should every path use, and what happens for a plant that has no time zone?
- **Options.** Clock: (a) The server's instant, projected into the plant's zone, delivered with each task load and used by every path (client, optimizer, Apply filter, server). Example: plant zone `America/New_York` (UTC minus 4 on Tue 20 Oct 2026), server instant 14:00 UTC, so the plant clock reads Tue 10:00 on every screen; an order stored Tue 08:00 to 16:00 is running for everybody. (b) The viewer's own instant projected into the plant's zone. Example: the same instant on a laptop whose clock is 6 minutes slow reads 09:54 plant time, so an order starting at 10:00 shows "not started" on that laptop for those minutes. (c) Keep today's mix. Example: a planner whose browser is in `America/Los_Angeles` reads the same instant as Tue 07:00, compares it with the plant's naive 08:00 start, and sees the order as not running, so Optimize may move it; the New York planner sees it running. No time zone: (d) Block the backward rule for that plant: no reversal, no derive-and-save, an admin alert "set the plant time zone", and zero such plants as a Phase 0 precondition. Example: a plant with an empty zone keeps its stored bars unchanged and shows the alert. (e) Fall back to UTC (the server's rule today). Example: a plant in `America/Chicago` (UTC minus 5) at Tue 20:00 local is Wed 01:00 UTC, so an order starting Tue 22:00 is already running to the server and not yet running in a Chicago browser. (f) Fall back to the viewer's clock (the client's rule today). Example: two planners in different zones see different running sets for the same plant.
- **Evidence.** `frontend/optimization/engine.mts:1018` `return task.start_date >= now && task.start_date < end;` and `:1026` `return task.start_date <= now && now < task.end_date;`, both with `now: Date = new Date()` (the viewer's instant compared with naive plant wall-clock values; the convention is stated at `engine.mts:1288-1290`). Server: `db.py:3203` `local = now_utc.astimezone(ZoneInfo(tz_name)) if tz_name else now_utc` with the docstring "an unknown/missing timezone falls back to UTC". `foundation.mts:749` `plantNowParts(tz?: string | null): { hour: number; minute: number; hhmm: string; zoned: boolean }` returns hour and minute only and falls back to the viewer's clock. Optimizer: `engine.mts:2028-2032` `const liveClock = (): Date => { const now = new Date(); ... return plantWallClockFromInstant(plantTimezone, now) ?? now; }`; with no zone `plantWallClockFromInstant` returns `new Date(instant)` (`engine.mts:579-580`). Apply: `optimize-ui.mts:2115-2118` `const applyNow = new Date();` then `Engine.isInProgress(live, applyNow)`. Remove Backlog throws without a valid zone: `engine.mts:1309` `Remove Backlog requires a valid IANA timezone for the selected plant`. The zone column is nullable: `schema.sql:289` `ALTER TABLE plants ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS timezone TEXT;`. The count of plants with no zone is unknown **[unverified: profile Q15 in 8.12 counts them; not run]**. The SAP to Mulesoft to staging to plant to browser zone chain is tabulated in the new section 4.13 (4.13.4).
- **Fed by.** 4.2.4, 4.2.5, 4.11, OQ18, OQ46, 8.9.
- **Recommendation.** (a) with (d). One clock removes a class of "running for one planner and not for another" defects that every path in this document depends on, and delivering the server instant costs one field on the task load (a skew-free clock). A silent fallback (e) or (f) changes which orders are running or frozen by where the planner sits, which a held finish must not depend on. Gate the cutover on the count of plants without a zone being zero (profile Q15 in 8.12, a G-2 item).
- **Depends on.** OQ6, OQ18, OQ19, OQ46.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Accepted as recommended.

### OQ53 Reversal order on one line, and how an on-time reversal is reported

- **Question.** (1) When several orders on one line reverse in one pass (at cutover, after a bulk re-upload, after a routing change), in what order do they land? (2) When a reversal moves the finish later but still before the due date, how does the planner learn that the held finish was overridden?
- **Options.** Ordering: (a) Independent, as built; overlaps stay alert-only. Example: line open 06:00 to 22:00, now Fri 16 Oct 2026 08:00, orders X, Y, Z of 6 h each whose derived starts are all before now: all three land on Fri 08:00 to 14:00 and three overlap alerts fire. (b) A per-line sequence among the reversing orders, in the order of their held finishes (ties by order id), each placed from the previous one's finish. Example: held finishes Thu 12:00, Thu 16:00, Thu 20:00 (derived starts Thu 06:00, 10:00, 14:00) give X Fri 08:00 to 14:00, Y Fri 14:00 to 20:00, Z Mon 19 Oct 06:00 to 12:00 (a 6 h `never` order does not fit the 2 h left on Friday). Only X, placed at now, meets the running test (start at or before now) at the moment of placement; Y and Z start after now and are not running until their start time passes (1.1, exception 10). A collision with a non-reversing peer is left to the overlap alert. (c) No bulk reversal: orders whose derived start would fall before now keep their stored bar and are marked "reversal pending" until a planner acts or runs Remove Backlog. Example: X, Y, Z keep their stored bars, three pending notices appear, and one Remove Backlog run compresses them in start order. This defers O2's reversal for those orders until a planner acts: a cost under O2, not a change to it. Reporting: (d) None when still on time. Example (4.2.4): a 6 h order with held finish Mon 19 Oct 12:00 on a 08:00 to 20:00 calendar, now Fri 16 Oct 19:00, due Fri 23 Oct 18:00: it reverses to finish Mon 13:00; no late warning fires (finish before due), and the next Send tells SAP Mon 13:00 instead of Mon 12:00. (e) A notice on every system move of a finish, whatever the lateness. Example: the inspector says "Finish moved Mon 12:00 to Mon 13:00 (reversal from now)" and one toast counts the batch. (f) List "finish changed since last Send" in the Send dialog. Example: the dialog shows "1 finish differs from the last Send: Mon 12:00, now Mon 13:00".
- **Evidence.** The reconcile loop places each order from its own stored start and sees no peers: `engine.mts:1258-1261` `for (const task of Store.tasksByPlant(plant)) {` ... `const changes = Engine.schedulePatchFor(task, line, task.start_date, policy);`. It pushes nothing for undo: `engine.mts:1274` `if (patches.length) Store.updateMany(patches, 'engine-runtime-reconcile');`. Remove Backlog has the sequencing cursor: `engine.mts:1377` `let cursor = new Date(now);`. Overlaps are advisory: `db.py:1229-1230` "advisory by default (commit and report)". The late rule reads the end against the clock: `frontend/nimbus-compute-core.js:414-416` `const todayStart = startOfDay(new Date());` ... `let activeTasks = tasks.filter(t => !t.end_date || t.end_date >= todayStart);`. How many orders reverse at cutover depends on how many carry the stale flag **[unverified: profile Q17 in 8.12 counts them; not run]**.
- **Fed by.** 4.2.4, 4.4, 4.8.7, 4.10.6, 4.11, 8.2.
- **Recommendation.** (b) for ordering and (e) for reporting. The sequencing cursor already exists in Remove Backlog and avoids stacking identical bars; the notice is how a planner finds out that SAP is about to be told a later finish, and it works without the clock. Offer (f) later if admins ask for it.
- **Depends on.** OQ3, OQ5, OQ6, OQ13, OQ18, OQ19, OQ56.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Accepted as recommended: orders that reverse together on one line are queued by held finish, and every system move of a finish gets a notice.

### OQ54 Data-driven frozen entry and the add-only SAP firm flag

- **Question.** The outbound message sends the SAP firm flag for any order whose start lies inside the frozen window, and NIMBUS never clears it. Under the new rule a run-time growth, a share change or a reversal can pull a start into the window with no planner action and no time passing. Should that set the flag, for a single order and for a distribution aggregate where one child qualifies?
- **Options.** (a) Keep the rule as built (staging decision D10). Example (single): now Wed 21 Oct 2026 08:00, frozen window ending Fri 23 Oct 00:00, unfirmed order P on a 24-hour line with held finish Sun 25 Oct 18:00; run time grows from 8 h to 80 h, the derived start moves from Sun 10:00 to Thu 22 Oct 10:00, and the next Send carries the firm flag; shrinking back to 8 h does not take it back. Example (aggregate): shared finish Fri 23 Oct 16:00 on a 24-hour line, a 14 h child starts Fri 02:00 and a 6 h child Fri 10:00; the frozen window ends Fri 06:00, one child qualifies, so the whole aggregate is sent firm. (b) Send the flag only for a planner firm or an existing SAP firm (this revisits D10, which is not one of O1 to O4). Example: P above is sent unfirmed; SAP's weekly regeneration may renumber it. (c) Judge the frozen term on the SAP start as received (one value per aggregate, it does not move with run time). Example: P's SAP start Mon 26 Oct is outside the window, so no flag; but a planner who pulls an order with SAP start Mon 26 Oct to Thu 22 Oct 10:00, which receives the firm flag today, would no longer receive it. (d) Keep the rule and put a human check in front of the irreversible step: Send lists the orders firmed only because of the frozen window, with the child that qualified for aggregates, and the admin confirms. Example: the dialog reads "12 orders sent firm: 9 firmed by a planner or SAP, 3 only because growth moved their start into the frozen window (P, ...)".
- **Evidence.** `backend/integration/sap_staging.py:2148-2158` `def firm_flag(manual_firmed, firming_indicator, eff_start, frozen_end) -> str:` ... `if frozen_end is not None and eff_start is not None and eff_start < frozen_end: return "X"` (one-sided: every past start qualifies; add-only by construction, the docstring says "an existing SAP 'X' always yields 'X'"). The aggregate roll-up: `sap_staging.py:2190-2191` `if firm_flag(r.get("manual_firmed"), r.get("firming_indicator"), r.get("eff_start"), frozen_end) == "X": g["firm"] = True` (any candidate child). Send already returns a firmed count: the `queue_send_to_sap` docstring ends "Returns {send_batch_id, queued, skipped_no_end, firmed, rolled_up_groups}", but not why. Document 4.11 ("The add-only outbound firm hazard"). The repository's design of record: `aggregate_to_detail.md:414` "SAP's own firming indicator still matters on the SAP side: it is what stops MRP renumbering a planned order" and `:475` "Unfirmed planned orders are deleted and recreated with new numbers by every MRP run". Decision D10: `docs/SAP_STAGING_DESIGN.md:37` "Firm Indicator = 'X' if planner-firmed **or** inside the frozen horizon **or** SAP already had it firmed. Add-only." What SAP does with a firm flag set this way is unknown **[unverified: needs SAP Development]**.
- **Fed by.** 4.5, 4.7.5, 4.11, OQ4, OQ27.
- **Recommendation.** (d), decided before the first live Send. It keeps D10 and the add-only property, and adds a human check before an act that NIMBUS cannot undo and whose SAP-side effect on the weekly regeneration is unknown; revisit (b) or (c) once SAP Development answers. The same reasoning is stated in OQ27 (the bullet that explains why frozen may follow the derived start when visibility may not): visibility and vanish decide which orders exist in NIMBUS and must not change with run-time data, frozen protects the schedule that is physically near, and the outbound firm flag is an irreversible SAP-side act, so OQ54 puts a check in front of it.
- **Depends on.** OQ4, OQ10, OQ11, OQ27.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** DIFFERS from the recommendation. Option (a): keep today's firm rule as built (planner-firmed, SAP-firmed, or starting inside the frozen horizon), with no confirm step. An order can therefore be firmed in SAP just by growing into the frozen window.

### OQ55 A held finish that lands inside a window's first minimum-piece minutes

- **Question.** Under a splitting policy, no piece may be shorter than the plant's minimum productive piece (default 30 minutes). A held finish that falls in the first minutes of a window leaves a fragment shorter than that. This is a second infeasibility trigger, separate from OQ13 (no slot at all). What does the walk do?
- **Options.** (a) Take the latest legal finish earlier, with an alert. Example (4.11): windows 06:00 to 16:00, minimum piece 30 minutes, order 620 minutes, held finish Tue 06:20: the Tuesday fragment is 20 minutes, so it is skipped and the finish falls back to Mon 16:00, 14 h 20 min before the held finish. (b) Allow a below-minimum piece at the held end. Example: Tue 06:00 to 06:20 as a 20-minute piece; the server rejects it today (`any piece below the floor on a multi-piece order`), so the validator needs a carve-out for the piece that ends at the held finish. (c) Move the finish later to the first minute that supports a minimum piece. Example: Tue 06:30, ten minutes after the held finish, toward lateness and later than what SAP holds.
- **Evidence.** The allocator's floor rule: `calendar-engine.mts:565-567` `if (remaining > take && remaining - take < minSegmentMinutes) { take = remaining - minSegmentMinutes; }` and `:571-573` (a piece below the floor is skipped). The server enforces the same floor: `db.py:400` `if len(clean) >= 2 and any(item["minutes"] < min_segment_minutes for item in clean):` (default `db.py:265` `MIN_SEGMENT_MINUTES = 30`, per plant overridable). The document's own trace: 4.11 ("finish silently pulled back to Mon 16:00 ... unless the walk refuses or snaps back". Under `never` the same finish is OQ13's case (no contiguous slot ends there).
- **Also decided here (the other degenerate finishes, R2-12).** The same rule should say what happens for: a finish that a system source puts inside a blackout (for example a date-only SAP midnight on a closed day), which takes the latest legal finish earlier as in (a); a run time of zero or empty, which places nothing and reports it instead of storing a bar (`engine.mts:1171-1172` `if (!Number.isFinite(runtimeMinutes) || runtimeMinutes <= 0) return null;`, while `schema.sql:94-97` `CHECK (... scheduled_end > scheduled_start)` forbids a stored zero-width bar); and a multi-day shutdown, where under `never` the finish may move earlier by the length of the shutdown (a 10-day blackout moves a Fri 23 Oct 18:00 finish to before the blackout, about 10 days earlier), which should be reported as one alert naming the distance **[inference, not traced]**.
- **Fed by.** 4.2.3, 4.11 (backward segment allocation), 4.9.
- **Recommendation.** (a) for system re-derivations, and a snap back to the previous legal finish for manual drops, both with an alert: the same split as OQ13's recommendation. (c) moves the finish toward lateness and (b) needs a server validator change for a floor that exists to prevent slivers. Apply the "also decided here" rules in the same pass.
- **Depends on.** OQ13, OQ15, OQ50.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Accepted with the block of smaller questions (recommendation taken as written).

### OQ56 Remove Backlog: window, sort, break rule and dialog default

- **Question.** Remove Backlog selects, sorts and stops on the start. With a derived start, a run-time growth can make an order with a future finish look like backlog, and a running order is still re-placed with its full run time. Should the four edges (the `[From, To)` window, the compression sort, the break rule and the dialog's default From) stay on the start, move to the finish, or exclude running orders?
- **Options.** Example setup for all: 24-hour line, now Fri 16 Oct 2026 08:00. T lies wholly in the past (Thu 15 Oct 08:00 to 14:00, 6 h). S is running (Thu 15 Oct 20:00 to Fri 16 Oct 20:00, 24 h). W has a held finish Mon 19 Oct 12:00 and a run time that grew from 6 h to 80 h, so its derived start is Fri 16 Oct 04:00. (a) Keep the start key, read on the derived start. Selected: T, S, W; sorted T, S, W; the cursor gives T Fri 08:00 to 14:00, S Fri 14:00 to Sat 17 Oct 14:00 (its 12 h already done is counted again, finish 18 h later than Fri 20:00), W Sat 14:00 to Tue 20 Oct 22:00 (34 h after the held finish). (b) Key window, sort and break rule on the finish. Selected: T only (S and W finish after now); S and W are untouched by Remove Backlog and W is handled by its own reversal (OQ53); T's new bar Fri 08:00 to 14:00 overlaps running S and raises an overlap alert. (c) Keep the start key but exclude running orders (the OQ3 recommendation applied here). Selected: T and W; T Fri 08:00 to 14:00, W Fri 14:00 to Mon 19 Oct 22:00 (10 h after the held finish); S stays running, and T's bar overlaps it with an overlap alert.
- **Evidence.** `engine.mts:1361` `if (snapshotStart < from || snapshotStart >= to) continue;`; `engine.mts:1373` `items.sort((a, b) => a.snapshotStart.getTime() - b.snapshotStart.getTime() || a.task.id.localeCompare(b.task.id));`; `engine.mts:1380` `if (item.snapshotStart >= now && cursor <= item.snapshotStart) break;`. The dialog default: `optimize-ui.mts:353-355` `const pastStarts = tasks.map(t => t.start_date).filter((d): d is Date => !!d && d < now);` ... `const computedStart = pastStarts.length ? new Date(Math.min(...pastStarts.map(d => d.getTime()))) : now;`, with the default To the lesser of the latest end and `now` plus four calendar months (`optimize-ui.mts:356-358`). The pinned running behaviour: `tests/modules/remove-backlog.test.mjs:290` "Engine.removeBacklog may still move a running (in-progress) order -- the one exemption from the running lock". The planner decision of 2026-08-22 ("insert-operation semantics require the overdue backlog to compress fully into now, including into the frozen window") is recorded in the comment above `removeBacklog` (`engine.mts:1318-1320`).
- **Fed by.** 4.8.7, 4.11 (GAP06), OQ3, OQ19.
- **Recommendation.** (a) for the first release: it keeps the contract planners were given on 2026-08-22 and the pinned test, and changes only which start is read. Show in the existing preview how many selected orders became backlog because their run time grew. Take (c) only if the owner accepts OQ3(iii) and also accepts removing Remove Backlog's exemption for running orders (which OQ3's recommendation keeps), because the owner then wants a running order's finished work no longer counted twice; otherwise take (a).
- **Depends on.** OQ3, OQ19, OQ53.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Accepted with the block of smaller questions (recommendation taken as written).

### OQ57 Explaining a system-driven move, and undo for system moves

- **Question.** After a re-upload, a routing change or a machine move, a bar can grow to the left with no planner gesture. The only signals today are the overlap and late alerts, which say that something is wrong and not why. What explains the move, and can the planner undo it?
- **Options.** (a) An explain-the-move line plus one toast per batch, no undo. Example: a re-upload on Wed 21 Oct 2026 09:00 raises order Q from 8 h to 12 h with its finish held Thu 22 Oct 18:00; Q's left edge moves from Thu 10:00 to Thu 06:00 and now overlaps order P (ends Thu 09:00). The inspector shows "Start moved Thu 10:00 to Thu 06:00: run time 8 h to 12 h (SAP upload)" and one toast says "3 bars changed by the system: show". The reason lives for the session only unless a column is added. (b) One undo entry per system batch. Example: after the same upload, Undo restores Q to Thu 10:00 to 18:00 against a 12 h run time, so the stale flag fires again and the order is re-derived; one of the ten undo slots is used. (c) Alerts only, as today. Example: the planner sees "overlap: P and Q" and has to infer the cause. (d) A "changes by the system" panel listing every moved order with before and after, kept for the session. Example: the panel shows Q Thu 10:00 to 06:00 and two other orders moved by the same upload; no restore button.
- **Evidence.** The reconcile pushes no undo entry: `engine.mts:1274` `if (patches.length) Store.updateMany(patches, 'engine-runtime-reconcile');` (the only `UndoStack.push` in the engine is the optimizer Apply at `engine.mts:2219`). The undo stack is short: `frontend/platform/CLAUDE.md` "`UndoStack` — `MAX: 10`". The late and overlap alerts carry no cause. The persisted whole-plan rollback is the Time Machine, up to `frontend/nimbus-intelligence.js:1333` `const TM_MAX_SNAPSHOTS = 200;` (restoring one after cutover can bring back a forward-rule pair, document R4-5).
- **Fed by.** 4.3, 4.4, 4.10.6, OQ13, OQ45.
- **Recommendation.** (a), with (d) as the same data shown as a list if planners ask. Undo of a system move would reinstall a bar that disagrees with the run time SAP or routing just supplied, so the explanation is more useful than a rollback; the existing Time Machine is the whole-plan escape.
- **Depends on.** OQ6, OQ34, OQ53.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Accepted with the block of smaller questions (recommendation taken as written).

### OQ58 Distribution children with a date-only shared finish: who writes it, and what is sent?

- **Question.** Children get no stored dates at ingest, and the server has no calendar. Under a shared finish, who writes the finish and the starts, at ingest and at the first re-weight? Both sample workbooks carry only date-only finishes, so the 60/40 example of 4.7.3 (a timed finish) does not match the data.
- **Options.** Inputs for all: aggregate quantity 1000, SAP start Mon 19 Oct 2026 and SAP finish Fri 23 Oct 2026 (date only), shares 60/40, C1 6 h, C2 8 h, line open 06:00 to 22:00 Monday to Friday, policy `never`. (a) Nothing is written at ingest or at a first re-weight; the browser reads the shared finish from the due date as the end of that date's working window (OQ23) and writes only when a planner or the optimizer places the family. Example: C1 Fri 16:00 to 22:00 and C2 Fri 14:00 to 22:00 are displayed; at 50/50 they display as C1 Fri 17:00 to 22:00 and C2 Fri 12:00 to 22:00; Send carries nothing for unplaced children (OQ33(B)), so SAP keeps its own Fri 23 Oct. (b) The server writes the literal date-only finish (Fri 23 Oct 00:00) with no start. Example: both children hold a finish and no start, the hybrid row five server predicates misclassify; the browser walks back from midnight and draws C1 Thu 16:00 to 22:00 and C2 Thu 14:00 to 22:00, a day early, while Send reports Fri 00:00. (c) The server writes finish and start at ingest from a Python port of the walk. Example: C1 Fri 16:00 to 22:00, C2 Fri 14:00 to 22:00 stored for both, both children become planner-placed at ingest, and Send reports Fri 22:00 against SAP's date-only Fri 23 Oct, which SAP may or may not read as a change **[unverified: needs SAP Development]**. (d) Keep date-only families start-aligned until placed (today). Example: C1 Mon 19 Oct 06:00 to 12:00 and C2 06:00 to 14:00; if Send carries unplaced rows it reports Mon 14:00, 82 hours before SAP's own Fri 23 Oct (00:00). This keeps a forward path for these families: a cost under O3, not a change to it.
- **Evidence.** Ingest writes no dates: `backend/distribution/data.py:784-786` `"basic_start_date": parent_facts.get("basic_start_date"),` `"basic_finish_date": parent_facts.get("basic_finish_date"),` `"run_time": float(child_run_time) if child_run_time is not None else None,` (the children copy the parent's SAP dates and take their share of run time). A child with no stored date reads as unplaced: `db.py:553` `COALESCE(seg.first_start, scheduled_start, basic_start_date)` and `db.py:559` `(seg.segment_count >= 2 OR scheduled_start IS NOT NULL OR scheduled_end IS NOT NULL) AS "USER_SCHEDULED"`. A first re-weight writes dates only for a brand-new child, forward: `data.py:2802-2826` (`_compute_reweight_anchor`: the earliest sibling's start, else the SAP start) and `data.py:1457` `end = start + timedelta(hours=float(run_time)) if run_time and _dec(run_time) > 0 else None`, so that child becomes planner-placed at once. A date-only value is midnight and is not zone-converted: `backend/integration/sap_staging.py:184-227` (`_parse_sap_time` returns `None` for a missing or `000000` time; `sap_to_plant_local` `if t is None: return naive`). Send carries the latest child end: `sap_staging.py:2188-2189` `if g["end"] is None or r["eff_end"] > g["end"]:`. Sections 1.2 and 8.11: both sample workbooks are 100 percent date-only; the 4.7.3 example uses `Fri 2026-10-23 16:00`.
- **Fed by.** 4.7.1, 4.7.3, 4.7.4, 4.7.5, 8.11, OQ11, OQ23, OQ33.
- **Recommendation.** (a). The server cannot write a correct start, a stored finish without a start is the hybrid row, and a date-only finish has no time to hold; reading the date through OQ23 gives every viewer the same family. For a new child of a placed family, copy the siblings' stored finish and set the stale flag so the browser derives its start **[inference, not traced]**. OQ11(a)'s wording has been conformed: "a default read at display time, written on first placement".
- **Depends on.** OQ11, OQ23, OQ29, OQ33, OQ34, OQ35, OQ51.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Accepted with the block of smaller questions (recommendation taken as written).

### OQ59 External writers of order dates under the new rule

- **Question.** `POST /tasks/bulk_update` (and `POST /task/update`) accept `start_date` and `end_date` from any authenticated caller. Their own docstring says the bulk route is "used by external tooling/Postman". Under the new rule the finish is the anchor and the start is derived. What do these writes mean afterwards, and does anything outside the browser call them?
- **Options.** Example for all: a script sends `{id, start_date: "2026-10-19T08:00", end_date: "2026-10-19T16:00"}` for an 8 h order on a line open 06:00 to 22:00. (a) Leave as is and document. Example: the pair is stored and reads the same (finish Mon 16:00, start derived Mon 08:00); but a script that sends start Fri 23 Oct 20:00 and end Sat 24 Oct 04:00 (start plus 8 hours, across the closed night) stores a finish on a closed day and a start that no walk would produce, and nothing flags it. (b) Accept both edges, read `end_date` as the placed finish, and set the stale flag so the browser re-derives the start. Example: the Friday script's finish clamps to Fri 22:00 and the start becomes Fri 14:00 at the next load, silently from the script's point of view unless the response says so. (c) Accept the finish only; a supplied start is ignored and reported. Example: the first script's start is dropped and the response lists `start_ignored` for the id. (d) Retire external date writes (admin-only job). Example: the script receives an error and the team moves its change into a planner action.
- **Evidence.** `backend/scheduling/routes.py:531-536` `@router.post("/tasks/bulk_update", response_model=BulkUpdateResult, dependencies=[Depends(auth.require_authenticated)])` ... `"""Alias for /tasks/update with a flat list payload (used by external tooling/Postman).` (any authenticated caller in plant scope; `force` is ignored for this route, N2). The payload model accepts start, end, run time, machine and segments: `backend/scheduling/models.py:236-261` (`TaskDateUpdate`). A missing edge is borrowed from the current derived edge: `db.py:1494-1495` `new_start = start if start is not None else cur_start` / `new_end   = end   if end   is not None else cur_end`; the only span check is `db.py:1551` `new_end <= new_start`. No caller inventory exists in the repository **[unverified: ask the platform owner or read access logs for the routes before the cutover]**.
- **Fed by.** 4.1.2, 4.3, 4.4, OQ34.
- **Recommendation.** (b), plus a caller list requested before the cutover. It breaks no unknown caller, gives the finish its new meaning, and lets the browser reconcile fix the start. The cost is that a script's start is replaced at the next load; document it and return a `start_derived` note in the response.
- **Depends on.** OQ32, OQ34, OQ43.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Accepted as recommended.

### OQ60 Reading B: does the inventory benefit fit the product goal?

- **Question.** Section 5 sells Reading B on "less finished-goods inventory carried between finish and due date". `PRODUCT.md` names on-time delivery as the north star and does not name inventory. Should B's inventory argument count as a reason to build any part of B? (O1 keeps B separately decidable; this asks only about its justification.)
- **Options.** (a) Count it: name finished-goods earliness as a secondary goal in `PRODUCT.md` and build B on that basis. Example (5.2 case 1): total earliness falls from 128.5 h to 22.5 h with the same late count and setup. (b) Do not count it: judge B only on on-time delivery, where it adds nothing and adds fragility. Example (5.2 case 1): lateness is 0 either way, and order C placed to finish exactly at its due date Thu 22 Oct 18:00 turns late if anything before it grows by 30 minutes. (c) Count it only with a slack buffer so on-time delivery stays the first number. Example (5.2, two-hour buffer, illustrative): C finishes Thu 22 Oct 16:00 (2 h early), B Wed 21 Oct 18:00 (18 h early), A Wed 13:30 (4.5 h early): 24.5 h earliness against 128.5 h forward, with 2 h of protection on C.
- **Evidence.** `PRODUCT.md:17` "Success is on-time delivery: orders complete by their due dates, with line utilization and changeover efficiency as a secondary, supporting concern rather than the primary goal." and `PRODUCT.md:33` "**Due dates are the north star.**"; the word "inventory" does not occur in `PRODUCT.md`. Section 5.1: "What B buys: less finished-goods inventory ... it cannot reduce lateness, and it leaves zero slack". OQ48 defers full B and builds the right-shift post-pass only if this question confirms that inventory is a goal.
- **Fed by.** 5.1, 5.2, OQ9, OQ48.
- **Recommendation.** (b) unless the owner confirms that finished-goods inventory is a planning goal; if confirmed, (c), because a zero-slack plan is the opposite of the document's own north star. It decides OQ48's recommendation: the post-pass is built only if the answer is that inventory is a goal; if it is not, B is deferred entirely.
- **Depends on.** OQ9, OQ48, OQ49.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Accepted with the block of smaller questions (recommendation taken as written). Reading B is deferred.

### OQ61 Should Send transmit unfirmed planned orders, given SAP's weekly planning run replaces them?

- **Question.** Send queues every order in the plant that has an effective end and is not in Needs Planning, firmed or not, and sends the SAP firm flag only when the planner firmed the order, SAP already had it firmed, or its start lies inside the frozen window (staging decisions D9 and D10). At the pilot SAP's planning run deletes and recreates unfirmed planned orders every week (4.13.1) **[unverified: the weekly renumbering is the owner's relayed record, not confirmed by SAP Development]**, so a finish sent for an unfirmed order is replaced at the next run and the placement that produced it is archived. Should Send still transmit unfirmed orders and, if so, how does the planner learn which finishes will hold?
- **Options.** (a) Keep today's rule: send every placed order. Example (order number illustrative): unfirmed order U is placed to finish Thu 22 Oct 2026 12:00 and sent on Mon 19 Oct; SAP's planning run of Wed 21 Oct replaces it with a new order carrying SAP's own dates, so Thu 12:00 disappears from SAP and the placement from NIMBUS. (b) Send only firmed orders, orders SAP already had firmed and orders inside the frozen window. Example: U sends nothing; SAP keeps its own dates for U until the run, NIMBUS never tells SAP a finish that SAP will discard, and there is no echo of an unfirmed order to misread. (c) Keep sending every order but split the Send summary into the orders that will hold and the orders that will be replaced. Example: the summary reads "212 sent: 41 firmed (will hold), 171 unfirmed (replaced at the next planning run)", and the planner can firm some of the 171 first.
- **Evidence.** `docs/SAP_STAGING_DESIGN.md` D9 ("every order in the plant that has an effective end and is not in Needs Planning") and D10 (the firm rule, add-only); `aggregate_to_detail.md:475` ("Unfirmed planned orders are deleted and recreated with new numbers by every MRP run") and `:665` (weekly at the pilot); `backend/integration/sap_staging.py:2148-2158` (`firm_flag`) and `2206-2215` (the candidate query). What SAP does with a finish-only change on an unfirmed order, and whether a firm flag set through the import holds an order the way a firm set in SAP does, is **[unverified: needs SAP Development]** (4.13.8, assumption A9, facts 3 and 4).
- **Fed by.** 4.13.1, 4.13.2, 4.13.8, 4.11 (the add-only firm flag), OQ11, OQ35, OQ54.
- **Recommendation.** (c) for the first release: it keeps today's Send behaviour and makes the promise honest for the planner. Revisit after the SAP test in 4.13.8 shows what SAP does with a finish-only change on an unfirmed order; if SAP says it cannot take one, move to (b).
- **Depends on.** OQ10, OQ11, OQ35, OQ54.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** DIFFERS from the recommendation. Option (b): Send transmits only firmed orders (planner-firmed, frozen-horizon-firmed or SAP-firmed). Unfirmed orders are never sent. See 1.6, consequence 5.

### OQ62 What is the derived start for a plant or line with no calendar row?

- **Question.** The browser derives every start by walking a calendar. When a plant or line has no stored calendar row, the engine walks its built-in default instead: Monday to Friday, 07:00 to 19:00, weekends closed. Nothing records which calendar a stored start used, and the profile queries did not count such lines until Q13 (8.12). Under O3 every plant switches at once, so a real 24-hour line with no row would receive 12-hour weekday starts and no weekend starts. What should the rule be for these lines? Raised by the second review, from the gap that 7.8 item 19, 8.12 (Q13) and 8.13 (G-2) leave open; none of those sections chooses an option.
- **Options.** Example for all: line L24 of a plant that runs seven days has no calendar row; order W (run time 8 h) has its finish held at Sat 24 Oct 2026 12:00. (a) Block placement with an alert. Example: W keeps its stored bar, no derived start is written, and the line shows "no calendar for line L24"; the count of such lines comes from Q13 before the cutover. (b) Derive on the engine default and flag the row. Example: Saturday is closed by default, so the held finish clamps to Fri 23 Oct 19:00 and the start derives to Fri 11:00, 17 hours before the finish SAP was told; the row is flagged "derived on default hours" and Send carries Fri 19:00. (c) Require a calendar row before a line is placed under the new rule. Example: L24 is excluded from the global cutover write (O3 stays global for every other line) and keeps its stored bar until it has a seven-day calendar row, then it is placed; no order of L24 is derived on the default.
- **Evidence.** The default is `DEFAULT_SHIFT: [7, 19]` and `WEEKEND_OFF: true` (`frontend/platform/foundation.mts:133-134`); a line or plant with no row is given it by `ensureCalendar` and `ensurePlant` (`frontend/platform/store.mts:457-465`, `494-503`); hydration leaves a slice the backend lacks as it is locally (`frontend/calendar/calendar-sync.mts:165-198`). The count of plants and lines with no calendar row has not been run **[unverified: profile Q13 of 8.12 is not executed]**.
- **Fed by.** 4.2, 7.8 item 19, 8.12 (Q13), 8.13 (G-2), R50 in section 9.
- **Recommendation.** (a), after the Q13 count: it never invents a start on hours nobody confirmed and it makes the missing row visible. This is a proposal from the second review, not a conclusion of the investigation. If Q13 returns zero the question does not arise; if it returns many lines, (c) is the cleaner cutover and (a) the interim.
- **Depends on.** OQ13, OQ46, OQ51, OQ52.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Accepted as recommended.

### OQ63 Firmed orders placed outside working hours on purpose (raised and decided 2026-10-14)

- **Question.** OQ1 and OQ15 clamp a manual drop into working hours. A planner may need a one-off exception, for example overtime on a firmed order. Who may place a bar outside working hours, and what keeps later recalculations from snapping it back?
- **Options.** (a) Firmed orders only, after a confirm; the bar stays as placed and raises an alert, and a per-order marker tells recalculations and the optimizer to leave it alone. Example: a firmed 10-hour order on a line open 06:00 to 18:00 is dropped at Mon 09:00 to 19:00, the planner confirms "outside working hours", and it stays Mon 09:00 to 19:00. (b) Any order, with the same confirm. Example: the same drop on an unfirmed order; SAP's weekly planning run replaces unfirmed orders, so the placement would be lost. (c) Not in this release. Example: the drop clamps to Mon 08:00 to 18:00.
- **Evidence.** The document does not cover this. Today manual placement is calendar-blind (`engine.mts:1225-1228`), so a planner can already place a bar over closed hours with only an alert; clamping (OQ15) would remove that. A re-derivation walks the calendar, so without a marker a re-derive would move the bar. The marker is shared with the release of an overlong order (OQ50).
- **Fed by.** OQ1, OQ15, OQ50.
- **Owner decision (2026-10-14).** Option (a): firmed orders only, with a confirm; the bar stays as placed. Needs a per-order marker (1.6, consequence 4); how it is stored and which sites must respect it are implementation questions.

## Appendix A: Things learned along the way (merged, deduplicated)

### A.1 Environment

- **HEAD moves.** Investigation start `0dda55d`; four owner commits followed in this order: `99e9ef6`, `fcf041b`, `757dd86`, and the docs-only `0317dd8` (14:36; `.claude/skills/promote-azure/SKILL.md` and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` only, details below). Owner commit `99e9ef6` (12:17, tests expanded; the formerly untracked test files became tracked), `fcf041b` (12:53, the Excel upload no longer fails on a date-type mismatch; touched `db.py` near `ingest_orders_from_excel`, the upload route, four locale files, `styles.css`, two tests; `db.py` anchors after about line 3980 shifted by about +4), `757dd86` (14:18, Gantt zone-band ticker; only `gantt.mts`, one sentence of the scheduling `CLAUDE.md`, and its test: every `gantt.mts` anchor at or past about line 3232 shifted by about +40, and the lock-band ticker region was rewritten). Reports cite lines from `0dda55d` to `fcf041b`; the document cites `757dd86`. The database file was modified at 12:33 and 12:43 during one lane's survey. No fleet agent wrote to the repo.
- **Owner edits during the investigation.** `.claude/skills/promote-azure/SKILL.md` and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` now say backend errors are read in the browser as an administrator (Admin Cockpit, Logs, Ctrl+Alt+L) because `GET /logs/backend` is access-gated and returns 401 to an anonymous request, and DEPLOYMENT.md says "confirmed 2026-10-13 on the v113 roll" (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:197`). The fleet read these as uncommitted edits; they are committed as `0317dd8` (docs only, 14:36). `.dockerignore` still carries an uncommitted edit. Reports that tell the operator to read `/logs/backend` with a plain request (the adjudicated runbook, GAP07) are superseded on that point.
- **Python is not runnable** on the investigation machine (the interpreter name resolves to the Store alias, exit 49); no Python test or import ran, and no pass/fail state of any test is known. The Node standard library was used for scans. A Bash loop of 128 files x 34 identifiers exceeded its time limit and was replaced. One lane's Bash tool failed with a fork error; its checks used the search and read tools only. Another lane's background whole-repo search timed out unused.
- **OneDrive.** The repository sits inside an OneDrive-synced folder; a "file lock" was listed among the environment problems during the run. **[unverified: no workstream report records the detail.]**
- **Local environment facts:** compiled `.mjs` twins are gitignored; `.dockerignore` excludes lowercase `*.xlsx` (so the COOIS extract is not in the image; the uppercase `Sequence_Testing.XLSX` may be); the COOIS `Raw` sheet has invalid date serials and an empty start column; the sample extract is dated 2026-08-17.
- **Which reports exist.** Adjudications and blind passes exist only for WS01, WS06, WS15; verifiers only for WS02a-d and WS16a-c; a cross-check only for WS09-10. WS03, WS04, WS05, WS07, WS08, WS11-WS14 have no independent verification.
- **Second review, 2026-10-13: the FSD changed while the fleet ran.** The owner re-saved `Nimbus_ECC_Integration_FSD.docx` at 17:02 on 2026-10-13. The first scratch extract (11:34) is stale, and the file was locked during one verification, so that verifier could not read the new text; a second extract was taken after the re-save. The new text adds that the planned-order export is gated relative to the planned-order finish (plant planning horizon plus one day). The sentence is unfinished in the draft and describes a program not yet built, so it is recorded as a lead and not as an answer (scratch extract `fsd2.txt:168`; Appendix E.5; Follow-up 13). If it holds, it answers Appendix D's "which date the planned-order export selects on" and bears on the start-keyed vanish test (`backend/integration/sap_staging.py:709-710`).
- **Second review: stray files and what ran.** Two reviewers wrote one scratch file each outside the scratch folder, into the user temp folder (`k_en.txt`, English locale key names; `matrix.txt`, a coverage extract). Neither was in the repository, and both were deleted in the housekeeping step. No reviewer or verifier ran application code, tests, a script that imports the app, or any database command. HEAD was `0317dd8` (docs-only) at the end; the second review's anchors are at `757dd86`.
- **Second review: dormant dependency overlay.** The Gantt dependency overlay reads a toggle element `#chk-show-deps` (`frontend/scheduling/gantt.mts:2429`) that exists in no HTML file in the repository, so the overlay cannot be switched on; a reviewer's finding about red gap arrows from a finish-held plan was therefore reduced to a recorded dormant surface (Appendix E.3 row 9).
- **Second review: what the reviewers could not verify.** SAP semantics, Mulesoft behaviour, live data and row counts, the server clock configuration, vis-timeline behaviour, benchmark timings, and the FSD sentence above; listed against Appendix D's categories in Appendix E.5.

### A.6 Additional items from the section drafts

Items found in the four section drafts that the merged list above does not already carry.

- **The mismatch flag has three writers, one computed arm and one clearer**, not "cutover only"; the browser always sends the segments key, so every browser save clears the flag with no width check (`backend/routing/resolver.py:674-679`, `718`; `db.py:2842-2852`, `1585`, `1128-1129`; `backend/distribution/data.py:1380-1386`; ruling ADJ-WS01 R3).
- **A start-only save that also carries a segments key writes the borrowed (derived) end** into the stored end (`db.py:1572-1573`); neither first report saw it. It is reachable only by non-browser callers.
- **`db.py` anchors after about line 3982 moved by +2 to +15 in `fcf041b`** (required-columns set `4118`, hygiene bad mask `3982`, midnight mask `4006`, Machine Hours override `4141-4152`). Any new derived-start column built with date arithmetic inside the hygiene frame needs the same data-type cast as that commit (`db.py:3988`, `4012`) or it re-opens the 500 on that pandas version.
- **`Calendar.workWindow` duplicates the compute core's** despite the root CLAUDE.md claim; default shift hours (7 to 19, weekends off) are stored independently in four places; the optimizer carries a third copy of the window intersection logic (4.2.1, 4.2.2).
- **`/tasks/baseline-correct` requires only authentication** and writes orders at first page load (up to 500 rows per request, bumping versions); `/tasks/refresh` does not carry the due date; `_resolve_machines` in distribution never reaches the child upsert while `_resolve_wc_codes` does (VERIFY-WS02c-6; 4.6.2).
- **Arithmetic correction in the run-time lane (WS05).** The 24-hour-calendar numbers were wrong: Monday 18:00 minus 14 h is Monday 04:00 (not Sunday 20:00), and Monday 08:00 plus 14 h is Monday 22:00 (not Tuesday 06:00). The conclusions are unaffected (4.4, SIM-A).
- **The migration log's edge-resize note (F12) is right about the effect and wrong about the mechanism:** the resized width is never sent, so there is no stored finish to revert (4.3, 11.8).
- **Test anchors moved in `757dd86`.** `gantt.test.mjs` gained about 12 lines; earlier lane citations of tests 959, 1029, 1113, 1209, 1284 and 1408 are now 971, 1041, 1125, 1221, 1296 and 1420. Tests before about line 960 (the setup-bar tests at 395 to 570) did not move.
- **`757dd86` changed the ticker, not alert freshness.** Zone bands are pushed only when "now" moved at least 0.5 px at the current zoom or an edge input changed (`gantt.mts:359-404`, helper `1748-1752`); the 30-second lock-band scan moved from 394-405 to 413-424 and still only restyles bars (4.11).
- **The locale ratchet has zero headroom** (VERIFY-WS02d): the missing count equals the 231 baseline in each of the four other locales, so any new English key must land in all four in the same commit (`tests/modules/locale-completeness.test.mjs:506`).
- **Counts that are unions or readings.** The "18 hard-coded-English clusters" are 12 from the i18n inventory plus 6 from the UI lane; "Store commit sites missed by the first inventory" were read as the two Store sinks (`updateTask`, `updateMany`) plus the four Gantt lines that call them (4.12, 4.3).
- **Three definitions of "enough changeover time" coexist** (wall-clock gap, contiguous in-window time, span coverage), no test asserts that the overlap finding fires, and no test exercises a start at a window open (4.9).
- **Dead or misleading code:** an unused shares summary field; the "firmed boundary elapsed" explanation is reused for a future protected order that merely overlaps another; a no-op resize leaves the Gantt's own item out of step with the Store until the next rebuild (4.3, 4.11).
- **Distribution details:** an unsegmented N-to-1 collapse survivor never gets a mismatch flag, so its bar widens silently server-side; the pane hydrates a new survivor as unfirmed although the server copied the firm (inference); a new child can be created "scheduled" while its siblings are unplaced (4.7.4, 4.7.8).
- **Held-order release door:** the Updated Start column is editable on every row, including held ones, so a planner can release any hold by keying a start; only run-time edits are restricted to the "run time unknown" hold (4.3).
- **Survey corrections:** the "main-thread utilization fallback" is dead code (`dayByLine`) and the real path is the same core function; `distribution-pane.mts:1417-1477` is not a drop path (it is the post-write reconcile banner) (4.10, 4.7).
- **Wire and mode facts:** `children_summary.earliest_start` is on the wire but no frontend code reads it, the aggregate route has no frontend consumer, and CSV dates use `str(datetime)` while JSON uses ISO "T" (4.7.9); the two optimizer mode whitelists disagree (the dialog accepts Remove Backlog, the settings modal does not) and the Due Date and Remove Backlog mode labels exist only in English; the distribution-separation alert is localised in the drawer row and English in five other renderers (4.10, 5.9).
- **Open and not decidable from code:** what SAP returns for blank or zero times, whether SAP shifts finishes to calendar boundaries, the real SAP zone, which date SAP's export and production-version selection use, whether real Excel exports carry finish times, and the content of stored `scheduled_end` on live data (Appendix D).

## Appendix B: Context

### B.1 The owner's request

The request, close to verbatim, in the owner's words:

> "Nimbus needs to be backward scheduling with routings/runtime changes etc. What all needs to change?"

Followed by the instruction to draw up a comprehensive change document, in the owner's words, that is "SUPER comprehensively vetted"; to use a fleet of Sonnet and Haiku agents; to answer as many of the prompted questions as the code can answer; and to drop the document in the main repository folder. The investigation brief states the purpose: before any code is written, list every impact and answer every question the code can answer; produce findings, not designs and not code.

### B.2 The four decisions

Settled by the owner on 2026-10-13 and treated as fixed throughout. The options column records the alternatives the brief defines or implies; the exact wording of the choices put to the owner is not preserved in the investigation brief **[unverified: the offered option list is reconstructed from the brief's definitions]**.

| # | Topic | Decision | Alternatives the brief defines or implies |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Scope | Investigate both readings. Reading A: finish-anchored orders everywhere (manual moves, run-time changes, ingest, distribution all hold the finish and derive the start). Reading B: a just-in-time optimizer that places orders as late as possible against due dates, presented as a separately decidable phase | Reading A only; Reading B only; both |
| O2 | A start in the past | When the backward walk from the finish lands before now, flip to forward from today (SAP's backward-with-reversal) and accept a late finish; lateness shows as an alert | Place the bar in the past; flip forward from now; refuse the placement |
| O3 | Rollout | Global cutover, all plants at once; forward code paths are replaced, not kept behind a per-plant switch | A per-plant switch (the existing `plants.routing_runtime_enabled` pattern, `schema.sql:327`); a global cutover |
| O4 | Anchor | The SAP finish as received is the due date and is never rewritten; the planner's placed finish (drag, optimizer) is the schedule anchor and is what goes back to SAP; the client-side rewrite of the SAP finish to "end of the working day of the start" is retired | Keep the client rewrite; let the placed finish overwrite the SAP finish; hold both separately |

### B.3 How the investigation was run

| Stage | What |
|---|---|
| Workstreams | 16 read-only workstreams (server read and save; inventories; calendar; manual placement; run-time propagation; ingest and SAP; anchor and baseline; distribution; optimizer under A; optimizer under B; setup; consumers; semantics; UI; cutover; tests and docs) |
| Haiku lanes | 7 Haiku inventory lanes (WS02a to d, WS16a to c), each verified by a Sonnet agent; only findings marked confirmed or corrected entered the document |
| Blind second passes | 3 (server SQL, ingest and SAP, cutover), each followed by an adjudication that overrides both inputs |
| Cross-check | 1 optimizer cross-check of the Reading A and Reading B workstreams |
| Coverage | A matrix of 97 production surfaces by workstream, with a ranked list of 22 gaps |
| Gap follow-ups | 14 follow-up investigations (GAP01 to GAP14) |
| Drafting and assembly | 4 section drafters and this assembly |
| Method rules | Doc claims were treated as leads and checked against live code; every finding carried an anchor; nothing was executed (no tests, builds, Python or database commands) |
| Moving tree | The owner committed during the run: `0dda55d`, then `99e9ef6`, `fcf041b` and `757dd86`; a docs-only `0317dd8` followed. The document cites `757dd86` (`db.py` at `fcf041b`). No fleet agent wrote to the repository |

### B.4 Key findings

1. The server computes the finish as start plus run time in plain elapsed hours and ignores a stored finish whenever a run time is set; it has no calendar, so the derived start must be stored and written by the browser (4.1).
2. The first echo of a Sent finish overwrites the due date in four places, Send transmits a computed elapsed end rather than a stored finish, and a finish at SAP-zone midnight resets on every echo (4.5).
3. A held finish cannot always be honoured under `never` and `overlong_only`, any forward re-derivation moves it, and running and frozen status flip by data unless the start is stored (4.2, 4.11).
4. Under Reading A the optimizer itself needs almost nothing; the danger is every path that re-derives the finish afterwards. Reading B is a separate, much larger piece of work, and a right-shift post-pass delivers most of its value cheaply (4.8, 5).
5. At cutover, identity by SQL is possible only for placed rows; never-placed rows need a read-time fallback; rollback is image-only until planners save; and only about 4 percent of tests pin the forward rule (8, 10).

### B.5 Rejected or deferred alternatives

| Alternative | Why it was rejected or deferred |
|---|---|
| A per-plant switch (O3) | The owner decided against it. The evidence agrees: it would keep two derivations of one finish alive, and the simulation of 4.8.6 shows two re-derivations already disagree (+2 h on the server, +18 h in the browser) |
| Keeping a forward path (for example leaving the manual drag, or the optimizer's old placement walk, start-anchored) | O3 replaces forward paths. The old optimizer walk is already unreachable for the four typed modes and is a start-anchored path nothing exercises (4.8.10). Three recommendations keep something start-anchored or forward on purpose and are listed as exceptions for the owner to accept, not as kept paths: running orders stay start-anchored (OQ3(iii)), never-placed rows keep a start-plus-run-time read (OQ33(B)), and the optimizer, the alert Fix and Remove Backlog place forward and store the result as the placed finish (1.1, exceptions 1 to 3). Rejecting those exceptions is what "replace every forward path" would mean in full |
| Retiring only the client rewrite of the due date | Insufficient: ingest also fabricates the due date (hygiene) and the first echo overwrites it in four places, and the distribution false reset survives (4.5.3, 4.6.1, 4.7.6) |
| A server-side calendar engine | None exists, and none of the server modules has a calendar-aware helper (4.1.5, GAP07-7). Split orders already use the stored, client-computed model, so the derived start is stored and client-written |
| Re-purposing `scheduled_end` without a backfill | Historical stored ends are an unmarked mixture of five provenance classes; every non-NULL stored end would become authority at deploy and bars would move (6.2, 8.1). Re-purposing with a backfill remains an option (OQ32) |
| Using `sap_basic_finish_date` as the due-date store | It follows every echo, is NULL when SAP sent no finish, and is not on the wire (6.3) |
| The derived start as the production-version validity anchor | Circular; rejected earlier by design decision D8 (4.5.12) |
| Treating Reading B as part of Reading A | B is a new algorithm sized separately (5.3), leaves zero slack, and depends on A's server contract (5.8); O1 makes it separately decidable |

## Appendix C: Contradictions and rulings

One line each: ruling, winner, anchor. Source: `CONTRADICTIONS.md` plus later cross-checks.

**ADJ-WS06 (ingest and SAP).**
1. Q06.4 start difference versus echo: same rule from opposite defaults, not a contradiction; start alone flags a change unless a slot echo or a minute-precision finish echo vetoes (`db.py:2639-2666`).
2. Baseline finish overwrite: **BLIND right**, overwritten; no column keeps the original SAP finish after the first echo (`db.py:2829, 2836`; header and children too).
3. Outbound: **BLIND right**; Send transmits a computed end, not a stored finish (`sap_staging.py:2211`).
4. Running-protection counter-examples: **both right**, two failure modes; the rule needs a stored calendar-aware start and a stored placed finish (`db.py:3216-3226`).
5. Midnight hole: **BLIND right**, systematic at exact SAP-zone midnight; the 19:30 case is safe; the hygiene rewrite after conversion is a separate defect (`sap_staging.py:192, 207, 221-223`; `db.py:2655-2659`).
6. Line numbers: use live numbers (required-column set `db.py:4118`).
7. Vanish predicate on start-less rows: agree; and WS06's 2.g/2.h lines confirmed.

**ADJ-WS01 (server SQL).**
8. ## Appendix D: Unverified items

**Needs SAP Development, Basis or the SAP integration owner:** what SAP returns for a finish with a blank, zero or 235959 time, and whether it ever returns 240000 (rejected as an invalid time, `sap_staging.py:198`); whether SAP moves an imported finish to a factory-calendar boundary on import (design assumption A9; if it does every Send resets every sent order); the actual value of the SAP system time zone setting (default UTC "until SAP Development confirms"); whether SAP rounds a finish by up to a minute (defeats the minute-precision echo); which date the planned-order export selects on (start or finish; assumptions A5/A11); whether the SAP planned-order finish equals the customer due date; which date SAP uses to select a production version; whether SAP reschedules the start when Machine Hours change; whether the real Excel export carries finish times; the weekly re-plan effect on unfirmed orders; the Excel Machine Hours unit.

**D.1 Added by the second review (2026-10-13): the SAP planning cycle.** Items 1 to 10 are for SAP Development unless another source is named. Items 1 to 3 are the A9 test (4.13.8). Item 8 is partly answered already.

1. **Float on an imported finish.** Is the finish NIMBUS sends read as the basic or the production finish, and does SAP add or remove float? (4.13.2.)
2. **SAP's own reversal and tolerance.** If SAP's lead time, counted back from the finish NIMBUS sent, puts its start in the past, does SAP schedule forward from today and return a later finish, from which "today", with what rounding or tolerance? (4.13.2.) Related, 6: which SAP engine's behaviour O2 matches.
3. **A finish-only change on a firmed planned order.** Is it accepted? Does SAP reschedule the order or leave the finish alone? (4.13.1.)
4. **Export and import cadence, and the acknowledgment path.** The Functional Specification says each program is "scheduled via a Process Chain" (6.6, 7.6) with no frequency, leaves the export's RFC style open ("Presently unsure if Async or Sync", 6.4) and calls the import's "timing/success of the ingestion" of high importance (7.3). How often does each chain run, and what comes back to NIMBUS per row beyond the log file (7.5)? Source for the second half: the integration owner (assumption A8). The cadence sets the width of the send-then-stale-snapshot window (4.13.8).
5. **Whether SAP discards the time of day.** Does a planned order keep the end time NIMBUS sends and return it in the next export? Decides whether OQ23 applies to every returned finish (4.5.5, case 3).
6. **ECC lead-time scheduling against APO "backward-with-reversal".** The only repository source for "backward-with-reversal" is an APO note (`docs/SAP_APO_Opportunities.md:48`); the pilot interface is ECC. Name the SAP behaviour O2 is meant to match and confirm it applies to ECC planned orders at the pilot plants.
7. **The finish-gate lead and its conflict with the start-keyed vanish test.** The Functional Specification (6.4) limits the export to the planning horizon plus one day "relative to the `PLAF-PEDTR` end-date" and the sentence is cut off in the file. If the limit is on the finish, an order that starts inside the horizon and finishes beyond it is absent from SAP's export and, under NIMBUS's start-keyed test (`sap_staging.py:709-710`), is archived on apply. Owner to say what the sentence was meant to say; SAP Development to say whether past finishes are excluded and which date the limit is on. Related to assumptions A5 and A11.
8. **How the weekly planning run treats a firm flag NIMBUS set, and an unfirmed finish-only change.** Partly answered: the owner's record says SAP's firm flag "is what stops MRP renumbering a planned order" (`aggregate_to_detail.md:414`, `:475`) and the pilot regenerates unfirmed planned orders weekly (`:665`). Not answered: whether a flag set through the import behaves the same, and whether a finish NIMBUS changed on an unfirmed order survives until the run or is replaced by it (4.13.1).
9. **Whether the SAP-side frozen horizon in the Functional Specification's plant table has a consumer.** NIMBUS ignores it and uses its own `frozen_horizon_days`; whether SAP's planning run treats it as a time fence is unknown (4.13.6).
10. **What the commitment date, sales order and committed quantity mean for a planned order,** and whether the planned-order finish is the customer date (4.6.3).

**Needs the owner to run SQL (profile Q0-Q17, the read-only profiles P1 to P5 of 4.13 and 4.6.3, and additions):** live class sizes (never-placed, placed, flagged, split, hybrid); the stored-end versus start + run time relation and the provenance classes; inverted rows; whether the live database carries the as-sent baseline columns and how many rows hold them; whether the range check and the run-time bound are validated; whether echoed finishes exist; whether a split order's stored end equals its segment envelope; the share of fractional-second run times and the longest working window per plant; family shapes for distribution (corrected Q10); Machine Hours versus run time on routing-off plants; the "1,842 agreed exactly" claim; index-use claims (no EXPLAIN was run).

**Needs platform or operator confirmation:** Azure automated backup and point-in-time restore (enabled, retention); whether `migrations/2026-10-06-sap-truth-firming.sql` and its writing image are applied on Azure, and what the 2026-10-13 v113 roll contains; whether the corporate proxy re-serves a stale `index.html`; the number of open browser sessions and their cached edits at cutover; the OneDrive file lock noted during the run.

**Needs a browser check (human, about five minutes):** vis-timeline 7.7.3 behaviour (which edge the snap applies to on a body drag versus a right-edge resize; whether resize handles show only on a selected item; whether the move event's time is the item start or the pointer time); whether the DB Load tile shows 0 and "ok"; the preview ghost delta basis.

**Needs code not run or tests not run (read-only fleet):** Python and test pass/fail state; baselines (1,625 / 1,244) not re-measured; about 600 of 651 test classifications from titles; which Python tests are DB-free (inferred); `store`, `sandbox`, `services` test bodies not read line by line; the live missing-key count versus the 231 ceiling; whether `finalizeCandidate` rewrites a held reason; whether zero-open-quantity orders keep a placeable run time; Remove Backlog caps in preview validation; DST round trip of a backward walk emitting plant-local times (inference); Reading A and B effort estimates (inference, low confidence); WS10's comparator order spot-checked at two lines and its percent-of-profile and 2.2-4.9 s timings quoted not rerun; the exact boundaries of the dead legacy optimizer walk; which calls elsewhere pass an untyped optimizer mode string; the setup-data re-derive test's place in the 651; the browser behaviour of the 1,842-order measurement; `Store.setFrozenHorizonEnd` emit behaviour; whether any test pins "alerts clear after midnight".

**Owner decisions the code cannot settle:** OQ1 to OQ62 (section 12).
